
# Code Sandbox

> **v1 status.** The `local` backend runs on the engine host, as a process
> tree or in a container. The engine-fronted OTLP receiver is wired.
> `providers.sandbox` is a **catalogue** of cells, required once a company has
> an agent seat and a `providers.llm` entry. Every seat's executor runs in one
> cell: the `run_in` of the `providers.llm` entry the launch picks, else
> `providers.sandbox.default_run_in`.

Every agent seat's **executor** is its harness's own agentic run (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build, Muse Code, Kimi Code, Hermes Agent or Pi) in a **box**: a container or a directory on the engine host, each with a shell, a filesystem and a git checkout ([ADR-0066](../../adr/0066-every-executor-is-its-coding-clis-own-run.md)). This page covers where that run happens and what becomes of it. The [turn engine](turn-engine.md) launches it with the turn's ask as brief and the seat's system prompt as standing instructions, and the turn **parks**. The run does all the seat's work with its own shell and editor, calls the seat's tools over the [tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box), and ends by calling `submit_work` there. Its collection, minutes or hours later and possibly on another node, re-enters the **same turn**, where the delivery check and the reviewer judge it; a reviewer's `self_iterate` launches it again. The engine's own tool loop runs only the surrounding phases, on the engine host: the reviewer, delegated workers, the onboarding pass and the side passes (see [Where the harness runs](llm-backends.md#where-the-harness-runs)).

This is how an agent answers a message, works a ticket, implements a feature, makes tests pass or reproduces a bug. **The run is fully permissioned in every cell**: Claude Code under `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; OpenCode with a `permissions` rule list allowing every action (`{"action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow"}`) and denying only `question`, since `ask_and_wait` asks the seat's people instead. A headless run has nobody to answer a prompt, so a gate left to ask would stall it or refuse the step. The **cell** decides what the run can reach: `container` keeps it off the engine host's files; `direct` runs it as the engine's own user (see [Where a run happens](#where-a-run-happens)).

**An entry that denies the web denies it to its executor too.** On an entry with `overrides: {web_tools: denied}` the run's harness gets none of its own web tools, as the entry's runs on the engine host get none ([The web can be turned off](llm-backends.md#the-harnesss-own-tools-denied)):

| Runner | How | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `--disallowedTools WebFetch WebSearch` | 2.1.330: both refused, in subagents too, with a repository's settings allowing them and an agent of its own listing them |
| Codex | `web_search="disabled"` on its app-server's command line, the top configuration layer | measured through the app-server on 0.171.0: the request offers no `web_search` tool, Codex's one web tool, where without the key it offers one; web search is hosted, so Codex runs nothing for it |
| OpenCode | the `opencode.tool.webfetch` and `opencode.tool.websearch` plugins removed, and both actions denied in the run's rules and its agent's | 2.3.2: neither registered for the run or a subagent, a repository's agent allowing them and its `plugins` naming them again included; Code Mode's `fetch` refused |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | `--excluded-tools` naming `web_fetch`, `web_search` and `semantic_code_search` (GitHub's code search, the one other tool that reached the network); `--deny-tool` would not do, since `--yolo` allows every URL | 1.0.114: none offered to the run, its built-in subagents or a repository's own agent listing them |
| Kimi Code | `FetchURL` and `WebSearch` left out of the run's agent profile, posted with the brief as the session's `disabled_tools`, and `KIMI_WEB_SEARCH_*` and `KIMI_WEB_FETCH_*` unset | 2.7.2: neither offered to the main agent, both refused to it and to a subagent its `Agent` tool started, with a search service configured; the profile alone left the subagent both |

Turning the web off turns off the harness's web tools, not the box's network: the run's shell, and any code it runs, still reach whatever the box can. The engine sets no egress rule of its own ([Security model](#security-model)), so a box reaches what its host's network and firewall allow, through `local.network` for a `container` box.

Code lives in `internal/sandbox/`: the provider, the manager, the harness runners under `executor/`, the waiters, the coordinator, the pending store, `launch.go` (plumbing between an executor's launch in `internal/engine/agentrun.go` and its detached run), `boxhost.go` (keeps a `direct` or `container` box with the node that launched it, [ADR-0065](../../adr/0065-a-local-box-is-driven-by-the-node-that-launched-it.md)) and `answerseal.go` (seals a person's answer onto the run's row).

---
## How a coding task runs

Every turn's executor is a run like this one. Its box is placed by the `run_in` of the `providers.llm` entry the launch picks, else `providers.sandbox.default_run_in`, and reads the seat's `role.sandbox` `setup`, `env` and `mcp` (see [Where a run happens](#where-a-run-happens)). Where the company hosts its own code, the run checks repositories on [Gitlet](gitlet.md) out into the box as it needs them, with a credential that ends with the run (see [Repositories on Gitlet](#repositories-on-gitlet)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant T as Turn (runner)
    participant E as Engine
    participant W as Waiter
    participant B as Box
    T->>T: open the Execute phase: the seat's surface and prompt, agent_phase_started
    T->>E: launch the executor, from the turn's pinned epoch
    E->>E: the turn's fence, the budget floor, the chain member and its cell
    E->>E: open the run's row as launching: the seat is held from here
    E->>E: open the bridge session under the job's id
    E->>B: continue the turn's box or provision one, apply setup, start the harness (detached)
    E->>E: publish executor_launched
    T->>E: the turn parks: its state is written, the row becomes running
    Note over E: the seat is busy: its inbox is held, so nothing is fetched
    B->>B: clone, code, test, push, open the PR or MR
    B->>E: the seat's tools over the bridge, ending with submit_work
    E->>W: the submission nudges an immediate poll
    loop every 15 s, the fallback
        W->>B: keepalive and completion check
    end
    W-->>E: the job finished: executor_finished
    E->>B: claim the row, collect the result, pause the box
    E->>E: charge the run's spend, publish its executor_collected record
    E->>T: resume the same turn with the run's calls and its submit_work
    T->>T: the engine's delivery check, then the reviewer
    alt the work is accepted
        T->>E: the turn settles
        E->>B: reclaim the box
    else self_iterate
        T->>E: launch again, continuing in the paused box
    end
```

The details, each load-bearing:

- **Launch → park.** Every launch takes the same steps, in order (`internal/engine/agentrun.go`): the turn's own fence, so a seat this node no longer holds, or one a person stopped, launches nothing; a sandbox runtime on the node, the turn's catalogue and a bridge its box can reach; the [budget floor](#budgets); and the member of the seat's executor chain the run goes to — the first whose harness has a runner and is not sitting out a spent plan ([The executor's run in a box](llm-backends.md#the-executors-run-in-a-box)) — with its cell. Every fact comes from the turn's pinned epoch, so a revision applied mid-turn is the next turn's. The coordinator then opens the run's row as `launching`, the job's bridge session is opened under the job's own id, the box is continued or provisioned and set up, and the harness starts as a background command. The row is a durable record in the [coordination store](coordination.md): the task the turn was working on, both conversation values — the conversation identity a later answer is matched on and the resume reports back to, and the inbox partition the triggering delivery arrived in — the trace context, the `providers.llm` entry the launch picked and its model, the node that launched it, whether the turn owes anybody an answer, and — where a colleague's [A2A ask](event-system.md#ephemeral-a2a-channels-internala2a) woke the turn — that ask's channel, question, chain and trace, which the frame that ends the turn replies to — or, for a run lost under its turn, the run's ending, which tells the asker so. The executor phase returns parked and the turn's segment ends. The seat is **busy from the write that opens the row** — before the box is provisioned, and so before the turn can end and the seat's consumer move on to its next message. The write is recorded before it is sent and its answer counts the run in once, so a recount between the two counts the run where it was: no row for a turn's launch, and the claim a resumed turn relaunches, which holds the seat already. The launch also publishes `executor_launched` to the seat's control topic, and processing it recounts the seat from the pending store's own list of the seat's active runs, which is what carries a busy seat across a restart or a handoff; but nothing waits for it. A node taking the seat over counts each run its recovery takes over the same way, recorded before any fence and answered once the recovery has done with it, starting the seat's counts afresh, so a recount off the control topic, which is attached before the recovery, never counts a run twice beside it. A launch that fails once its row is written (its log not opened, no box, a job that will not start, a parked state the turn cannot write) gives the seat back as the delete that ends the row lands, never before (a delete the store did not take leaves the row, and its run, counted until the ending's retry deletes it); where the store did not answer the write, it ends the row only if the row names its job, and the seat is recounted from the store, since that write counted nothing. A launch refused before it closes its phase as failed — or as stopped, where a person stopped the seat — so no screen shows a phase that never ends. Nothing is parked in memory; everything the collection needs is in the row.

  **The record lands in two writes, and the state says which one it is at.** The turn's parked state (`internal/agent/execstate`: the round, the closed rounds, the surface and the skills it had loaded, the task, what it was asked and by whom, the items it wrote, the spend no segment has paid yet, the turn's deadline and the context it froze at its start — no conversation, since there is no engine loop to re-enter) is written by the turn as its frame unwinds, *after* the launch returns. So the launch opens the row as `launching` and the unwinding turn writes its state, flipping the row to `running` in the same compare-and-swap. In between, the job is already executing and the row has nothing to resume — so **nothing polls or claims a `launching` run**: a completion claimed in that window would find no turn to resume and would have to fail a run that finished. The window is milliseconds on an idle host and hundreds of milliseconds on a loaded one, and a trivial run is exactly the one that fits inside it.
- **A seat runs up to its cap of runs, one per conversation.** `sandbox.max_concurrent_runs` (two where unset) is how many of a seat's runs hold it at once, and no two of them work one conversation: its own, or one a wake its steps read came from ([ADR-0169](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0169-a-seat-runs-up-to-its-cap-of-runs-one-per-conversation.md)). Each launch and each answer's resume takes a slot in the same step as its write, refused at the cap or on a busy conversation, and the answer then waits for a slot. Below the cap the seat takes new work beside its runs, except a message that waits on one of them: one of a conversation a run works, or one the seat's [router](#notes-to-a-running-run) relates to a run (its requester's about its work, or another's the triage weighs). That message is routed to the run as at the cap (another writer's request put as a fold-in to the run's approvers, whose answer readmits it at once), then **set aside** on the inbox, unacknowledged and spending nothing, while the mail behind it flows; when the run leaves (settles, parks on a person, fails, is collected, or is found gone by a new owner's recovery) its waiting mail is readmitted at the head of the inbox, where a wake the run read is skipped as worked and an unread one runs as a turn of its own. An inbox holds at most 64 messages aside; past that it is held, as at the cap, until a readmit frees room. A person whose message waits so is told on its queued line. A launch's [budget floor](#budgets) counts the seat's other runs at the static floor each, since a run's spend is charged at its collection; and a checkout of a branch another of its runs pushes is refused, naming it. What follows is a seat at its cap, both of its runs working at the default of two.
- **A seat at its cap takes no other work, and that is every turn.** While its runs hold every slot (or the seat owes an answer's resume, or a reply a run let go of), the seat **starts no turn**: not for new work, not for a colleague's message. What reaches the run meanwhile is a message **about its work**: the seat's [router](#notes-to-a-running-run) reads the held inbox and hands the run its own requester's message in its conversation, about its work item or about a record the run wrote ([ADR-0167](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0167-a-busy-seats-wake-from-its-requester-joins-the-running-run.md)), anybody's information about the work, and a lead's correction as their note, each decided by a triage the engine gates ([ADR-0168](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0168-a-busy-seats-other-wakes-are-triaged-and-the-engine-gates-the-choice.md)); a request for other work waits. And **no person's answer to a different run of the same seat is resumed meanwhile**, whether that answer is a chat reply or one given [by naming the run](#answering-a-parked-run). That is the rule, not a cost of the mechanism: an agent in the middle of its work is busy with it, and it takes up the next thing when this one is done, as a person would; resuming a second run beside the first would put two of the seat's turns in flight at once, each acting for the seat without seeing the other. So **a seat runs no more executor runs at once than its cap**. A chat reply waits on the broker with the rest of the mail and is offered when the busy run **settles or parks on its own question**, which for a long job can be hours; an answer given by naming the run travels on the seat's control topic instead, is recorded on its run at once, and its resume waits for the busy run and then runs ahead of the held mail. Nothing is lost while either waits (the reply keeps its place and the question its anchor), and a parked run whose box outlives `pause_ttl_seconds` in the meantime re-seeds from its branch when the answer arrives.
- **Busy while it runs.** While its runs HOLD every slot of the seat's cap, the seat's inbox is **held** (the `sandbox` hold): the coordinator takes it as the launch that fills the last slot opens its run's row — and when a node that takes the seat over recovers runs still going, before the mailbox opens — and lifts it when one of them settles or parks on a question. The hold is taken for the attachment of the inbox the seat holds on that node, so a hold decided while the node held the seat and asked after its release detached the inbox is refused by the queue: it never gates the inbox the node attaches if it takes the seat back, which a seat retaken with nothing to recover would otherwise attach held, with nothing left to lift it. Held, nothing is fetched: the mail waits on the broker in order, nothing is held against a broker ack window during an hours-long run, no new turn starts and nothing runs at all until the run is done. The mail is still read: the seat's router hands the run each message its own requester wrote about its work (see [Notes to a running run](#notes-to-a-running-run)). A person's chat reply to *another* of the seat's runs waits with the rest of its mail and is offered when the run settles or parks; an answer by turn to one travels on the seat's control topic, is recorded at once, and its resume waits for the run and then runs ahead of the held mail. A colleague's [A2A ask](event-system.md#ephemeral-a2a-channels-internala2a) waits with the held mail as a chat reply does, and its channel is not closed under it: the idle sweep spares a channel whose seat's inbox is held, as it spares one whose ask a run's record carries. A run parked waiting on a human answer holds nothing — the seat works as usual, and its deliveries are offered to that question before they become turns (see [Mid-run clarification](#mid-run-clarification-ask_and_wait)).

  A delivery that reaches a held seat anyway (it raced the hold, or the queue refused to take it) asks for the hold again and is deferred, keeping its place at the head of the inbox — never requeued behind the seat's newer mail.
- **Completion → resume.** The resume starts a turn, so it asks the node's admission first, as every turn does ([ADR-0063](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0063-every-turn-on-a-node-passes-the-nodes-admission.md)): the seat owned fresh, a slot under `node.max_concurrent`, and no drain. It asks **before the claim**, so a node that refuses leaves the run exactly as it was, and the completion is handed back by the condition the refusal names: a draining node defers it, which quiesces the seat's control topic for the rest of the drain and leaves the completion at its head for the seat's next holder, while a condition that clears by waiting (the seat's ownership not yet proven again after a store blip) acknowledges it, spending none of its deliveries, because the waiter that drives the run's box announces a finished run again until a node claims it, on a schedule that doubles from one poll interval to twenty ([announced again on a schedule](#durability-completion-and-observability)). The node also keeps the refused completion and re-fires it **the moment the condition clears**, on the same signal that wakes an answer waiting on that condition, so the resume waits for the condition and not for the waiter; a clearing nothing signals is caught by that waiter's next announcement, at most **five minutes** after its last at the default cadence, and by the node's own re-fire of what it keeps, at the instant the refusal names for its lifting on the clock (a lease merely stale, a provider's limit) and never later than five minutes, save for a completion the node holds off itself until a limit's instant ([Both series are bounded](#mid-run-clarification-ask_and_wait)), whose re-fire waits for that instant, while its five-minute backstop before it does only what an announcement of the job does, ending the run once its turn's deadline has passed and otherwise keeping the hold, cancelled when the completion is carried or let go of, so a kept completion waits no longer where no waiter announces it. A completion whose resume its seat's budget held on the run's record is kept too, though the record holds it rather than the node: its delivery is spent by the hold and no claim wins before the hold's instant, which for a turn with a deadline is never later than the deadline, so the hold lapses there and the job comes round to be ended at it rather than when the budget's window turns, so the node re-fires it at that instant and never sooner, and on the signal that lifts the hold only once its own lift of the hold has landed (a lift the store does not answer leaves it kept for the instant), a signal that landed while the resume the budget held was still running included, since the node compares what was signalled before it admitted that resume, every lift that signal makes re-firing the job besides unless the node already keeps it for anything but that hold or is re-firing it, so neither a lift nor the seat's recovery starts a second re-fire beside one, and a lift clears only the hold it read, so one read before a re-fired resume was held again leaves that newer hold and re-fires nothing, while a keep for the very hold the lift cleared is re-fired in its place and a re-fire that leaves the job kept for that hold is followed by one as it returns, and the seat's recovery, after a restart or on the seat's next holder, keeps every held record it finds the same way, and since the write that holds the record also records the completion as owed, re-arms one whose hold a lift cleared before its re-fire claimed the job; a delivery of the completion that meets the hold leaves it kept, and a claim the hold refuses where nothing is kept for the job, whatever was kept in its place having re-fired into the hold, keeps it again from the record; with the box's host's store silent, nothing else announced the job once its hold had lifted. **The waiter is that backstop while the coordination store answers the box's host, and the broker is while it does not**: while the seat's holder keeps its clock on the store of the host of a `direct` or `container` box (below), or the run's record says what that clock would (the job's record of its host's last answer that its store did not answer it, which every hand-back of a claim writes, or the job recorded lost with that host and its round not yet carried on, which a node reads before it lets a delivery go), that host's waiter reads the run's record through a store that does not answer it and announces nothing, and a kept completion is the seat's holder's memory alone, which its restart or its letting go of the seat forgets. So the refused completion is then not acknowledged: it is still kept for the condition's signal, and its delivery is handed back on the queue's backoff whatever the condition (a drain and a seat let go of still hand it on) and renewed before its last (`sandbox_completion_renewed`), so nothing is lost to a restart, a release or a clearing nothing signals; a re-fire made while that delivery is in flight announces nothing afresh. **Every refusal the seat's holder acknowledges is owed on the run's record**, written before the acknowledgement by one write that takes it only where the record owes none (the condition and when, so a re-announcement refused again writes nothing): a silence of the store's runs alone, which the host's lease and presence do not share, has no bound, and a refusal kept in the holder's memory alone, made before any collection had heard of that silence, went with its restart or the seat's move. A record the store does not take is no acknowledgement: the delivery is handed back as the store's silence and recorded when it comes back. A draining node's refusal is never recorded: its delivery is handed on to the seat's next holder, never acknowledged, so it leaves nothing owed, and a write for it would have cost one per job and, where the store did not take it, handed the delivery back to the node that is leaving. The park on the job's question clears it, as the job's next launch and the run's end do, and the seat's recovery reads it ([below](#durability-completion-and-observability)). That host's waiter's own announcement says when it asked its store for the run's record it was made from, which a renewal, reading no record, never says, so one made from a read asked after the clock or the record began ends the clock, a claim of it clears the record, and a refusal of it is acknowledged again; one whose read was asked before ends nothing, however late it was made. Whichever arrives first claims the run, once. The box's waiter, its host's own, keeps running through a drain, so its keepalive keeps the box meanwhile, and it announces the run to the seat's next holder, who reads the box back through that host ([a waiter on every node](#durability-completion-and-observability), [ADR-0065](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0065-a-local-box-is-driven-by-the-node-that-launched-it.md)). The admission is held until the resume and its settle return. The completion event is claimed **at-most-once** (an atomic status flip on the row) and **only for the job it reports**: every launch gets a new id on the row and the completion carries it, so a duplicate that arrives after its job parked on a question, or after a relaunch started the next job, claims nothing. The result is collected, tokens are post-accounted once per run (see [Budgets](#budgets)), each launch is published once as a record of its own (see [each launch is published as its own record](#what-ends-a-run-each-launch-is-published-as-its-own-record)), and the turn is rebuilt from its parked state: the surface and skill-guard state as the run left them (as the launch recorded them, every tool the run can reach, with every skill it loaded over the bridge replayed onto them, so the collected phase's record lists the tools the run held as `tools_available`, with nothing left to discover beside them), the call log seeded with every call the turn and the run made, each counted by the identity it was admitted under (the digest of its whole canonical arguments) — the run's bridged calls in the order the bridge admitted them — and the run's `submit_work`, replayed from the bridged calls in its log, taken as the round's work. A run that never submitted is rescued as `incomplete`, never read off the prose it ended with. The engine's delivery check and the reviewer then judge it in the same turn (`Runner.Resume`). The same `turn_id` continues, so the whole sequence renders as one turn on the dashboard, and so does the round count: the collection is the round the run was launched in, so a launch and its collection share one `turn_engine.max_iterations`. A failed resume dispatch hands the claim back, to the status it was taken from, so the redelivered completion can retry, and the parked turn is never lost. That includes a resume a drain interrupts: the hand-back does not inherit the drain's cancellation, so the seat's next owner resumes the turn rather than reaping it as abandoned. The exceptions are resumed turns that must not be resumed again: one that broke after it had already written outside the engine (pushed a branch, commented on an issue), since a retry would repeat those writes; one that panicked, since a retry reaches the same defect; one refused for good, its round [lost with its host past its limit](#what-a-runs-record-and-its-log-keep), since every retry is refused the same way; one a person stopped, since the stop ended it; and one whose relaunch failed and ended its run with it, since a retry has no run left to collect. For each, the run is settled instead, its box reclaimed and its record deleted, and the seat is freed. Otherwise it hands back only the claim it took: when the resumed turn has already relaunched its executor and the relaunch started another job, or the seat's next owner has reaped the run as abandoned, the row is left as it stands, because the relaunch replaced the job a retry would collect and the reap has already ended the run. **The seat stays held through the resumed turn**: a run claimed for its resume is `resumed`, which holds the seat, and it is counted so until the resumed turn has returned and the run's record is gone, when the seat is recounted from the store. The record goes once the turn's end is on the executor log, which the run's ending records off the frame that ran the resume, by its own retry, once every capture of the turn has settled ([How a turn ends on the executor log](turn-engine.md#how-a-turn-ends-on-the-executor-log)): so the seat's next mail waits for the turn's captures to settle: each capture the end sees at most its whole life from the moment the end first sees it and one more read of the record, on which the end decides (about an hour and fifteen and a half minutes at the bounds: its take, a session upload at the object store's slowest pace, every change of its record, each given the thirteen minutes a change of a record at its bound takes to cross a link at the slowest pace allowed, and each read of it, that one included, the four minutes a read's reply takes), and a read standing by for one at most its window and its takeover's life, each with that read, about three hours and fifty-one and a half minutes in all from the moment the end first sees it — its taker's lease TTL and one read of the executor log for a capture whose taker stopped ([Each launch's session, kept](#each-launchs-session-kept)) — and for that write too. A store answering at an ordinary pace settles a capture in seconds. The resume's frame and that retry each recount the seat, and can do so at once; whichever is written second reads the store again first, so the seat is never counted held for a record the retry has deleted. The run used to be uncounted just before the resumer ran, which lifted the seat's inbox hold for the whole resumed turn and let the seat's next mail start a second turn, and a second job, beside it. And a seat runs up to its cap of turns on its node, one per conversation, whichever road the turn comes by (`node.ErrSeatFull`, `node.ErrConversationBusy`): a resume that finds no room waits for it, holding nothing, and one that is admitted holds the seat's inbox until it returns, so the mailbox fetches nothing meanwhile and spends none of its mail's deliveries.
- **A node makes at most `node.max_concurrent` reads of its runs' boxes at once.** Each read of a box made on the node, for a collection or for a stop's or a lost run's ending, holds one of as many collections as the node runs turns for the read alone, so these reads stay within the memory a Gitlet node keeps for them ([The cache on a Gitlet node](gitlet.md#the-cache-on-a-gitlet-node)). The admission does not bound them all: a completion past its turn's deadline that the node will not admit is collected and its run ended with no turn, and an ending starts none. A read asked of the node whose host the box is on holds none here; that node's own reads for its peers bound it. A read that waits says so (`sandbox_collection_waits`); one whose wait ends before it starts reads nothing (`sandbox_collection_unstarted`): a collection hands its claim back uncounted and the completion comes back, and an ending keeps its run and box for its retry. Every collection, the node's own or a peer's, also holds its weight of the node's [answer budget](../guides/deployment.md#the-engines-memory-limit) while it reads (a peer's until its reply is written): it opens every file it reads first, weighs them at five times the sizes those opens give (at least 5.3 MiB, at most 160 MiB), and reads each no further than that size, so a file that grew after the open is described as a piece past its bound, not read.
- **What the resumed half writes under.** The resumed turn's tracker, knowledge-base and chat writes derive their operation ids from the same unit of work as the first half's, minted at the instant that work began, so a first-half write the second half repeats — the retry an `unknown` asks for — lands once. The exception is a resume that runs **more than twenty-nine days after its work began**: the [operation ledger](../guides/replication.md#what-a-retry-is-judged-by-the-instant-its-operation-was-minted) keeps each row thirty days, and an operation minted before what a node's ledger swept, whose row is gone, is answered `unknown` and never published — so minted at that start, every write the resumed half made would be lost on every data node. Such a half is **rebased**: it mints its ids at the attempt instead and records that instant in the fleet's coordination store under the unit of work, logged as `turn_rebased`; the price is that a first-half write it repeats is written a second time — except a work-item comment, a created item and a created view, whose ids are the keys of their rows and are derived as the work began, so the first half's is found and answered from its row rather than made again. **Every attempt is judged against its own clock.** A resume that fails is retried — by the completion coming round again, or by the person's next answer, which can be weeks later — and each retry is judged afresh, never held to a decision an attempt took while the start still looked recent. A later attempt **inherits** a recorded instant while it is within the same twenty-nine days of it, so a failed resume retried on this node, on the seat's next owner or after a restart derives the ids the attempt before it derived, and so does the resume of the turn's next launch — a reviewer's send-back, or a run carried on with a person's answer — whatever the earlier attempt or the earlier half wrote is not written twice. The line is drawn a day short of the thirty so that no sweep passes the instant while one attempt is still working. A turn with no unit of work seeds its ids from its run and mints them at the run's start, and is rebased by the same rule, under its run; a scheduled fire is not one, since its fire is a `task_assigned` the completion ledger records, and its unit of work is that fire, or every fire a merged run stands for. The same rule covers a trigger dispatched long after it arrived — see [Turn Engine](turn-engine.md#a-turns-two-identities).
- **Reuse across launches.** On collect the box is **paused** (its process tree stopped, or its container paused), not destroyed. A relaunch in the same turn — a reviewer's `self_iterate`, or a person's answer carrying a parked run on — **continues in it**, checkout and disk state kept and provisioning not applied again, when the job that used it is over, the member the launch picks runs the same harness in the same cell, the box is on this node's own host, and the box is **younger than seven days**, counted from when it was first attached to the run (`PriorBox.ContinuesIn`). The age is the box's, not a job's: every send-back and every answer launches a job with a credential of its own, so without it one checkout could work for as long as the turn lasts, and Gitlet keeps a deleted seat branch's engine commits for fourteen days after the deletion, after which a box pushing one back is refused `forged_committer`. Seven days — the fourteen less the seven a job's credential is valid for — keeps every push from a box inside that window; an older box is reclaimed (`sandbox_prior_reclaimed`, its `box_since` the date) and the job starts in a fresh box from the pushed branch. Its harness's session is not the box's to keep: every relaunch of the turn — a send-back as much as a run carried on — continues the turn's session where it can, from the copy this box holds or from the turn's kept capture restored into whichever box the launch gets ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). Otherwise the box is **reclaimed through its own cell** before the fresh one exists (`sandbox_prior_reclaimed`), so a fallback onto a member in another cell moves the run without leaving its last box behind; a box that cannot be reattached is reclaimed and replaced (`sandbox_reuse_failed`), the work re-seeding from the pushed branch; and a box on another node's host — the seat moved since the last launch — is left to that host, whose waiter reclaims it (`sandbox_prior_left_to_host`, see [A box is the node's that launched it](#durability-completion-and-observability)). Whichever ending the turn reaches reclaims the box its row names. The two jobs are told apart by the launch id, not the row's status: a new job that finishes, or parks on a question of its own, before the resumed turn has returned keeps its box and its tail.
- **Publishing a build from the box.** `create_artifact` and `publish_artifact` name a box as a source — `source: {sandbox: "dist"}` for a directory as an artifact's whole file set, `from_sandbox` for one file, each relative to the workspace — and the engine serves one only to **the run working in it**: the run's own call, made over its bridge while its record reads `running`, so the run publishes its build when it says the build is ready. A [worker](turn-engine.md#workers) the run delegates to never makes that call: both tools write to a surface people read, and a worker is granted no such tool. It attaches that box as a reader — never resumed — lists the directory through the box itself with links never followed, holds every listed path to the workspace and the published-path grammar, and streams each file through the [artifact upload pipeline](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#artifacts), which reserved its bytes first and reads them back verified before the version is decided. The box is never handed an upload URL or a credential. A seat's call that finds no such run — none launched yet, parked on a question (its job paused, which a read would wake), collected, another seat's, or torn down — is refused `not_running`, and nothing is published; so is one served on a node other than the one that launched a `direct` or `container` box, which only that node reaches ([ADR-0065](../../adr/0065-a-local-box-is-driven-by-the-node-that-launched-it.md)). A caller that is not an agent seat — a person, or their own assistant, calling through the operator catalogue — has no such run and is refused `forbidden`; a seat's call on a node that runs no sandbox is refused `unavailable`. A collected run's resumed segment calls no artifact tool — its reviewer holds one submission tool — so a running record is the only one a box source is read for. A `from_sandbox` path that names no file (one that's missing, a directory or a link), and a `sandbox` source that names no directory (one that's missing, a file or a link), are refused `invalid`, for the seat to name another. A workspace that's gone from the box is refused `not_running`, for the seat to build again, and a directory the box couldn't walk whole (a directory under it the box's user can't open, a read error) is refused `conflict` rather than published as the part it could read: the listing reads `find`'s own exit, and passes the directory to it as `./dir`, so a name that reads like one of its options is still a directory. A box its provider can't read right now is told by the [same classes](#when-a-run-does-not-start) a launch is, with a wait offered only where one helps, and so is a listing or a file check the box itself ended: one it timed out or killed, or whose container runtime failed on its own side, is the box not answering, and one whose box can't run its shell, `find` or `head` is its image, a `configuration`.
- **A settled run has no record.** When a run ends, whether its turn finished, a person stopped it, or it failed, its box is reclaimed first and then its record is **deleted** from the coordination store, once the ending's last step is done: where the engine records every turn's end, once that end is on the executor log. Until then the executors board shows the run's decided `ending` beside the status it was ended in, its box no longer its own, and nobody is asked to answer it. The record's bucket has no age (a parked run can wait days, and an age would reap a parked run's only record of its turn and its answer), and the completion poll and every seat recovery read all of it, so a finished run kept there would be read on every one of those passes for the life of the deployment. What a run ended as is recorded elsewhere: the resumed turn's own phase events, an `executor_failed` event naming why it was lost, or an `executor_stopped` event naming who stopped it. The box goes first on purpose: a record that outlives its box is reaped by the seat's next recovery, while a box that outlived its record would be named by nothing.
- **An ending is decided before it is done, and announced exactly once.** Ending a run is several effects in several systems — a person's reply handed back to the seat's inbox, the box reclaimed, the loss announced, the record deleted — and a node can stop between any two. So the ending is first **decided on the run's record** (`ending`), in one compare-and-set under the ending's terms: what it announces, under an identity of its own, and whether a person's reply goes back. From then on the record takes **no other write** — no claim, no take of an answer, no hand-back of a claim, no relaunch, no new answer, no park — so nothing can move the run off the ending, and whoever reads the record next (this node's retry, or the seat's next holder) finishes **that** ending from wherever it stopped, never one of its own. The loss is announced (`executor_failed`) **before** the record is deleted, under an id derived from the run and its ending and the instant it was decided, so a repeat after a crash is the same event to the event store — whose key is that (time, id) pair — and to the fleet's reads, which merge rows on it. The announcement used to be made only after the delete: a delete that landed and reported a failure, or a node that stopped between the two, left the loss announced by nobody, and the seat's next holder, finding the claim the delete had not taken, announced it as `abandoned_tail` whatever it had been ended for. A broker that refuses the announcement keeps the ending, and the seat's mail waits behind it until it is made. **The box goes after the decision, never before it.** An ending is made by a node that read the run and decided it is over, and that read can be stale: a node that lost the seat while settling a claim it had taken used to kill the box first, off its own read, and only then had its ending refused under the seat's next holder's lease — after that holder had given the claim back to its answer, so the run it then resumed had lost its checkout while its record still named the box. The reclaim now rides the decided ending, so the store checks the ending's lease against the run as it stands before anything is killed, and an ending refused there leaves the box to the run's holder; whoever finishes the ending — this node or the seat's next holder — reclaims the box the record names before deleting it. A node that loses the run that way says nothing about it either: what became of the run, and of a reply on it, is announced by whoever holds it now.
- **A person's stop is an ending too, and never a loss.** A [pause with `stop_running`](agent-runtime.md#pausing-a-seat) ends the seat's runs that are launching or running, at once, on the node that holds the seat — when the pause lands, when the node next reads every pause, or when it acquires the stopped seat. The stop is decided on the run's record like any ending, with **who stopped it** recorded in the same write, and only while the run is still that job in one of those two statuses: a run whose completion was claimed first is a resumed turn, which the turn's own fence stops at its next round, and whose call that was out as the stop landed, if it comes back refused for a limit or the seat's budget, is settled as stopped there and then rather than waiting for the limit's instant or the window's turn, and parks nothing; so is a run back in `running` whose job a collection already read — its resume held by the seat's budget, held by its node for a model's limit, or handed back for a retry — which the store refuses a stop of, because its job is over and its spend is the resume's to charge, once, and whose wait the stop ends instead (its hold lifted, a completion its node kept re-fired, and a stopped seat's completion admitted past its budget and its models' limit, which its stopped turn never reaches), so that turn is closed now rather than when its condition would have cleared; and a run parked on a person's question does no work and stays parked behind the pause. Finishing it closes the run's tool-bridge session first — nothing it does after that acts as the seat — then **ends the job**, off the frame that decided the stop and whatever `conversation_session.enabled` says, since ending a job is waiting for it: the job's script, asked, stops its harness and packs the session as its own end does ([Claude Code](#a-claude-code-runs-session), [OpenCode](#an-opencode-runs-session)), and a job not over within 2¼ minutes, or one whose script answers no request (one an older build started), is killed. Only then does it read what the run had spent off its box, charge it to the token counters and publish it as the launch's own `executor_collected` record (noted as stopped, not failed, and saying how the job was ended), all recorded on the row so a repeat after a crash neither charges nor publishes twice; then the box is reclaimed and the stop is announced as `executor_stopped`, under an id derived from the run and its ending exactly as a loss is. The turn that was parked on the run is closed as stopped — `agent_turn_stopped` and a completion carrying `stopped` — under identities derived from the same ending, so the seat's next holder finishing a stop this node could not finish closes the turn once. A run stopped while its turn was still launching it is closed by that turn as it unwinds: its park is refused, and it ends as stopped — from the stop's own decision, which the node keeps for that turn, so a seat resumed before the turn unwinds does not turn the stop into a park with nowhere to go. The completion poll leaves a run whose ending is decided alone, so it never keeps alive a box the ending is reclaiming.
- **Review sees the whole turn.** Every call the run made over the bridge is recorded in the log kept beside its row, in the order it was admitted, and joins the turn's record after the closed rounds' calls when the turn resumes, so the delivery check and the reviewer's evidence see what the run did as the seat. The harness's own editing, commands, tests and commits happen inside the box and are in **no** log, and every review is told so: the reviewer judges that work on the executor's report and on the branches and pull requests listed under `## What the agent delivered`, and a missing shell or test call is never fabrication. Nor is a person's reply in any log: one refused as too large for the run to take is shown to the reviewer under `## Replies the agent did not get`, so a question the run asked again after it reads as the follow-up it is ([below](#mid-run-clarification-ask_and_wait)).

There is deliberately no synchronous "block the turn until the run finishes" shape: a turn that held its concurrency slot and its broker message for a real run's length would trip the inbox ack window and the shutdown drain. A short run in the detached model simply completes fast.

---

## Configuring it

One block is required and one is optional. **`providers.sandbox`** is the catalogue every agent seat's executor runs in, and a company needs it as soon as it has an agent seat and a `providers.llm` entry: without it the company is refused at `providers.sandbox`, once, naming the first such seat and how many more, and suggesting `local: {}` with `default_run_in: direct` (on this host as the engine's user) or `default_run_in: container` with a `local.image` holding the harness. A company with no agent seat, or an org chart written before its credentials (no `providers.llm` entry yet), needs none: it holds every seat's work until a revision adds a model, and the catalogue with it. A seat's own **`role.sandbox`** is optional, and only adds what that seat's box reads.
### Engine provider — `providers.sandbox`

A sibling of `providers.llm`, live-reloadable; secrets are `${VAR}` references resolved at construction.

```yaml
providers:
  sandbox:
    # THE CATALOGUE: the engine host's boxes, in both cells.
    local:
      state_dir: ""               # empty → $CREWLET_SANDBOX_LOCAL_HOME,
                                  #   else ~/.crewlet/sandboxes
      image: ""                   # required where a run is placed in a container;
                                  #   a company hosting code runs its checks in it
      runtime: ""                 # auto | docker | podman; empty → auto
      network: ""                 # the container network; "none" cuts the box off
      run_args: []                # how a container box is SIZED
      runtime_env: {}             # extra environment for the docker/podman CLI
                                  #   itself, never the box (below)

    default_run_in: direct        # direct | container — where a run on a
                                  #   providers.llm entry naming no run_in happens
    host_grace_seconds: 900       # how long a launching node may be away — NOT a run cap (below)
    default_pause_ttl_seconds: 1800     # omit for this default; 0 = never pause. how long a blocked run's paused box is
                                        #   held before the reaper takes it
    default_max_turns: 0          # agentic-round cap for one executor run; unset or 0 = uncapped
    commit_attribution: true      # credit Crewlet as co-author on a run's own commits;
                                  #   unset = true, false = credit nothing (below)
    setup: []                     # engine-wide provisioning steps (see Setup steps)
```

- **The block is a catalogue, not a mode.** It says which boxes *exist*; the `run_in` of each `providers.llm` entry, else `default_run_in`, says where a run on that entry goes. A company has one `providers.sandbox`, so a company-wide `type:` could not serve both the run whose harness needs the host's own reach and the run that must reach none of the host's files; write two entries and point each seat at the right one. **The block may be left out** only by a company with no agent seat or no `providers.llm` entry yet; absent means "no boxes", and a company whose agent seats have a model and no box is refused.
- **An empty block is refused.** `providers.sandbox: {}` configures nothing, and every agent seat's executor needs a cell. Give it `local:` or `fake: true`.
- **`default_run_in` is required unless `fake: true`, or nothing would read it.** `local:` is **two** cells (`direct` and `container`) with no implicit answer: `direct` runs the harness as the engine's own user and `container` needs an image holding it, so neither is chosen for an operator who did not say. Only `fake: true` resolves on its own. It is required when some entry a seat's executor can launch on (a `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `qwen-code`, `opencode`, `copilot`, `grok`, `muse-code`, `kimi-code`, `hermes` or `pi` member of its executor chain) names no `run_in`. A company whose every such entry names its own cell needs no default; validation refuses the silent entry **where it is written**, offering `default_run_in` as the other remedy.

An ambiguous catalogue may not reach **nothing at all**: a default, an entry's `run_in` or a company's [checks](#check-boxes) (which reach `container` once `local.image` is set) has to name some cell. A backend is built only for a cell something reaches, so a catalogue nothing names builds none, which is why an empty block is refused too. Every catalogue that resolves a default reaches it, so a seat added later has somewhere to go.
- **`local.image`, `runtime`, `network`, `run_args` and `runtime_env` are container-only**, checked against the cells your executors reach: an image is **required** when some run is placed in a container and **refused** when nothing runs in one (it would configure nothing). On a company hosting code the image is what its [checks](#check-boxes) run in, so there it always reaches `container`. This keeps a direct-only company valid and fails a container company at validation rather than at container create, minutes into a turn.

- **`host_grace_seconds` is neither a run-time nor a provisioning limit.** It is how long the node that launched a run's box may be absent from the fleet, or find its store silent, before the run is [recorded lost or its parked box released](#durability-completion-and-observability); and the orphan reaper's cutoff on a node's box root: a box that records neither a run nor a check, with nothing running and no keepalive stamp for this long, is reaped ([Local sandboxes](#local-sandboxes)). The completion poll stamps a running box on every tick, and a launch stamps a box still [provisioning](#setup-steps--provisioning-the-box) every 15 s until its setup steps are done, so the cutoff never takes a live box. The 900 s default outlasts a node's restart or rolling deploy, which comes back and keeps its runs. A run is never stopped on a clock of its box's. The one clock that ends a run is its **turn's** wall-clock cap, where the trigger carries one (a scheduled fire's `timeout_seconds`): written on the run's row as its deadline, it makes the completion poll end a run still working past it (`sandbox_run_past_deadline`); the collection ends the job as a person's stop does (harness told to stop, session packed as its own end packs it) and reads what the run did, marked as cut off.
- **`default_pause_ttl_seconds`** bounds how long a run blocked on a human answer keeps its *paused* box. A paused box holds its directory on the launching node's box root and its memory (a stopped process tree, or a paused container), and nothing else reclaims it while the run waits, so expiring it is the engine's job: past this age the completion poll [reaps it](#mid-run-clarification-ask_and_wait), and when the answer arrives the run continues in a fresh box from the pushed branch. A paused box keeps the run's **working tree** (uncommitted work included) and its harness's copy of the conversation. Where the turn kept the asking run's session ([Each launch's session, kept](#each-launchs-session-kept)), the relaunch continues it in any box, so the conversation outlasts the reap; where it kept none (`turn_engine.conversation_session.enabled: false`, or the capture refused, the seat's session budget full say), the paused box is the conversation's one copy, and an answer after the reap continues in a session of its own, told the question and the answer ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). 30 minutes, by when a person is evidently not answering promptly, trades that held disk and memory against the working tree surviving quick replies; raise it if your teams answer in hours. `0` means never pause: the box is torn down the moment the run blocks. *Omitting* the key takes the 1800s default; the field distinguishes the two. Negative values are rejected (an unbounded pause is the leak the knob prevents). A *role* inherits this default by leaving `role.sandbox.pause_ttl_seconds` out; a negative role value is rejected too. Correctness never depends on the box: the durable state is the pushed branch plus the persisted row.
- **`default_max_turns` is off unless you set it.** The harness judges how many rounds a task takes, so runs are uncapped unless the company or seat sets a bound. A positive value caps the run's agentic *rounds* (work done, not time) on every runner: Claude Code's `--max-turns`, Gemini CLI's and Qwen Code's `model.maxSessionTurns`, OpenCode's agent `steps`, Copilot's extension ([GitHub Copilot CLI](#github-copilot-cli)), Grok Build's `--max-turns` ([Grok Build](#grok-build)), Muse Code's `--max-model-steps` ([Muse Code](#muse-code)), Kimi Code's steps a turn ([Kimi Code](#kimi-code)), Pi's extension ([Pi](#pi)), and for Codex, which has no such setting, its note helper's count of each turn's model responses ([Codex](#codex)). **Unset or `0`, a run is uncapped**; a negative value is refused. An uncapped run is still never stopped on a clock of its box's (see `host_grace_seconds`): it ends when it finishes, at a scheduled turn's own cap, or when a person [stops it](agent-runtime.md#pausing-a-seat), and what it spent is charged against the seat's [budget](#budgets) when collected. Set a cap for a wall that a run going in circles hits within one turn, such as a weaker model running unattended on your own plan window. There is no companion budget cap: the fleet's [token meter](agent-learning.md) already post-charges a collected run, and a second ceiling in the operator's dollars would disagree with it. A role overrides this with `role.sandbox.max_turns`, where `0` lifts a company's cap for that seat.
- **`commit_attribution` credits Crewlet on the commits a run makes as itself**, unless `false`: `Co-authored-by: Crewlet <noreply@crewlet.com>`, plus `Crewlet-Seat`, `Crewlet-Run: <turn id>` and `Crewlet-Work-Item` naming the seat, run and work item, added by git rather than the model. A person's commit the run amends, cherry-picks or rebases is never credited. See [Commit attribution](#commit-attribution).
- **Sizing is `local.run_args`, not a limits knob.** There is no `default_limits`: a `container` box is sized with `local.run_args` (`--cpus`, `--memory`), and a `direct` box shares the host. There is no per-run or per-seat size: sizing belongs to the backend, configured once.
- **Hot-reload, in every direction, with no restart.** The runtime under the catalogue (the coordinator that holds which seats are mid-run, and the completion poll) belongs to the *process*, so the first company that reaches a sandbox cell brings it up **once**: at boot, or at the apply that brings one (the apply's `sandbox_runtime` stage; see [Configuration](configuration.md#the-engine-half)). That covers a node started with no company (the quickstart's route) and a company adding `providers.sandbox` later. The same apply prepares seats the node **already** holds: each attaches its completion topic and recovers the runs recorded on it, as a later-taken seat does, and a seat whose preparation fails is handed back so its next acquisition runs all of it. After that a revision only **swaps the manager** (`Coordinator.SetManager`), and three rules keep in-flight runs whole:
  - **The poll follows the swap.** It asks the coordinator for its current manager each tick, so a job launched after a reload is polled through the backend that made it.
  - **A dropped cell stays reachable for what is already on it.** A run's placement is on its row, so a revision removing a cell (`local:` taken out while a `container` job runs) carries that backend as *retired*: running jobs are still polled, collected and reclaimed, and parked ones reaped, through it, while no new box is provisioned there. An entry still naming the removed cell, or falling to it as the default, is refused at validation.
  - **Removing the block keeps the last manager.** A company validates with no `providers.sandbox` only when it has no agent seat or no `providers.llm` entry, and every launch reads its turn's pinned epoch, so it launches nothing; the runtime and last manager stay to finish runs in flight.

  A catalogue that cannot be **built** is refused before anything on the node changes, so a company whose executors would launch into a box nobody can mint is never published.

### A seat's own box settings — `role.sandbox`

The block places nothing: the box is placed by the `run_in` of the `providers.llm` entry the launch picks, else `providers.sandbox.default_run_in`, and the runner is that entry's harness. It holds what the seat's box reads beyond the engine-wide settings: `setup`, `env`, `optional_keys`, `mcp`, `pause_ttl_seconds`, `max_turns` and `max_concurrent_runs`. Absent, the box gets the engine-wide settings alone. Any other key is refused as unknown.

```yaml
roles:
  - name: Senior Engineer
    handle: senior-engineer
    mcp_env:
      github: { Authorization: "Bearer ${GITHUB_APP_TOKEN_SENIOR_ENGINEER}" }
    sandbox:
      # pause_ttl_seconds:              # leave out → provider default; 0 → never hold a paused box
      # max_turns:                      # leave out → provider default (uncapped unless set); 0 → uncapped
      # max_concurrent_runs:            # leave out → 2; runs holding the seat at once, one per conversation
      env:                              # env injected into this seat's runs, ${VAR}-expanded
        NPM_TOKEN: "${NPM_TOKEN_SENIOR}"
        DATABASE_URL: "postgres://${TEST_DB_HOST}/app"
      optional_keys: [DATABASE_URL]     # expected to resolve to nothing at times: left out quietly,
                                        #   where any other unresolved key is left out and logged
                                        #   (sandbox_env_unresolved) as a gap in the run's environment
      mcp:
        servers: [files]                # the role's MCP servers that run in the box; the
                                        #   tool bridge serves every other one it holds
      setup:                            # per-role provisioning steps, applied after the
        - name: node                    #   engine-wide providers.sandbox.setup
          # No `corepack enable`: it writes pnpm's shim beside the Node binary,
          # and a setup command runs as the box's own account — the engine's
          # user, on the host for `direct` — which cannot write there
          # when Node was installed as root. `corepack pnpm …` needs no shim.
          commands: ["command -v corepack >/dev/null || { echo 'no corepack on PATH' >&2; exit 1; }"]
          brief: "Node and corepack are installed; run the repo's pinned package manager through corepack (`corepack pnpm install`), never a bare `pnpm`."
```

`role.sandbox.env` declares **external-service tokens** (a registry token, a test database). The agent's own credential at an integration is not declared here: Crewlet puts it in the box, such as the agent's GitHub App token as `GITHUB_TOKEN` and its Expo robot's as `EXPO_TOKEN`, so PRs and MRs land under the agent's own identity (see [An agent's own integration credentials](#an-agents-own-integration-credentials)).

---

## Where a run happens

A `providers.llm` entry's `run_in` (else `providers.sandbox.default_run_in`) names one **cell** of the catalogue, and every executor run on that entry happens there. Two cells, one backend:

| `run_in` | Backend | Runs as | Isolates state | Isolates the **host** | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direct` | `local:` | the engine user, on the host | yes | **no** | the harness installed on that host |
| `container` | `local:` | a PID in a Docker/Podman container | yes | yes | `local.image` with the harness ([bring your own](#bring-your-own-image)) |

The entry places a run, not the seat, because what a run needs from the host is its runtime's: the entry whose harness needs the host's own reach runs `direct`, the rest run in `container`. An entry naming none takes `default_run_in`, resolved at **launch**, so changing the catalogue reaches every entry that wrote nothing. The entry's cell is **reached**: its backend is built, and `run_in: container` needs `local.image`. A seat's `role.sandbox` therefore places nothing; its `setup`, `env`, `mcp`, `pause_ttl_seconds` and `max_turns` are the seat's settings for the box its entry places. Validation refuses the impossible and nothing else, each case otherwise reading as working configuration and failing inside a turn:
- a run reaching `container` with no `local.image`;
- an entry some seat's executor reaches that names no cell, against a catalogue with no default;
- agent seats with models in a company with no catalogue at all;
- a `run_in` on an entry whose harness cannot run an executor (anything but `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `qwen-code`, `opencode`, `copilot`, `grok`, `muse-code`, `kimi-code`, `hermes` and `pi`), since no launch would read it.

### Choosing a cell

The run is the same fully permissioned harness in every cell; what differs is what it can reach.

- **`direct`** runs it as a process tree on the engine host, as the engine's own user, in a directory of its own. It is the shortest path (no image, the subscription login `crewlet llm login` already made on that host) and fits a dedicated host you will hand to an autonomous agent, an entry that needs the host itself, or a first run on your own machine while its seats take work from you alone: the run can read what the engine's user can read and reach what that user's credentials reach. On any node that binds `api.port`, a `direct` box reaches its [tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box) on that node's own loopback listener with nothing to set, which is why the [quickstart](../getting-started/quickstart.md) starts every seat this way; before a seat takes work from anyone else, move the runs into `container`.
- **`container`** runs it in a Docker or Podman container on the engine host with only the box's own directory mounted. It needs `local.image` with the harness ([Bring your own image](#bring-your-own-image)) and `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL`, which a single host sets to its own loopback: a loopback address is handed to the box under the runtime's name for the engine host, and on Linux `api.host` must not be loopback, since the container's calls arrive from its bridge network ([Local sandboxes](#local-sandboxes)). Pick it for any other instance (a workstation included), a shared host, or work that should not reach the engine host's files.

A company can use both: two entries on the same harness and model with different `run_in` let each seat take the right one, and a fallback member of a seat's executor chain is placed by its own `run_in`.

**A run remembers its cell.** The placement is written onto the run's durable row *before the box exists*, and reconnect, teardown and the pause reaper read it from there rather than re-derive it: the collecting turn may be another process on another node, days later, after the configuration changed, and reconnecting a `container` box as a `direct` one reports a box that has vanished, abandoning a running job as gone. An entry naming no cell is given the company's default at launch, so every row names one.

### Whether a cell is ready

Each node probes the cells `providers.sandbox` declares and publishes the answer on its [status record](coordination.md#its-status-record), so the Models page can say per node which cells can start a box now and disable the rest with the reason:

| Cell | Ready when |
|---|---|
| `direct` | the box root under `local.state_dir` is writable |
| `container` | `local.image` is set, the runtime (`docker` or `podman`, per `local.runtime`) is on the engine's `PATH`, and its daemon answers `version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'` within 5 s |

A cell the company does not declare reads `unconfigured`, never not ready. A cell not ready carries its fix, for example "Install Docker or Podman on this node and restart the engine: PATH is read at start". The probe runs at boot, at every apply and every minute, and never makes a box. `direct` is not probed for host confinement: its box is not confined, so a host without bubblewrap or Landlock still runs it.

### Sandbox backends

The provider layer is pluggable behind the `sandbox.Provider` interface (`internal/sandbox/protocol.go`). One backend runs code, and one stands in for it:

- **[Local](#local-sandboxes)** (`local:`). The engine host itself — `run_in: direct` (a process tree) or `run_in: container` (Docker/Podman). The harness can use the **subscription login** `crewlet llm login` already established. See below.
- **`fake: true`** — deterministic in-process stubs (`internal/sandbox/fake.go`): an in-memory filesystem, scripted harness results, no network. The unit-test substrate, and a way to demonstrate the flow: it does **not** run real code, and every run it plays finishes at once with a report saying the double played it, so the turn collects a run that submitted nothing and is judged on that. It answers **every** cell, and is refused beside `local:` — the double *replaces* the backend rather than joining it, so a real block underneath it would read as configuration and configure nothing.
- **No sandbox at all** — omit `providers.sandbox`, which only a company with no agent seat, or with no `providers.llm` entry yet, may do. Any other company is refused at `providers.sandbox`, naming its first agent seat.

The closed set `run_in` is checked against is exactly the set the engine can construct — a test walks it, because a value the config accepts and the engine cannot build fails at the first run and nowhere earlier. The engine builds a backend only for the cells your company actually **reaches**, read from the same computation validation uses: built eagerly instead, it constructed a container backend for a company whose seats all run `direct` and failed the apply demanding an image the validator had just refused as a field nothing would read.

### Local sandboxes

The `local:` backend runs the harness on the machine running `crewlet run`: you already logged a harness in on that host ([LLM backends](llm-backends.md)) and every executor run uses that login, with no account, API key or token of its own.

```yaml
providers:
  sandbox:
    local:
      state_dir: ""               # empty → $CREWLET_SANDBOX_LOCAL_HOME,
                                  #   else ~/.crewlet/sandboxes
    default_run_in: direct        # direct | container — no implied answer
```

**`state_dir` is the box root** of both cells: a seat's box is made under its `boxes/`. Give it a volume sized for boxes, never the one holding the store and the stream ([Where a box writes](../guides/deployment.md#where-a-box-writes)).

The shipped example, [`examples/nimbus.company.yaml`](../../examples/nimbus.company.yaml), pairs a `local:` catalogue with `run_in: direct` and runs every seat's executor as its entry's [own run in a box](llm-backends.md#the-executors-run-in-a-box) on the engine host, on the Claude Code entry's plan login: a first run on your own machine while its seats take work from you alone. It names the `container` block to move to before a seat takes work from anyone else. Its code is on [Gitlet](gitlet.md), so a run checks a repository out with `code_checkout` and proposes its branch as a change; the catalogue needs no git recipe, since the engine gives the box its git ([Repositories on Gitlet](#repositories-on-gitlet)) once the node is given `CREWLET_BOX_GIT_URL`.

A sandbox needs no code host: with nowhere to push it still runs a spike, benchmark, reproduction or SDK example. Add a code host later and the same runs open changes or merge requests; the sandbox block does not change.

**`local:` alone still needs a `default_run_in`** (or a `run_in` on every entry a seat's executor launches on), because choosing `direct` is choosing to run an autonomous harness as the engine user. The block has no mode of its own: `direct` and `container` are a choice about **one entry's runs**. Point seats that should use the host's login at an entry with `run_in: direct`, the others at one with `run_in: container`.

| | `run_in: direct` | `run_in: container` |
|---|---|---|
| Runs as | the engine user, on the host | PID inside a Docker/Podman container |
| Isolates state (per box) | yes | yes |
| Isolates the **host** | **no** | yes |
| Needs an image | no | yes (`image:`, no default) |
| A setup file outside the box's home | refused: it would be the host's | refused: only the home is mounted |
| Setup commands run | on the host, as the engine user | in the container: as the engine's uid on a rootful runtime, as container root on a rootless one |
| Sizing | the host | `run_args: ["--cpus", "2", "--memory", "4g"]` |
| When memory runs out (Linux) | the kernel kills the box before the engine | the same, through the runtime's `--oom-score-adj`; past its own `--memory`, only inside the container |

**Both modes isolate state.** Each box has its own directory under `boxes/` with two sides:

- `home/` is the agent's. `HOME`, the XDG variables and `TMPDIR` point inside it; its working directory is an empty per-box workspace there (a `direct` command starts in the home and its own shell enters the directory it was asked to run in); in `container` mode it is the one directory mounted into the container.
- `records/` is the engine's: the logins the box was seeded with and a digest of each (so a reconnected teardown knows what to write back, where, and against what), the keepalive stamp, a `direct` job's process group, a `container` job's process group in its container (read at the job's start so a kill reaches the whole job and nothing else of the container's), the engine process that last saw the box's job running (see [A job lost with its host](#durability-completion-and-observability)), and the env file. The two sides are separate so a containerised job cannot rewrite what the engine knows about its own box.

A box's environment is **allowlisted** (PATH, locale, TLS trust, proxy; never the engine's keyring, Tier A token values, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` or the collector credential in `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`). It is the allowlist every child the engine starts gets, a [stdio MCP server](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#what-a-stdio-servers-environment-is) and a harness included. In `container` mode the run environment goes to the runtime through an `--env-file` in the box's records, not `-e KEY=value`, because argv is world-readable on the host (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, every `ps`) and that environment carries the seat's LLM key and whatever token `role.sandbox.env` declares. A `direct` job runs as the engine's user with no mount, so it can reach its box's records too.

**The container runtime's own CLI gets an explicit environment too.** Every `docker`/`podman` invocation (`run`, `exec`, `pause`, `rm`, `ps`, `info`) gets exactly the environment a [stdio MCP server whose `command` is `docker` or `podman`](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#what-a-stdio-servers-environment-is) gets, which that table lists name by name: the host allowlist, the engine user's home, temporary and XDG directories (the runtime's config, and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, where a rootless daemon's socket lives), and the runtime's own configuration (the `DOCKER_*` family, Podman's, and the few settings they read by name). Nothing else of the engine's reaches it, or any plugin and credential helper it runs.

**Whatever else the runtime needs, declare in `local.runtime_env`**: for example the role, profile or key file a credential helper needs to pull your image from a private registry (`docker-credential-ecr-login`, `docker-credential-gcr`), or settings of a runtime plugin. Name them as you would an MCP server's `env:`: a `${VAR}` resolves from the [secret store](secret-store.md) first, then the engine's own environment, when the backend is built on an apply. A declared name wins over the fixed list's value for it.

```yaml
providers:
  sandbox:
    local:
      image: ghcr.io/acme/crewlet-coding:1
      runtime_env:
        AWS_ROLE_ARN: "${REGISTRY_PULL_ROLE}"         # docker-credential-ecr-login
        AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE: /var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token
        GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS: "${GCR_KEY_FILE}"   # docker-credential-gcr
```

It is the **runtime's** environment, never the box's: nothing in it reaches the harness except through an argument you add to `run_args`. A bare `-e NAME` in `local.run_args` copies `NAME` from the runtime harness's environment, so it copies only a name the fixed list carries or `runtime_env` declares; anything else arrives unset, and `crewlet validate` warns about each such `-e NAME`. Put what a box needs in `role.sandbox.env` (or a setup step's `env`), which reaches the box directly.

**Boxes are removed at teardown, and one left behind is reclaimed by its node.** A box made for a run records the run and is its node's completion poll's to reclaim: kept while the run's record names it, reclaimed once that record is gone or names another box, which the poll's first pass after a restart finds for a run that ended while the node was stopped. A run blocked on a human answer keeps its box, its job ended and nothing touching it, until `pause_ttl_seconds`. A [check's box](#check-boxes) records its check's attempt and is its node's check runner's to reclaim the same way, off the attempt's row ([Who runs a check](gitlet.md#who-runs-a-check)). A `container` box goes only with its container, one a failed start may have made included (created and never started, or started as the runtime's command was cut off): where `rm -f` fails and the runtime still lists the container, or cannot say, the box keeps its directory and record, and its reclaimer tries again on its next pass. **A box that records neither** (one whose record could not be written) **is reaped on the next create, but only when genuinely orphaned.** Two questions are asked. *Is anything running in it?* A live process group that is still the box's own job (`direct`) or an existing container, read from the operating system. *Has anything touched it?* Whatever drives the box refreshes a keepalive stamp (`Sandbox.Touch`): the completion poll on every poll, and a launch on a box still provisioning, which has no job yet. Such a box is reaped only when both say no: nothing running, and nothing touched it for a whole `host_grace_seconds`. A reaped box still gives back any login the run refreshed before it was abandoned.

**A pid is not an identity.** A `direct` box records its job's process group as the leader's pid *with the leader's start time*, read from the kernel's process record (`/proc/<pid>/stat` with the boot id on Linux, `sysctl kern.proc.pid` on macOS) while the engine holds the unreaped process. Every later act on that record first asks whether the group is still that one, since the kernel reuses pids. A recorded group that is gone or now belongs to a later process keeps no box alive and receives no signal, so a teardown, kill or clarification pause never reaches a stranger's tree. When the kernel's record cannot be read, the reaper keeps the directory and a signal is withheld and logged (`local_sandbox_signal_withheld`).

**Only `container` isolates the host.** In `direct` the harness runs fully permissioned as the engine user, reading what that user can read and reaching what its credentials reach. That is `direct`'s bargain, right on a dedicated host you will hand to an autonomous agent and for a first run on your own machine while its seats take work from you alone, but not a boundary around the host. **For any other instance, a workstation included, and before a seat takes work from anyone else, run code work in `container`**, with [an image of your own](#bring-your-own-image), and keep `direct` for the entry that needs the host itself. Give a `providers.llm` entry `run_in: container` and every executor run launched on it runs there, or point the whole company at it with `default_run_in`:

```yaml
providers:
  sandbox:
    local:
      image: registry.example.com/coding:1   # must have the harness installed:
                                             #   see "Bring your own image" below
      runtime: auto                          # auto | docker | podman
      network: ""                            # "none" cuts the box off entirely —
                                             #   including from its own LLM
      run_args: ["--cpus", "2", "--memory", "4g"]
    default_run_in: container
```

A `local.network` you set has to reach the engine host too: `none` cuts the box off from its [tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box) and so from every tool of its seat.

The box directory is bind-mounted at `/home/user`, one fixed home a setup step, an image and a brief can name before any box exists. The container is started with `--init` so a finished detached job is reaped, not left as a zombie the completion probe would read as *still running*.
