The turn's end waits for a standby as for a capture still being kept, and for as long as its takeover and its keep can take, from the moment the end first sees it: the standby's window from its own instant (its take's rest, its wait, and the changes and the last read of the record around its takeover, about two hours and thirty-one and a half minutes) and then its takeover's own life, each followed by one more read of the record, about three hours and fifty-one and a half minutes in all at the bounds. It counts from first sight, never from its own start, since a read admitted on another node's host before a stop can take the job's session and stand by after the end began; it once waited one span from its own start and recorded the end ahead of the standby's keep. A standby that cannot keep what it took — its own spool failed, its node is stopping — withdraws, and one whose taker lease has lapsed is withdrawn by the wait, as a begun capture whose taker stopped is settled (below). A standby or a takeover the coordination store took and never answered is settled rather than left on the record with nothing keeping it: the read goes on as one that may stand, and its keep reads the record before it keeps anything. One read stands by for a place at a time: a third read of the same job at once stands down. On a version without it, a standby is dropped by that version's own stamp of the capture and not waited for, and the session is left to the read that holds the place, as before.

**A capture whose taker stopped is settled, not waited out.** A take dies with its engine process, leaving its place stamped begun and its spool on that process's disk; read by its age alone, such a capture would hold the turn's end for the whole hour and more a capture can live, and a relaunch that followed it for its fifteen seconds before it went on without it beside a record the executor log may well have taken. So every engine process holds a **taker lease** of its own in the [coordination store](coordination.md#the-three-valued-answer) — claimed as its sandbox coordinator starts, named by its incarnation (`<node>:<uuid>`) so a restarted process never waits on its predecessor's, for the seat lease TTL (`coordination.lease_ttl_seconds`, 45 seconds by default, and never past the three hours the store keeps a lease outside seats and presence), renewed four times a TTL (every 11.25 seconds by default), **held through a drain** until its last keep has ended, then released; a process that dies leaves it to lapse on its TTL. Every stamp names that lease: its holder and its fencing token (`taker`, `taker_epoch`), read again right before the take reserves its place, so a lease claimed afresh while the session was packed is the one named. A wait for a capture — the turn's end's and a relaunch's — asks whether the lease still holds at that token, one coordination read, and a store that cannot answer is never a taker gone. Where it has **lapsed or moved to another epoch**, the capture is read off the turn's row on the executor log at `linearizable`, which has seen every record the log took before the read: **landed** where the row names its place, stamped from the row and kept; **refused** where it does not — "its taker `<node>` stopped before it was kept" — which the turn's end then names. That settle is written only over the begun stamp it was read from, so a stamp the taker wrote meanwhile stands: an unresolved one, whose record was sent and may yet land, is asked again under its own operation rather than refused. **A capture the log took is settled landed whatever its taker's lease:** a host whose coordination store answers its leases and not its runs, the two being other streams, keeps its taker lease while no stamp of its own reaches the run's record, so a wait also reads the turn's row for a begun capture whose taker still holds its lease, or whose lease the store cannot say of, and stamps it landed where the row names its place, never refused, since a taker not read gone may still send its record: the turn's end at most once every 30 seconds of its wait, and a relaunch once, for a capture of the job it follows however long ago it began, after its fifteen-second wait has run out, in a read held to fifteen seconds more; and a read standing by for it once, when it has stood begun past the time a capture can take, in a read held to the standby's own wait, and once more where that wait runs out first, in a read held to one change of the record, each before the standby takes the place after it. So the turn's end goes on once the log names such a capture rather than waiting out its half hour, a standby does not upload the session a second time beside it, and a job lost with such a host (`launch_node_store_silent`) is relaunched from the capture the log took. The keep is **fenced**: it checks its own lease before its upload and again before every attempt at its record, from its own renewals rather than a store read — held at the token its stamp names, inside the window its last confirmed renewal covers, three quarters of the TTL, which closes a renewal interval before any peer can read the lease lapsed — and **every attempt at the record is cut at that window's end**. One renewal the store does not answer costs a keep nothing: the next is still asked inside the window, with an interval to answer in. A keep its lease no longer covers uploads and records nothing more, stamps the capture refused — or unresolved where a record of it was already sent and not answered, which the turn's end and a relaunch ask again — and says so (`executor_session_fenced`, and `executor_session_not_kept` as every capture not kept does). What the fence cannot reach is a record the taker had already handed on — to a data node, or to its connection's buffer while the broker was unreachable — that the log takes only after a peer has read the turn's row: on the turn's end the log orders the two itself (a record it took before the end is kept, one after it is refused by the end's tombstone). **That is decided, and nothing is recorded on the log for it:** a refusal ordered there, as the end's tombstone is, would have the log refuse the late capture and lose a session, and no session history is given up for a stamp. So a late capture the log takes before the turn's end is kept and read as any other — the turn's row names it, a session read and the conversation's next turn take it — and one decision alone takes the stamp's word over the log's: the relaunch that follows the job whose capture was settled, which continues only what the run's record keeps, and the record never takes a refusal back, so every attempt at it starts without that capture — the one whose wait settled it and one asked again after the record landed alike — and a seat's [sessions read](../reference/api-endpoints.md#executor-sessions) says of that relaunch that the log keeps the capture, not that it was not kept, as the relaunch's own reason does, which reads the turn's row for a capture its record refused — and the run that relaunch starts is told the turn's own session is there to read with `read_session`. Nothing else does: the end names it unkept at the row's own place, which releases nothing, and every account of how the turn ended (the sessions read's, the seat's own `list_sessions` and `read_session`, and the one the conversation's next turn is told) says a session was not kept only where that capture is newer than the row's own place. The end, decided off the run's record, also says the turn [went on past](turn-engine.md#how-a-turn-ends-on-the-executor-log) the session its row names; so where that capture is the turn's **last word** — the final capture of its last launch that ran a job — it names it so (`last_word`), and every reader holds the row's place to it: the row that holds it is read as all the turn did, as one whose final capture landed is, so no account says the turn went on past it and the conversation's next turn is led through that turn. That holds whichever side of the end's decision the late record landed on, since the log took it before the end either way. That relaunch starts without it, as one whose job kept nothing before a slow keep does ([below](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)): in the session the turn's first launch was handed, where the turn has kept nothing and its row still held that session when the relaunch read it — the late record landing only after — and otherwise in a session of its own, or the one its job's box holds where it carries the run on there. Beside an older capture its job kept, which a relaunch past a slow keep continues, it starts without that one too: the turn's row names the newer capture, and a relaunch restores only the session the row names. The lease is not the node's presence, which answers another question: a draining node gives presence up at its first step while its keeps still upload, and a turn's end that read its captures as refused for that would tombstone the turn before the draining node's records landed, losing the turn's last session. So a stopped taker's capture is settled within one lease TTL of its last renewal — a crash, a restart, a scale-down, a lost VM — and a draining one's is waited for until it lands. A process that holds no taker lease — its claim unanswered, or its renewals unanswered past their window — begins no capture at all. A stamp that names no taker, which only a coordinator built with no taker lease writes (a test's: every engine holds one), is waited for by its age alone.

**A capture's age is read on every clock within twice their skew.** A stamp's instant (`at`, `standby_at`) is its taker's clock's, and each node reads its age on its own; the engine holds every machine within an hour of the fleet's clock ([`clock_skew`](../reference/alarms.md)), so any two within two. So a node reads a begun capture as still being kept until its life and two hours have passed (about three hours and eleven minutes at the bounds), and a read standing by as standing until its window and two hours have, about four hours and thirty-one and a half minutes; a reader whose clock stands ahead never releases a capture before its life ends. The waits do not hold that long on a reader's word: a read standing by waits on its own clock for the capture's whole life, and a turn's end holds each capture for its life, and each standby for its window and its takeover's life, from the moment it first sees it, on its own clock, and then reads the record once more and decides on that read, since its last read inside a bound could come before a takeover that lands in the bound's last instants. A capture held past its life is one whose taker stopped or whose stamp never reached the record; a store answering at an ordinary pace settles every capture in seconds.

**How long a read waits.** A collection on another node asks the box's host to read it ([below](#durability-completion-and-observability)), and the session is taken inside that read, before the box is paused: so the asker waits for the read's own minute **and** what a take may cost — a half minute for the read of the run's record the capture is placed by, made before the take's own eight minutes begin, and the four minutes that read's reply, carrying the record whole, takes to cross a link at the slowest pace allowed, two minutes for the pack and six for the scrub, a half minute for the reservation of the capture's place, a half minute for the take's own record, the stamp of what came of it or the digest it leaves in the box, another for how a collection's job's harness ended, and another for the read's pause and its answer — **and the crossing of each change of the run's record the host's read makes**, since every change reads and writes the record whole: the reservation, the stamp of what came of the take, how the job's harness ended and the pause's record, each given the thirteen minutes a change of a record at its bound takes across a link at the slowest pace allowed, since the asker cannot know which link the host is on. The asker's wait crosses with the request, and the host's read is given three quarters of it from the moment the request reaches the host, by the host's own clock: about ninety minutes in all (60 s + (480 s + 2 × 30 s + 240 s + 90 s + 4 × 780 s) / 0.75) for the collection of a turn with no wall-clock cap; a host whose store is in its own process, or on a link of any ordinary speed, answers in seconds, and only a node that asks another node's host waits on it at all. A Claude Code or an OpenCode collection's asker waits 36 s more, for the read of its job's main thread (an OpenCode job's, the export its script left), made once on the box's host within 27 s before the take ([What a continued session is told](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)): about 5,416 s, ninety minutes (60 s + (480 s + 2 × 30 s + 240 s + 90 s + 4 × 780 s + 27 s) / 0.75), for a turn with no cap, and about a hundred and eleven and a half minutes with one; a stop's and a loss's wait as stated here, unless the run holds a note a hook served its job: then a Claude Code read waits too for its job's session's verdict on that note (the thread's read, ten seconds and one more change of the record), about a hundred and eight minutes for a collection of a turn with no cap, a hundred and twenty-nine with one, and a hundred and eleven for a stop's or a loss's read. A stop's or a loss's read ends the job before it takes the session ([above](#each-launchs-session-kept)), and so does the collection of a job its turn's cap passed while it still ran, so their asker waits for that end on top — its 2¼-minute wait and the kill's ten seconds, counted at the same three-quarter share — about ninety-three minutes in all for a stop's or a loss's read, and about a hundred and eleven for a collection's, whose host records that the cap ended a job it saw working, one more change of the record and a teardown's grace for it (60 s + (145 s + 30 s + 480 s + 2 × 30 s + 240 s + 90 s + 5 × 780 s) / 0.75), which leaves the host's take its whole eight minutes after an end and its record at their bounds. Every collection of a turn with a cap waits the hundred and twelve and a quarter, whether or not the cap has passed on the asking node's clock: the host decides on its own, as it reads. A session of a day's work is a mebibyte or two and is taken in seconds; the bound is what a host that has truly stopped costs before its claim is handed back. The upload and the record — up to about twenty-five minutes for a session at its bound at the object store's slowest accepted pace, and the keep's two reads of the coordination store before it, held to thirty seconds each, twenty-six in all — are the keep's, made off the read from the moment its take has spooled the session. A stop's read and a loss's ending take the session off the frame that decided them, in the ending's own retry — the pause watch that decided a stop, and the seat's acquisition that found a loss, go on to the next run at once. **The seat's next turn does wait**: its mail is held behind every ending kept for its retry, through the job's end and the take — up to the read's hundred and twelve and a quarter minutes (a Claude Code collection's hundred and thirteen, a stop's ninety-four and a quarter, an uncapped turn's collection's ninety-one), or a hundred and thirty and a half where a hook served the job a note (a stop's or a loss's hundred and twelve and a half), where the box's host is silent, and for a stop asked again until the host has been silent for the host grace by the asking node's own clock — at the earliest when the ask that finds it so returns, one stop's read — or the stop is the host grace and two hours old by that node's clock — and through the end's wait for the turn's captures to land, up to the hour and eleven minutes a capture can live from the moment the end first sees it and one more read of the record, an hour and fifteen and a half minutes in all — about three hours and fifty-one and a half minutes where a read stands by for one that does not land, through its takeover and its keep — or for a capture whose taker stopped its lease's TTL and one read of the executor log (above) — since the turn's end is recorded only after them and the conversation's next turn only after its end.

**The switch.** `turn_engine.conversation_session.enabled: false` keeps no session — nothing is taken out of a box or stamped, no launch seals what it handed its box for a scrub, no node asks another's host to read a lost run's box for one, and a relaunch continues at most the session its own box holds, never a capture kept while the switch was on, which a seat's sessions say too; and no turn reads its conversation, is told how its earlier turns ended or continues the session its last turn left — and still records how each turn ended, which is the turn's account and not its session ([Turn Engine](turn-engine.md#how-a-turn-ends-on-the-executor-log)); and a person's stop still ends the job before its box goes, in the stop's own retry, and a collection past its turn's cap still ends a job still working before it collects it, since that is how a stop and a cap end a job rather than anything kept. Whether to prepare a capture is read off the revision each node runs; whether to keep one, off the revision the fleet runs; whether to continue one, off the revision the relaunching node runs, as a capture is prepared.

### A session's spools on its node

Each engine process spools into a directory of its own under the node's temporary directory (`crewlet-sessions-…`), holding a lock on it while the process lives. Every start and every take removes each other process's directory whose lock it can take, since the kernel drops a lock when its process ends however it ends: what a crash left goes with the next process to start, a container restart that keeps `/tmp` and a crash loop included, and nothing a live process spools is touched.

**Every spool of a process shares one room**: a take's room for each of the four saves a node takes at once and one more, `(maxConcurrentSaves + 1) × takeRoomBytes`, 481.17 MiB, held per engine process, so two engines on one host hold one each. A take's room is two parts of one size, a sealed session at its bound (`SealedMaxBytes`) with as much as gzip adds to input it cannot shrink and to the scrub spool's members, 96.23 MiB in all: its sealed spool takes its part first, and its scrub's spool, which the scrub writes at the kept archive's level, the rest, so a scrub's spool never makes a seal fail, and one that would pass its part refuses the take. A save takes a take's room before its pack and never waits for it: with none free it is due again, so saves hold at most four takes' room and a final take always finds the fifth. A final take, a standby's included, takes its room before anything else it holds, in a save's order (room, then the node's pack slot, then the take's own scrub slots), so no take waits for room holding what a save holding room waits for; once its pack is done its sealed spool's part gives back all but its archive's counted size, and its scrub's part goes back as the scrub's spool is read back and removed, before the take's stream ends. It waits at most a minute: room comes back as other takes' packs and uploads end, seconds for a session at its bound on a working store, so a minute without it is a store near its floor pace. Past the minute the take keeps nothing, stamps its capture refused as `no_spool_room` (so the turn's end names it, and says the turn went on past the session its row names), logs `executor_session_not_kept` at warning naming the room, and the turn's next launch continues its newest kept capture and says why ([When a run does not continue its session](conversation-sessions.md#when-a-run-does-not-continue-its-session)); a standby logs it at info and stamps nothing, since the read it stands by for still holds the capture's place. The line carries `waited_seconds`, `bytes` (the room asked for), `room_bytes` and `others_held_bytes` (what other spools held as it gave up); every final take's wait is recorded in `crewlet.executor.spool.wait` by `outcome` (`taken`, `refused`, `ended`), and the room held in `crewlet.executor.spool.held_bytes` ([Metrics](../reference/metrics.md)). The room and the minute are engine constants, not settings: a rising `refused` count is one to report with both readings, which say which of the two to retune. A seal is refused before it writes past its room, so the disk never holds more than the room. Three costs follow. A standby's spool holds its room for up to its wait (`standbyWait`), so five standbys at the bound on one node hold final takes off that long. A final take holds the bound's room through its pack, so beside four saves a node packs one final take at a time, and one queued behind other takes' packs for a minute keeps nothing. And the room is fixed, so it refuses a final take at the bound beside four others that a pod's disk (10Gi on the operator's default) would hold.

### A running job's session, saved as it works

A job can work for hours, and a box lost with its host, or a `direct` job that went with the container, unit or host its engine ran in, leaves nothing to read. So **the node driving a running job's box saves its session as it works**: what the harness has written so far, taken as a capture of its own, cut off and not final, which the turn's row names once it lands. A relaunch of a job lost with its box then continues its newest save rather than an older session or none, told that its run went on past it ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). An OpenCode run's save is the session's export, made by a private OpenCode process (`--standalone`) beside the run's own server, whose address and password the run's script alone holds: it holds the session's settled messages, never the step in flight, whose calls lie past the save's point; it is refused before its gzip where it is empty or past the quarter of a gibibyte the scrub reads; and it is made only on the release its saves were measured on (2.3.2), a save of any other refused before its pack.

**The poll offers it.** The waiter that keeps a box alive, its launching node's, already polls it every interval, so every box a poll finds running within its turn's cap is offered for a save. Nothing else starts one: a call through the bridge, a clock in the box's script or a signal would each be a second way into the box, beside its waiter. The offer decides from the node's memory and never waits, since the poll is the box's keepalive: the run's harness saves, the node is not draining, no save of the turn is under way on the node, the save is due, and one of the node's **four save slots** is free, taken without waiting (the next poll offers again). The save runs as a task of its own and holds its slot until its upload ends, so the four bound the packs, the scrubs, the spools on the node's disk, inside the room every spool shares ([above](#a-sessions-spools-on-its-node)), and the uploads together. A job's final captures take no slot.

**When it is due.** [`save_interval_seconds`](conversation-sessions.md#configuration) after the node's last attempt (600 s by default, 300 to 3600), counted on that node's clock alone, and only once the job moved: its harness's event stream, read by its size alone, grew since the node's last landed save, so a job waiting on one long command is not saved again. A save that failed is tried again after twice the wait, doubling up to the larger of the interval and an hour; one that found something it needs missing for now (the box, the license, the taker lease, its place, its box's room to pack it) waits one interval without doubling; a landing starts again from the interval. A node that first sees a running job after it restarts counts from the later of the launch's start and that launch's newest capture, instants other machines stamped, clamped into the last interval: its first save there falls due within one interval of first sight, whatever any clock says, and is paced by size as any other.

**The box only while its waiter runs.** The attach, the read of the stream and the pack end with the waiter's life, so the coordinator's stop or a drain's end cuts a save there, and a save cut before its place stamps nothing and is removed from its box. Past the pack the save is the node's, as every take is: its take's budget starts then, and the values its scrub takes out are read then, so a token the poll renewed while the pack ran is scrubbed too.

**Cheapest first, on one read of the row.** Before it packs, a save reads the run's row once, settles a save of the turn whose taker is gone or whose record went unanswered ([settled, not waited out](#each-launchs-session-kept)), and is held to the license a save's place is reserved under: the run running, the save of its current launch, nothing of the job's end read and nothing of the turn that may still land. Its place is after the row's newest capture, placed as a cut-off capture is (above), and a relaunch that continues it is told every call past its point but those a reading of its archive finds it holding. The place, the cursor and what raises the save point all come from that one read, so a capture placed since refuses the save, and a final take never loses its place to one.

**Each seat's saves have an allowance.** The object store keeps a superseded save's object until the collector deletes it, a day and more, so `max_bytes_per_seat` is also the allowance of the seat's saves, and a seat holds up to twice it. Each save is charged before its stamp, in the seat's ledger in the coordination store's uploads bucket, which the whole company agrees on: written by compare-and-set, counted at the packed archive sealed with an eighth or 64 KiB more for what the scrub changes, keyed so an answer lost and asked again counts once, and held 29 h 2.5 min (the take's life before its object is stored, the collector's grace and two of its passes, and twice the clocks' assumed skew, since another node's clock reads the entry's end). A crash or a lost answer can only over-count, and a spool that seals past what was counted is refused before its upload. A seat with no room takes no save until entries lapse.

**Paced by size.** Spent at the interval, a large session's saves would fill the allowance in hours, so a seat's saves are spaced by the hold times the expected size over the room left, the expected size this launch's last save's, or before its first the kept session the launch continued: at the defaults, with the seat's allowance free, the interval holds until a save is about 0.4 MiB sealed, and past that a session is saved about every 27 minutes per sealed MiB (1 MiB every 27 minutes, 3 MiB every 81), and about every 54 once the seat has saved for longer than the hold and its room settles near half. A session growing 1.2 to 1.8 MiB sealed an hour is saved about every 0.54 to 0.81 times its age, 1.1 to 1.6 in a busy seat: what a run lost then does again, which its line reports (`since_save_s`). So a relaunch continuing a 2 MiB kept session first saves it about 54 minutes in rather than at the interval, and one lost before then continues that kept copy. A first save that no kept session sizes (the box's own copy, the conversation's base, a session of the run's own) is packed at the interval and paced again at what the pack measured, before its charge: too large for the room, it is released from the box uncharged, and the size it measured paces the next save before its pack. Releasing a superseded save's object at once is the root fix, [crewlet/crewlet#1469](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/issues/1469).

**As its node drains.** The stop a drain comes before usually takes a `direct` job with it (its container, its unit or its host), so a draining node saves each `direct` job it launched whose session moved since its last save there, beside its wait for turns, most stale first under the same slots, for at most 30 s from the drain's start; a save of the turn already under way counts. Not a `container` job, which outlives the engine and dies only with its host. A drain save is charged, never paced; from the drain's first instant no poll starts a save; and its pack takes the job's files as they stand, or an OpenCode session's settled messages, one pack after another. A save the 30 s cut is stamped refused where it had taken its place, and the run keeps its newest periodic save. The drain returns once each save it began has passed its spool and its upload is counted among those the stop waits for, saying so while it waits (`executor_session_saves_draining`), and their uploads end with the coordinator's stop ([Graceful shutdown](agent-runtime.md#graceful-shutdown)).

**What it costs.** Per due offer, an attach of the box and one read of the stream's size, then the pack; a due job whose stream has not moved is checked so again at every poll, every 15 s, until it moves. An OpenCode save's pack is a process of its own beside the run's server, about 90 MiB for about half a second on an ordinary session; at its peak it holds about four and a half times the box's OpenCode database plus 90 MiB, and up to about ten times once the session holds a character past Latin-1, as most do (a dash past ASCII, a curly quote, an emoji). So a node packs one session at a time in a box that shares its memory (a `direct` box), a save's or a take's, and a save waits one interval, never doubled, while its box lacks twelve times that database and its WAL plus 128 MiB; a final pack checks no room, since refused it would lose the job's newest state. In the coordination store, one read of the row (and a settle where one is owed), two reads of the seat's ledger (its room, then the read its compare-and-swap writes over) and one write (52 KiB at its cap of 512 entries, within the 64 KiB a save ledger may be), two reads of what the box was handed (before the pack, and for the scrub's values after it), the reservation and the outcome on the run's row, and the keep's own reads. On the executor log, one capture record of about a kibibyte, which its census counts. In the object store, one upload, held a day by the collector within the allowance.

**What it logs.** `executor_session_saved` (info) on each landing, with `point` (`save` or `drain_save`), `late_s` (from due to start), `took_s`, `counted` and `bytes` (what the ledger counted, and what was kept), beside the keep's `executor_session_kept`; `executor_session_save_deferred` (debug) for a save not taken now, with its `class` and `why`; and `executor_session_not_kept`, `point` `save` or `drain_save`, for one that failed before its place or found its box without the room to pack it, or a seat whose save ledger a newer build owns, which takes no save until that build's ledger ages out, at warning the first time for a launch and a kind and at debug after, with `failures` and `next_due_s`. A save that fails past its place is logged as every capture is.

**What a reader is told.** A save is a capture like any other: a reader of a turn still running whose row now names a newer capture than the one read is told its runs have kept its session again, never that a run saved it, since a reader of the row reads no run record ([A seat reads its own](#a-seat-reads-its-own)).


## A relaunch continues the turn's session

Every relaunch of a turn — a reviewer's send-back, a person's answer carrying a parked run on, a round whose job was [lost with its host](#durability-completion-and-observability), a round refused on a sign-in replaced while it ran — **continues the turn's own session** where it can, in whatever box and cell the launch gets: the box the session was last worked in, or any other. What it continues is **the session of the job it follows** — the job its reviewer collected, the one whose question was answered, the one lost or refused — as that job's kept capture holds it ([above](#each-launchs-session-kept)), named by the turn's row of the executor log, read through the estate router at `linearizable` so a capture another node's keep recorded is seen, and opened against that row alone: the seat's and the turn's own session, never another turn's of the same conversation, whatever ended since. A turn that has kept no session of its own yet continues the one its first launch was handed instead, and a conversation's next turn continues the one its last turn left ([below](#a-conversations-next-turn-continues-its-last-turns-session)).

**Which session, and when none.** Only the job before's session holds everything the turn's jobs were told — the round's task, or the review that sent it back; a person's answer; the job's own work — so a relaunch continues the newest capture of that job that was **kept**, and nothing of an earlier job: a capture an earlier job took holds none of what the jobs after it were told. It continues it past newer captures of that job that will not be kept (refused, begun longer ago than a capture can take, or sent and never answered past the window a record may name it in), and past one still being kept, or whose record still awaits its answer, once its wait for that one (below) has run out: it waits for that one and asks it first, and continues it where it lands. The run is told every call of the round after the save point of the capture it continues, but those a reading of a cut-off capture's archive finds it holding (below), so it never takes itself to know what a newer capture held. The job's capture is taken by the read that collected it and kept off that read, so a relaunch that follows at once waits for the keep — for about as long as an ordinary keep takes, fifteen seconds, and no longer: the frame that waits holds the seat and a slot of the node's admission, and a keep still under way past that is a slow store's or a stopped node's, which it does not wait out. It waits only for a keep its decision depends on: that job's, and an earlier job's only while the turn has kept no session, since once one lands the session its first launch was handed is no longer continued (below); beside a session the turn kept, an earlier job's keep changes nothing a relaunch decides, and it decides at once. Within that wait, what is unsettled is settled before the relaunch decides: a capture whose taker's lease has lapsed is settled from the turn's row on the log ([above](#each-launchs-session-kept)), so a relaunch that follows its taker's crash or restart continues the capture that process landed, where the log took its record before that read, rather than starting fresh beside it (one the log takes only after that read is kept on the log, and the relaunch starts without it); once the wait has run out, a capture of the job it follows whose taker still holds its lease, or whose lease the store cannot say of, however long ago it began, is settled landed where the turn's row names it, and continued, in one read of its own held to fifteen seconds more, while one the log has not taken is still being kept, and passed over for the capture that job kept before it, where it kept one, which the relaunch says as `capture_late`, continuing an older capture ([When a run does not continue its session](conversation-sessions.md#when-a-run-does-not-continue-its-session)); and a capture whose record was never answered is asked again under its own operation, as the turn's end asks it, and continued where it lands. The wait bounds the waiting and every read and ask it makes, never what it settles: each settle is the node's own write to the run's record, given a record's thirty seconds and the row's crossing past the wait, as every stamp is, so a store slow to take one leaves the capture settled rather than read as still being kept, and the relaunch's frame can run that much past its fifteen seconds only where the store is that slow; an ask the log leaves unanswered writes nothing, since the record already says so. So a relaunch continues no kept session where the job it follows kept none: its box went with its host, its take or its keep was refused, its record was never answered, or its keep was still under way when the wait ran out, with none kept before it. It then continues, where the turn has kept no session at all, the session its first launch was handed — the one its conversation's last turn left, frozen on the run's record and held on the executor log, never read again — in a box of its own; else, as it always could, the session the job's own box holds, where a person's answer or a replaced sign-in carries the run on in the box it parked in; and starts fresh anywhere else. A keep still under way when the wait runs out is no kept capture, and, where the job kept none before it, goes that way too: the session its first launch was handed, where the turn has kept nothing and its row still holds it, since that holds everything a session of its own would and the conversation besides. Should that capture land after the relaunch read the row, the relaunch's own first capture supersedes it, as any newer capture does, and what that job did is lost to the relaunch whichever session it started in. A newer capture that lands after the relaunch chose an older one but before its launch makes the launch's own check refuse the older one, whose briefs were written for it: the run starts a session of its own, or continues its box's copy where it carries the run on there, and the line says so. And a kept session is continued only:

- by a runner that restores it: the harness that wrote it, in the archive format this build restores, written by a release whose sessions another box continues — and in a box whose harness can take it up, which the launch asks the box before it chooses the run's brief (Claude Code 2.1.310 or later, never older than the release that wrote it; OpenCode 2.3.2, Codex 0.171.0, Gemini CLI 0.70.0, Qwen Code 0.28.4, Copilot 1.0.114, Muse Code 1.4.25, Kimi Code 2.7.2, Hermes Agent 0.23.3, Pi 1.6.0 and Grok Build 1.0.92 exactly, box and writer alike; [Claude Code](#a-claude-code-runs-session), [OpenCode](#an-opencode-runs-session), [Codex](#a-codex-runs-session), [Gemini CLI](#gemini-cli), [Qwen Code](#qwen-code), [Copilot](#github-copilot-cli), [Muse Code](#a-muse-code-runs-session), [Kimi Code](#a-kimi-code-runs-session), [Hermes Agent](#a-hermes-agent-runs-session), [Pi](#pi), [Grok Build](#grok-build)). The box a job parked in, continuing its own copy, is asked its release only where a hook's read is at stake (below), which is how the engine learns the release that holds that copy: every Claude Code run pins `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, in the wrapper and in its settings over a repository's own, so a box's release never changes under the session it holds, and the release that wrote that copy is the one that answers and continues it. A Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Muse Code, Kimi Code, Pi or Grok Build box is asked its release before it continues its own copy, which it does only on its harness's one supported release and only where the record of its last run names that release as the copy's writer, so a box downgraded since a newer release wrote its copy starts a session of its own;
- under the `providers.llm` entry it ran under: the entry's identity is built from the entry's route and sign-in mode only (its key, auth mode, the profile's `identity_env` and `sign_in_env` switches as its `env` sets them, each address cleaned to its scheme, host, port and path, and, for OpenCode, the provider its `model` names; [a value that is no route is refused](llm-backends.md#profile-fields)), since a harness may keep what a session was created with. A replaced credential keeps the entry; a box's own routing is outside it. The identity is keyed by the fleet's entry key, derived from its keyring ([a keyring rotation starts these sessions afresh once](llm-backends.md#a-limit-is-the-sign-ins)). The exception is a harness measured on its newest release to send a resumed session's calls on its launch's route: Claude Code (2.1.310 and 2.1.330), Codex 0.171.0 (whose runs all use its built-in provider, a run's configuration naming none), OpenCode 2.3.2, Gemini CLI 0.70.0, Qwen Code 0.28.4 and Pi 1.6.0 continue a session under any entry of the chain; Copilot, Grok Build, Muse Code, Kimi Code and Hermes Agent continue one only under its own. The same holds for the session the turn's first launch was handed and the copy a job's own box holds;
- where the seat's budget can carry it: a session whose launch would need more than the most room the seat's or the company's capped windows can leave it, each ceiling less what the launch's own turn spent there first (its context with the brief that continues it, or, where nothing measured its context, `turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens` with that brief beside it: [What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)) is not continued, which the launch decides once that brief is written; a seat with no capped window continues a session of any size;
- and once per lost round: a round whose job is lost a second time starts a session of its own, rather than replay the state it was lost in toward the round's limit.

A session a job of the turn [ran out of context](conversation-sessions.md#a-session-that-ran-out-of-context-is-retired) in is continued by no relaunch, whichever copy it would be: its kept capture, the session the turn's first launch was handed, or the one its box holds. The relaunch starts a session of its own, and that job's collection takes no capture of the session that ran out.

A relaunch that continues no kept session of the turn's own continues the session its first launch was handed where the turn has kept none, or the session its box holds where it could before, as above — each only where the seat's budget can carry it with the brief that continues it ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)), the box's copy being the same session, as large or larger — and otherwise starts a session of its own, with the brief written for one. In its job's own box, where a person's answer or a replaced sign-in offers the launch that box's copy of the session, it continues the copy rather than restore over it a kept capture taken while that job still worked: the copy is the same session, which went on past that capture, so it holds everything the capture does and all the job did after it, where the capture would roll the session back. A capture taken once its job had ended holds that job's whole session, and is continued there as anywhere. Each reason is logged as `executor_session_not_continued` once what the launch continues instead is decided, its `outcome` naming that — the session the box holds, or a session of its own — and it is **never a failed launch**. A relaunch that continues the capture its job kept past a newer one logs the same line once, naming each newer capture it went past and saying whether that one was not kept, and why, or may still be kept, and how, its `outcome` the capture it continues instead.

**Read whole before it is carried, and spooled nowhere.** The session is read from the [object store](object-store.md) and its seal opened whole once before a byte of it reaches the box, so an object the store no longer holds, or one whose seal does not open, is found before the run's brief is chosen rather than part way through writing the archive into the box. It is then read again, streamed into the box as the run starts and held to the first read: its last byte reaches the box only once the whole matches, so a store that answers otherwise the second time fails the run's start, which the turn retries, and nothing in the box is restored from it. Nothing of it is spooled on the node's disk ([the spool room](#a-sessions-spools-on-its-node)). A box that already holds the archive keeps its own copy, by the digest it keeps ([Claude Code](#a-claude-code-runs-session)); where the job before ran in this very box and its harness exited cleanly, nothing is fetched at all.

**A session its harness was cut off in** — every capture of a lost job, whatever packed it; every one the engine packed rather than the run's script: a job that died before its script could pack, or one still working that its box would not end; every one the script packed after a harness that did not exit cleanly, killed by a signal or its memory limit while its wrapper lived on; and every one the script packed on its way out of an end a stop, a loss or its turn's cap asked of its job (`job-ended`), its harness told to stop mid-step — **replaces the box's own copy**, which may end in what its harness never finished, and the run is told its session may end mid-call. **Its save point is not the calls the run's log had taken before the pack** either: a harness killed while a message streamed never wrote the calls it had made and had answered, one told to stop was measured recording the call it was cut off in only with that call's message already written, and a loss's read cannot say how its job went — so such a capture is placed as one of a job still working is ([Each launch's session, kept](#each-launchs-session-kept)), at the round's start, raised after its take (above), and a run that continues it is told every call of its round past that point, but those a reading of its archive finds it holding (below) — and every note the turn has read, as notes it may already show, since such a session may lack its job's last serve of the notes and is not known to hold its job's brief, which told the notes the session it continued lacked (below). Each harness takes such a session up as it stands, by its own rules: Claude Code's resume (2.1.310) records an error result for a tool call the previous process died in, saying its outcome is unknown, and then "No response requested.", and the script resumes it without `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN`, which would run the cut-off turn again before the brief, and cuts back to its last whole line the transcript and every subagent's thread under its sidecar directory ([A Claude Code run's session](#a-claude-code-runs-session)); OpenCode's export holds only the messages that settled (OpenCode 2's `session/transfer.ts`), so a step that never settled is not in it.

**The copy a job's own box holds, where its harness was cut off.** A person's answer or a replaced sign-in that carries the round on in the job's own box without a kept capture of the job — where it kept none (its keep refused, or still under way when the relaunch's wait ran out, with none kept before it), where the one it kept was taken while it still worked, so the copy went on past it ([above](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)), or where the company keeps no session — continues the copy of the session that box holds, which no capture describes. That copy holds every call the job made and every note it read only where the job's harness **ended its own run**: the job over, its harness gone cleanly by itself, its script packing it. So the read that collects a job **records on the job's own record how its harness ended** (`harness_end`: `own_run`, or `cut_off` by the same line a capture's save point is drawn by — a harness killed, crashed or told to stop, or gone with any status but 0; a job ended before its harness started or one its end could not stop; a box that packed no session), whether or not it takes or keeps a capture of the session, once its take is done and within the room the read leaves the take's own records, so the record never costs the take or the box's pause their time; once recorded cut off, a later read never records it whole, and nothing is recorded over a word this build does not know. A relaunch that carries the round on in the job's box reads it, and where it does not say `own_run` — the harness was cut off, or a build before this one collected the job and recorded nothing — the copy may lack calls its harness made and had answered without writing them: Claude Code 2.1.310 makes a call, and can have it answered, before it writes the call to its transcript. Nor is the copy known to hold the job's brief: nobody has measured whether 2.1.310 writes the message a continued session is handed before it answers a call (it was measured answering a fresh session's first two calls before that session's transcript file existed, but a fresh session cut off then leaves its box nothing to continue, and the relaunch starts a session of its own), and a job that ended before its harness started leaves the session it was handed. So the session there is told, after what carries it on:

- **that it was cut off** where the record says so, and **that it may have been** where it says nothing or says it in a word this build does not know: it may end in the middle of a call, and may not show the last of what its run did — said whether or not any call follows, since the call a harness was cut off in may be one of its own tools, which the tool log never holds, and in words that speak of no save;
- **the messages its job's brief opened with**, under a header that says the session may already show them (a message shown both there and in the session being one message, sent once, the later of two that differ standing): the answer that carried the job on, a review that sent its round back, or, where the job continued the session its conversation's last turn left, where this turn began and the turn's task with the turn's answers that brief told after it, or was to tell where they could not be read, and every such message that brief told again in turn ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). A copy cut off before its harness wrote its brief holds none of them: told only to continue from where it is, the copy of a job that continued the conversation's last turn would carry that turn on.
- **every call of the round**, under the header of calls the session may not show (a call shown both there and in the session being one call, made once), with every call the round's tool log dropped from its middle counted: what the continuation of a cut-off capture placed at the round's start is told. Never only the job's own calls: a copy that lacks the job's brief lacks the calls that brief told — an earlier job's, or the call an earlier answer approved. Never the call a person approved for the answer that carries the round on, though: what carries it on says what that call returned, and a later attempt at the answer, which finds the call in the tool log, would otherwise tell it twice;
- **every note the turn has read**, under a header that counts them as notes the session may already show (a note shown both there and in the session being one note, sent once), in the order read and before the notes waiting for it, as a kept session cut off is told them: the copy is not known to hold its job's brief, and a copy that lacks it lacks the notes that brief told — the ones the session it continued lacked, an earlier job's among them — and no record says which those were.

Its skill guard holds the skills the job's launch armed, which the session held before the job began, and **none of the job's own loads**: one its harness never wrote is told as a call the copy may lack, and the skill is loaded again before a call it covers. A job whose harness ended its own run is told none of this — only what carries it on, then that a successful `submit_work` among the calls its copy holds does not stand, the reads its job's brief counted past the read cap without listing them, which its copy holds only as that count ([below](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)), every call the tool log took after the job that made it was replaced, every call nobody waited for by the time it returned ([below](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)) and every call still in flight as the round was read ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)), whose outcomes its copy is not known to hold, every note from the first read the record marks [unanswered](#notes-to-a-running-run) on, under the header of notes it may already show, since its copy lacks that note and holds the answered ones after it, and the notes waiting — and its guard holds its loads, but none any of those calls made: its copy holds every call the job made and every call the job's brief told, which is every other call of the round (a fresh run's brief carrying the round on tells every one of them), though of a call its harness gave up on only that it timed out, and of a read the brief counted without listing it only that it was made. Nothing of it is built where the job's box is gone, which no launch continues in. A read made while the run's ending is decided — a stop's, or a loss's ending — records nothing, since nothing carries that round on; a lost job whose round is carried on is read by a collection, which records it. A kept capture cut off is told the messages its job's brief opened with too, after the section that says it was cut off and before its calls; one whose harness ended its own run, like the copy of such a job, holds its brief and is told none of them.

**What that costs.** The told calls are held to the prior-work ledger's budgets as every continuation's are, and a rewrite of a long call by the seat's auxiliary model is charged before the relaunch, which is refused, launching nothing, where that rewrite fills the seat's window; the notes are told whole, as every brief tells them. The brief is the longer for every call of the round and every note the turn has read, for every copy not known to have ended its own run, which includes **every relaunch after a replaced sign-in whose refused harness exited with a status other than 0**, and every job a build before this one collected. The launch's floor ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)) counts that brief and grows with it, beside the copy's context, the larger of its job's newest capture's measure, kept or not, and what the read that collected the job found the copy's newest request carried, and beside `turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens` where neither measured it: a launch offered the turn's kept capture beside the copy is held to the larger of their floors, since its box takes up the copy only where it cannot restore the capture, and where the copy's own floor is past what the seat's windows or its model's can carry, the launch does not continue the copy (`executor_session_not_continued`) — it continues the kept capture where its own floor fits, and otherwise starts **a session of its own**, which, as every fresh run that carries a round on is, is told every call of the round, within the prior-work ledger's budgets, and, as every one after a loss, an answer or a replaced sign-in is, that what the run before it did through the seat's tools did happen, to be checked before any of it is done again: the list cannot tell what that run did outside the seat's tools, nor a call it counts past the read cap or only in the tally. Every relaunch that carries a round on builds that telling beside whatever else it offers, since its box may fall back to the fresh brief: its rewrites of long calls are charged before the relaunch, and a rewrite the continuation beside it already made is not made again, the seat's rewrites being kept by their text for the turn; and the launch's floor counts the fresh brief, the calls in it ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)).

**Four briefs, and the box picks between two.** The run's brief is chosen by whether it continues the session and where:

| The run | Its brief |
|---|---|
| Continues the session in the box it was last worked in | The session's next message: what carries it on, then what it lacks (below) |
| Continues the session restored into another box | The same, then what a new box changes: a fresh checkout — for a run offered `code_checkout`, of a repository the box's setup clones, while one the session checked out of Gitlet is not in the box until it checks it out again, at its branch's head ([Repositories on Gitlet](#repositories-on-gitlet)) — the work-in-progress branch to check out, the uncommitted work gone, and that the session's absolute paths under the earlier box's home were that box's |
| Continues the session its conversation's last turn left, in a box of its own | Where this turn begins and what a new box changes, then the turn's own brief whole — its fresh brief, or a relaunch's reseed ([below](#a-conversations-next-turn-continues-its-last-turns-session)) |
| Starts a session of its own | The turn's ask, with the ledger of its earlier rounds, every note the turn has read, every answer that carried the turn on before it (each naming its round) and what became of the run before it, and, of a round carried on, every call of the round so far — and, where a kept session it could read is not continued, that session and how to read it, never why it is not continued ([What a harness is told](#what-a-harness-is-told)) |

Whether a restore succeeds is finally the box's to find out — an archive that does not unpack, an import OpenCode refuses — so a run asked to continue a session carries **both** its continuation and the fresh brief, and its script hands its harness the one its restore came to: a new session never answers a brief written for a model that remembers. It carries both wirings of the seat's tools too, one per session its box may start, and installs the one of the session it started, which is how the box tells the bridge ([below](#which-session-the-box-started)). The launch publishes the brief it handed as the round's opening frame once it has its box, before the run starts — the started record, published before the launch knows its box, carries the fresh brief — and its `executor_collected` record says which brief it handed (`brief`), whether the run took the session up (`harness_session_continued`) and, where it did not, why (`session_not_continued`, `restore_failed` with the script's reason as its detail).

**What a continued session is told.** Not its task again in full: the session holds the task as it read it where it holds the message that told it and, where its harness ended its own run, every call it made — one it gave up on with no outcome or a failed one, though the call ran on (below) — and every note it read; one cut off may not show all of them, and is told so and told them again (below). Its brief is what it lacks:

- **What carries it on.** A send-back: that its work was reviewed and sent back; the task restated, since a compacted session holds only its own summary of it; the rules its earlier rounds' calls are read by — what already ran and must not be issued again, what may be re-run, what to cite as a delivery — without their list, which the session holds; and what the review and the engine asked of the next round. A person's answer: the question and the answer, and, where the question was a call held for a person's approval, what became of the call — made, and what it returned, or, where what it returned is recorded but cannot be read on the node carrying the run on, made and whether the tool reported a failure — which tells the call they approved once: nothing below lists it. A loss: that it was cut off, and why. A replaced sign-in: that the sign-in was replaced.
- That it may end mid-call, where its harness was cut off when it was saved — or, for the copy its job's own box holds, where that job's harness is not known to have ended its own run: said to have been cut off where its record says so, and to perhaps have been where it says nothing. A kept capture taken while its run still worked, never its job's final one, is told instead that it was saved then, when, and that the run went on after it: the session ends where it was saved, not where the run stopped, and what the run did after it beyond the calls told below (the commands it ran, the files it read or changed) is in no record, so the working tree is checked before any of it is done again.
- **The messages that carried the work on that the session may not show**, where it may lack its job's brief: a kept capture cut off, or the copy a job's own box holds where that job's harness is not known to have ended its own run. The engine keeps the turn's leads beside the run's record, in a value of their own as the tool log is, the messages its sessions were carried on with: an answer to its question (a withdrawal, a refused reply, or a call held for a person's approval with what became of it and what it returned, as the run's row sealed it), the engine's answer to a run parked on its own calls or on `wait_for_run` (each kept under a kind of its own, so a build that does not know the kind says it cannot read the message rather than tell it as a person's answer), a review that sent its round back, for a job that continued the session its conversation's last turn left, the turn's task, and, for every launch whose run may start a session of its own on its fresh brief, the task that brief opened with: a turn's first launch, a send-back, and every relaunch, whose box falls back to the fresh brief where it cannot take up the session it was handed (kept beside such a launch's own leads, and marked told only where the brief its run read was the fresh one). Each is signed once under the fleet keyring in a key domain of its own ([The keyring](secret-store.md#the-keyring-is-not-optional-and-it-does-four-jobs)) by the job whose brief first told it, and kept as signed, never signed again, while each job's record marks the ones its own brief told. Such a session is told again the ones its job's brief told, oldest first, after the section that says it was cut off and before its calls, under a header that says it may already show them, a message shown both there and in the session being one message, sent once, and the later of two that differ standing, and never why it may not show them, which the section before says in the words its record bears out; and its own brief records them as told in turn, so a continuation of its session, which may lack that brief too, tells them again. Told in words true of any session of the work, never in the form first told: an answer as one a run of this work asked and its answerer answered, a chat reply fenced under who wrote it; a held call as one a run of this work called, with what it returned, so no list of the round's calls repeats it; a review recomposed from the round it closed, as a send-back of this turn's work whose earlier calls stand whether or not the session shows them, never as "the same session", or said in its place as a review that is not kept where the turn's park has folded that round into an entry standing for the rounds it dropped, which keeps no review, never among the earlier messages not kept, since it can follow a message told before it; and the turn's task with where the turn began, saying what that brief said of the session the conversation's last turn left (where it ends, that its files were the earlier box's, that it was cut off when kept) only of a session that began as that one, since a session that may be a summary (below) is told every lead the engine keeps, another session's among them, and marks them told in turn, and only the closed rounds that brief rendered, found by their numbers, since such an entry can stand for several rounds, and such an entry whole where it runs on past them, since it holds their calls, never the new box, checkout or paths that brief spoke of, which may be stale or false of the box the session is in now, and then the turn's answers that brief told after it, or was to tell where they could not be read, in that brief's order (told with the task and never apart from it where the task is told, each once, under the oldest task told that carries it, since told apart every earlier answer would sort before the task and let the task, the later message, stand over them). **A session that may be a summary is told the task a fresh brief opened with too**: a compaction summarizes a session's opening message, which for a session its run started of its own was that task, while a session cut off, or one known to hold its job's brief, holds its opening message and is told none. It is told as the task this work was started on, with no turn boundary and nothing of a box, the closed rounds that brief rendered and the answers it told after it, nested under it as under a task. The turn's ask is told once a section: every launch keeps a fresh task, and a base continuation a task too, each rendering the ask and its closed rounds, so a summary told each would be handed them as many times as the turn launched; a task is told where one is, with where the turn began, else the newest fresh task that can be read here. An answer is kept to 16 KiB of its words, the rest counted and said, with a word that the run may ask again for it; the turn's leads are kept to 512 KiB, the oldest dropped first and counted, which the brief says too, and where they cannot be read at all, every one the record counts is said as not kept rather than left out, and the ones the job's brief told stay marked on the job the relaunch opens, so the next continuation that can read them tells them; and a lead the node building the brief cannot read, sealed under a key it does not hold, is said in its place, and kept for a node that holds the key.
- **The reads an earlier message to the session counted without listing them.** A brief tells a round's calls held to the prior-work ledger's read cap and counts the reads past it rather than listing them, so a session it was handed holds those reads only as a count: that they were made, and none of what they returned. The launch records which they were on the job it opens, by the brief its run read (the one it handed, or, where the box started a session of its own in its place, the fresh one; both where the box never said), and a capture of that job's session placed by its own read states them, so the next message to the copy in the job's box, or to that capture, tells them ahead of every other call it tells, under words that say an earlier message counted them, with how many of them the log has since dropped from its middle: a read is run again where its data is needed, never invented. The read cap is spent on them last, and the reads that message counts in turn are recorded for the next, so a session owes exactly what its newest brief left out, each told by the next brief with room for it; a brief that tells the round from its start, a fresh run's or a copy cut off's, starts the account afresh. Not across a send-back: it opens a new round, whose tool log restarts, so the reads a send-back's brief counts of the collected round are counted once, as the prior-work ledger counts a closed round's reads past its cap.
- **Every call its run made through the seat's tools that the session may not have been answered when it was saved** — every call the tool log took after the read that is the session's save point, so after the point it was saved at and any still in flight then, whose outcome it may never have been handed, however much of a long round's middle the log dropped below it — with each call's outcome, as the [prior-work ledger](turn-engine.md#prior-work-ledger-across-self_iterate-rounds) renders a round's calls and within its budgets: an argument value or a failed call's error past its budget rewritten by the seat's auxiliary model, or left out by its size and digest where no rewrite can be had, and the reads past the ledger's cap counted rather than listed, under one cap for every list the brief tells, spent on the late calls' reads (below) first, since the session never shows their outcomes and they are few, then on the reads told under a subagent's name (below), then on these, the ones of either left out counted and told by the next brief, which the session lacks, then on the reads an earlier message counted (above), since the session holds those as a count, and on the calls listed again (below) last, since the session may show each of them, so a continuation never lists more of a round's reads than the ledger's cap. They happened. Where its harness ended its own run the session does not hold them; **where it was cut off**, its save point is the newest a capture its session holds states, where its take found no compaction since, and otherwise the round's start, rather than where it ends, so the list can repeat calls the session holds: it is headed as calls the session may not show, never as calls it lacks, and a call shown both there and in the session is said to be one call, made once. **A Claude Code session cut off is read for the calls it holds**, and told only the rest: the relaunch asks, once, which of the calls it would list (never a late one, one in flight, one a person approved, nor one whose id the log does not keep or another call carries) the capture's archive holds the logged result of ([ADR-0073](../../adr/0073-a-seats-executor-session-is-a-sealed-object-its-turns-row-names.md), the reading), for the release that wrote the session, and builds a brief beside the one above that leaves out every call the reading finds held, under words that say the session may show some of the rest and that the list leaves out any it found the session holds or lists below; a call the reading finds in the thread of a subagent whose report the session does not hold is told under that subagent's name instead, in a section of its own after the list, the subagent named by its id and its description (cut to 200 characters, its whitespace collapsed, defused), a `submit_work` among its calls said not to stand. That brief counts only where its own first request sends the session whole (judged on it, as below) and its box answers the release it was read for: the launch asks the box's harness its `--version` before it chooses the brief, and hands the brief told by the reading only where it answers that release exactly, and the brief above to every other box. Each refusal falls back to the brief above, which tells more and never less, and is logged; none refuses the launch. A call the reading holds joins the calls listed again (below) where a listed call could be taken for it, and a skill it loaded is armed where the launch hands that brief and the job made it. **An OpenCode session cut off is read by what it holds.** OpenCode names no call to the engine, so the relaunch asks the same reading of the capture's kept export for each call by what the call was: the tool, its arguments as the run's record keeps them, whether it failed, and what it returned. A call is counted as one the session already shows only where every call of the round alike in all four has a result of its own there, after the place the job's run began in the session and after the session's newest compaction, exactly as OpenCode hands it to the model; only for a session OpenCode 2.3.2 wrote, measured writing and continuing the engine's calls; and the brief told by it goes only to a box of the writer's release whose first request sends the session whole. Every other call is told, in the main list, under the same words as any call the session may show. Some calls are always told, by design: a call made through Code Mode, every call to a seat's own MCP server, which OpenCode offers through its one `execute` tool so that a seat's long tool list stays out of every request (the session holds the program the model wrote and what it returned, never the call); a call a subagent made, whose session is never carried; a call whose result OpenCode cut, past 2,000 lines or 51,200 bytes, which the session marks as cut; a call whose arguments the run's record keeps only in part; a call identical to another of the round that the session does not show, an earlier job's of the round among them; every call made before the session's newest compaction, since the session holds only that compaction's summary of it; and every call, where one message of the session runs past 32 MiB, since the session is then not read. **A Qwen Code session cut off is read the same way**, only for a session Qwen Code 0.28.4 wrote, along the chain of records its own load walks, and only from where the job's run began in it: a session whose file is not that one chain in its own order, names one record's id twice, holds another release's record, is shorter than where the run began, has a line after the run's start that is not its brief, holds a record or part of a shape 0.28.4 was not measured writing, a line no record (blank, not an object, or holding a carriage return), or a step of more than 4,096 calls or a call id past 256 bytes is not read. Some calls are always told there too: a call whose result Qwen Code saved to a file, cut at its MCP limit or rewrote to keep a batch of results within its budget; a result with an image or a structured part; a failure of invalid parameters; a result Qwen Code answered in words of its own, for an empty output or a failure that sent no text; a failure whose text was blank (not measured, so never counted); a call whose arguments run past 64 KiB; a call the session holds no result of, which a resume answers with words of its own; every call made before the session's newest compression; and every call of a tool whose name another MCP server in the box could be given (a tool name opening with `_`, holding `__` or longer than 48 characters). **A Gemini CLI session cut off is read the same way**, from the lines its run's take verified, where Gemini CLI 0.70.0 wrote it and its box passed the run's guard against another server spelling the bridge's tools; what it tells by design is in [Gemini CLI](#gemini-cli). **A call the session may show that a listed call could be taken for is listed again**: one of the round the session holds, or one of the turn's earlier rounds that the brief tells nowhere else (never on a run of its own, which has no session above; never of a round the brief renders as work already done, as a task told again renders the rounds its brief rendered; never a `submit_work`, which was sent back; and never a call sealed for a person's approval of the round and tool of a held call whose answer the brief tells, which tells what became of it), where it names the same tool with arguments neither call's line tells apart (each value both lines show whole the same JSON value, a number by its value however it is spelled and a string alike the number or boolean it spells, and no key in one and not the other, a key whose value is null read as absent; a value either line rewrites or leaves out by its size reads alike whatever it was, as does a value the log left out of arguments too large to keep whole, at any depth, while the values it kept are compared; and a call's arguments read alike any wherever they are not comparable: sealed for a person's approval, in flight, left out whole by the log, recorded with no digest, as an older build's call is, or in text the engine cannot read back; results are never compared), it is listed after the list and before the late calls (below), the earlier rounds' calls first, each ending with a note that it was made in an earlier round of the turn (of the fire, in a schedule's conversation), under words that say the session may show it and that the listed one could be taken for it and is a call of its own, made as well, so a run told only that a call shown twice is one never takes the listed call for the held one and loses it. **A call the brief tells that another call it tells could be taken for ends with a note that it is a call of its own**, which another call the message tells could be taken for: a call of the other of its two lists, this one and the late calls (below), read alike as above, both then marked; a call of its tool held for a person's approval whose answer the brief tells, or the call the person approved for it, whose arguments no line shows, but never that held call itself, whose fate the answer tells; and work already done that the brief renders (a fresh brief's earlier rounds, the rounds a task told again renders), a line of it read as above, or a count of its calls by tool that names the call's tool or no tool. Never two calls of one list, which are two calls, nor a line the cap left out, and on a run of its own as well, whose late calls are each said to be one call, made once. **Where the session may show calls no list holds one by one, a section before the lists says so**, by the tools the told calls name, and that however alike one of them reads to a listed call it is a call of its own, never that one shown twice: calls of the conversation's earlier turns, where the turn continued the session its conversation's last turn left; calls of the turn's earlier rounds where the session may hold them only in a summary's words (it may be a summary now, or a Claude Code session's thread restarted at some point, before its job or in it), less the ones listed again; calls of the turn the log no longer lists one by one, where some of them may be in the session; and calls of workers the turn delegated to, which reach the session only in their reports. It is told only beside words that say a call may be shown twice (the late calls, or a list of calls the session may already show), and never on a run of its own, which has no session above. Where the session's harness ended its own run the list is headed as calls it lacks, which none is shown twice under, so nothing there is listed again, and the reads an earlier message counted (above) never bring a listing either. That brief is the longer for it, by every held and earlier round's call of a tool where one listed call of it has arguments not comparable, by a note on each marked call, and by the section of calls no list holds one by one, about two hundred bytes and a line per part, and the launch's floor ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)) and any rewrite of a long call by the seat's auxiliary model grow with it. A round carried on in its job's own box, that copy continued rather than a kept capture, is told every call of the round where the job's harness is not known to have ended its own run (**The copy a job's own box holds**, above). Never the call a person approved for the answer that carries the session on, which what carries it on tells: a later attempt at that answer, its first attempt's relaunch refused after it made the call, finds the call in the tool log after the save point of every capture taken before it was made, and listed here as well it was told twice. A call an earlier answer of the round approved is listed as any call is, since nothing else in the brief tells it. A successful `submit_work` among them is told as no submission of the work, so the run makes its own: every call listed was made before the relaunch whose brief lists it, and none of those is the work's submission, since the collection takes one only from the calls after the round's last answer; a lost round, or one refused on a replaced sign-in or by its provider in a session it continued, whose calls since that answer hold one is collected on it rather than carried on; and a send-back's brief can list the submission its review sent back.
