A successful `submit_work` of the round that the session itself holds, which no list tells (one at or before its save point, one a reading of a cut-off session's archive finds it holding, or, in the copy its job's own box holds where that job's harness ended its own run, any but a late one or one nobody waited for), is told first, whether or not any call is listed, as no submission of the work either: it was made before the relaunch as surely as a listed one, and a run that submitted and then asked, continued in its box, was otherwise handed the answer alone and could read its own submission as done. Only the round's own calls are read for it, never a submission an earlier turn made in the session its conversation's last turn left.
- **How many more calls after the save the tool log dropped from its middle**, which it keeps only as a tally (past two hundred calls a run's log keeps its first and last and tallies those between): an exact count, since the log numbers every call it takes — but for a call an older version of the engine appended in a fleet mid-upgrade, which carries no number, so where one is listed it may be counted here as well: an over-count, never an under-count — followed by the log's tally of every call it dropped, by tool, the line every other reader of a long run is given, or, where the late calls dropped are counted below it, after that count instead: every count of dropped calls a brief gives says the tally is below it, so the tally is said once, after the last of them. The tally counts calls made before the save point as well, and a call counted only there has no outcome, so the run is told to check whether its tool already did what the call was for before doing it again.
- **Every call the tool log took only after the job that made it was replaced, every call nobody waited for by the time it returned** ([below](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)), **and every call still in flight as the round was read** ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)), whatever the save point, apart from the calls above and under words of their own, whether or not its harness was cut off — and to the copy a job's own box holds whatever its job's harness's end, which where that harness ended its own run is told these calls alone, since it holds every other call of the round wherever its job's brief told the round's calls (above): such a call is one the run that made it stopped waiting for before it finished (it gave up on it, or was cut off or replaced), or one whose outcome is unknown, so the session may show it with no outcome, as still running, as interrupted or as failed, and an earlier message may have told it, a brief or the item that handed it to the job working as it landed, so it is said to be one call, made once, whose outcome as told here stands. A call the session may show that one of them could be taken for, one of the round or of the turn's earlier rounds, is listed again right before this section, as beside the calls after the save (above), on every harness: wherever a save point holds calls beside a late one, in the copy whose harness ended its own run, which holds every other call of the round, and wherever the turn has closed rounds. A call still in flight is listed failed, in words that say its outcome is unknown and that what it did may have taken effect, and with its arguments said to be kept on no record, never drawn as a call made with none, so the section never says its calls finished, nor that a failed one whose line says its outcome is unknown did not take effect: that one may have, and the run checks whether it did before making it again. Told that every call there finished and that every failed one did not take effect, a run could make such a call again, a second post or delegation. A `submit_work` among them is told as no submission of the work, so the run makes its own. Each telling is in the brief, so in the launch's floor, and in any rewrite of a long call. Such a call a long round's log dropped from its middle keeps no mark and no number, so the log counts it, and every continuation is told that count under the same words whatever its save point, with the log's tally after it, the last count the brief gives — never as a call the session lacks, which the session may show. One that came after the point is counted among the calls dropped after it as well, by its number: an over-count, never an under-count.
- **Every note a person sent the turn that the session has not read** — read after it was saved, by the run that went on in it or by a review, which is never the session's — and then the notes this brief is the first to read ([Where a note lands](turn-engine.md#where-a-note-lands)). **Where the session was cut off**, and for the copy a job's own box holds where that job's harness is not known to have ended its own run, the notes before those are **every note the turn has read**, in the order read, under a header that counts them as notes the session may already show, a note shown both there and in the session being one note, sent once: it is not known to hold its job's brief, which told the notes the session it continued lacked, an earlier job's among them, and no record says which those were. So a capture cut off states no note it holds, whatever its job read, and the brief that continues it is the longer for every note the turn has read, as a fresh brief is, which its launch's floor counts where its capture measured the session's context ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)). **Where its notes stop before a read the record marks unanswered** — a take whose write landed with its answer lost ([Notes to a running run](#notes-to-a-running-run)), whose note the session lacks though its harness ended its own run, while it holds the answered ones after it — **or restarted**, a note the session shows a hook took only before its last restart, which a resume rebuilds the conversation after, **or before a note a hook served and no step has read**, which the session may lack while it holds the reads after it, the notes from that point on are told under the same header, and none before it: whichever job's take it was, and where the mark landed only after the capture was stamped, the relaunch reading the record's marks itself. A launch that tells a note marked unanswered again records it read by the job it opens, at the marked take's own place among the reads, so a capture of that job counts it held; a mark that lands after a brief was built, which that brief did not tell as marked, stops the cursor of every capture after it. The copy a job's own box holds, its harness having ended its own run, is told them the same way. **And a note the run's bridge served a harness** — recorded served before the poll that handed it over was answered, and read only once the harness confirmed its model was sent it plain ([OpenCode's notes plugin](#opencodes-notes-plugin)), or before a hook's answer, and read only once the job's session showed the hook took it ([Claude Code's hooks](#claude-codes-hooks)), a serve its harness cancelled among them unless the session proved it never took the note — may be in the session whatever the record says of its read, so every continuation tells it under the same header: read since by a review, among the notes it has not read, or still waiting, among the ones the brief is the first to read — where the header takes every note before the last one served, so the order read is kept, and only the notes after it follow plainly, each one the turn had not read before. A fresh run is told it as every note.
- **Everything again where its harness may hand it a summary.** Claude Code compacts a session before a request where its own count of the conversation (its last counted reply's input and output, everything after it, and what the server cleared) with the brief and what its new turn attaches reaches the window it holds the run to less its reply reserve and a 13,000-token buffer, and keeps only a summary of what came before its last reply: a continued run's first request is no exception. The engine bounds that count from above off the session's own main thread, as a capture is taken (what its scrub took out of the thread added back at a token a byte, since a box may resume its own copy unscrubbed) and as a collection reads the job's box (`resumed_count` on the capture and on the job's record), and judges it under the least window the harness can hold the run's model to and the window the run reported. Where the continuation may compact at its first request, or the count cannot be bounded (an image, a document or a PDF read after its last counted reply, a reply's usage it cannot read, a server clearing, a saved precompact summary, a compaction with no reply after it, a thread not read whole, a release older than 2.1.310, a model the engine does not know), and where its job's main thread restarted after its brief (a compaction as it worked, or a restart it cannot rule out), the session is told as a cut-off one: why, every lead its record keeps, every call of the round from its start and every note the turn has read, as messages it may already show, under its own words where nothing says it was cut off. Its skill guard then holds no skill, each loaded again before a call it covers. A reading of a cut-off session's archive (above) still thins the calls where its job restarted it, leaving every other word: the reading counts a call only past the main thread's last restart. `executor_session_may_compact` says so where the verdict switches the telling, and `executor_session_count_unbounded` where a collection's read could not bound the copy. OpenCode compacts by a rule of its own (below), whose point only the box the run is handed can say, so **an OpenCode continuation is judged in its box**, as its launch has it, and so are Gemini CLI's and Qwen Code's: the relaunch hands the launch both tellings, the held one and the one told as a session that may be a summary. Gemini CLI's and Qwen Code's launch hands the held one only where the harness's own count's bound (the capture's, the worse of it and the copy's where the box resumes its own copy, as the take and a collection count each), with the brief and what the box hands over each at a token a byte, is strictly below the box's point (both above), whatever provider wrote the count, and the summarized one everywhere else. OpenCode's launch reads the box's point (one exec, under the run's own environment and the box's documents, the engine's own document set aside as the run's script sets it aside: the box's login imported, `opencode api model.list` and `config.get` answered into files, the plugin folders listed) and hands the held one only where the count's bound, on the launch's own provider, with the brief and what the box hands over before it, each at a quarter of its bytes rounded up, is strictly below that point; or where the box's documents turn compaction off (`compaction.auto: false`). Everywhere else it hands the summarized one, whose guard arms no skill. The point is the model's limit (the smaller of its input and context limits) less the buffer the highest document sets below it (tokens, or a share such as `"10%"`), else less the larger of fifteen hundredths of it and 16,000 tokens once the limit is twice that. There is no point, and the continuation is told as a summary, for a box release outside the set below or other than the one that wrote the session (`release`, `pair`), a plugin other than the engine's own, in a document or a plugin folder (`plugin`, since a plugin can compact the session or add to it before the first request), a provider's `contextManagement` option (`contextmanagement`), a launch whose model names no provider (`nomodel`) or one the box's catalog does not list, its provider's credential not in the box among the causes (`absent`), a model whose compaction is its provider's own (`native`), a limit nothing states (`defaulted`: OpenCode holds such a model to 200,000 tokens, which may not be its server's window), a zero limit with compaction on (`nolimit`), and a read that failed or ran past its 60 s (`unread`; on the kept path it follows the 60 s the launch may wait on the box's answer to whether it carries the session, so such a relaunch's box is asked for up to two minutes before its run starts). **An OpenCode box hands over nothing before the brief**: a continuation that keeps its box's copy re-imports it first ([An OpenCode run's session](#an-opencode-runs-session)), and an import keeps no record of what OpenCode told the session, so the count and the brief are all the launch judges. The engine counts an OpenCode session by that rule all the same, from above, as a capture is taken (what its scrub took out added back at a token a byte) and as a collection reads the export the job's script left once its harness ended its own run (a job cut off is not read): the last counted reply's input, cache reads, cache writes, output and reasoning, as its provider reported them, and every message after it, the reply's own tool results among them, at a quarter of its bytes in the export, rounded up, which is never under OpenCode's own estimate of it and over it by about 95 tokens a message; restarted at the newest completed compaction (`resumed_count`, with the provider of that reply beside it, `count_provider`, since a continuation on another provider's model is not held to the figure, and on the job's record the release that wrote the copy, `count_release`, the writer a continuation in the job's box is paired with, whether or not a capture was taken). It reads the newest compaction of any status as where the session restarts, the transcript's own rule. What the bytes cannot bound is a mark: a session with no counted reply since its start or its newest completed compaction (`unanchored`), a PDF after the reply (`pdf`) or any other file (`media`), an export not read whole or a provider that does not read (`unread`), and a session written by an OpenCode release outside the set whose rule was read in its shipped code and measured at its boundaries, **2.3.2** (`release`): a set, never a range, since any release may move the rule, and a later release joins it only once it has been read and probed the same way. The count holds an OpenCode continuation's launch to the size of its next request (below).
- **Every note from a hook's step again, in a box whose Claude Code release the engine has not read.** A note a hook served is read where the job's session shows it on the conversation Claude Code's resume rebuilds, which the engine has read for 2.1.310 and 2.1.322 alone ([Claude Code's hooks](#claude-codes-hooks)), and the box a relaunch lands in can run another: a new box whatever its image holds, the job's own box the release that wrote its copy, which the engine has not read off it and which `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` keeps from changing since ([A Claude Code run's session](#a-claude-code-runs-session)). So where a hook's read is at stake the launch asks the box's harness its release before it picks the brief, the job's own box included, and a box that answers any other release is told every note from the first one a hook's step read on, under the header of notes it may already show. That telling is judged on its own brief, as every path's first request is: where it may bring the session to its compaction point, it is the telling of a session that may be a summary (above). Where the seat's budget cannot carry its briefs beside the session's own, the launch's floor ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)) drops them alone: the session is still offered, told as it would be anywhere else, and a box that then answers another release starts a session of its own.

**A call that ends after its job's relaunch.** The bridge runs a call under the run's own context, never the request's, so a call can finish after its harness died, gave up on it or was replaced. Where a relaunch that carried the round on — a loss's, a person's answer's, a replaced sign-in's, a refused session's — has opened the run's tool log to the next job by then, the log still lists the call as one of the round — its entry, written before it ran, updated — numbered as any call is, and marks it `late`. So does that opening, for a call of the job it replaces that the log took after the read the relaunch's briefs were built from — while the relaunch was readied: its probe of the kept session, any rewrite of a long call by the seat's auxiliary model, the call a person approved — but never for the call a person approved, which the relaunch's lead tells. What a late call cost is charged to no job: the next job's resume would pay it as its own, and its own job is over. What it committed counts in the turn's outcome as any call's does (a message it posted, a work item it filed), whether the log still lists it or has dropped it from a long round's middle, since the log keeps the kinds of change the round's calls committed apart from the calls. The round's record marks a late call, and its reviewer reads it as an earlier run's: its line in the reviewer's log says an earlier run of the task, replaced before the call finished, made it once, and that an earlier round may list the same call with its outcome unknown, which is no second call; the delivery checks and the submission's citations count it as the turn's, as they count an earlier round's call. No brief of the round had told it when the log took it, and the session of the job that made it may not hold it, so no save point holds a late call: every continuation of the round built after it landed is told it whatever its save point — a copy continued in its job's own box among them, whatever its harness's end — under words of its own (above), but a continuation of a session that took it (below); no skill guard counts a skill it loaded, so the skill is loaded again before a call it covers; and the round's collection never takes a late `submit_work` for the round's submission, nor keeps it whole as it keeps the round's own: the job carrying the round on makes the round's submission, and wherever the late one is told, to that job as it lands or to a continuation after it, it is told as no submission of the work. A long round's log keeps a late call while it drops ordinary calls from its middle, and counts one it does drop. A call still running as its round's collection read the log, whose update lands once a relaunch that started a new round, as a send-back does, has opened the log to that round, is listed in the new round's log as a late call with no place, since its place was its own round's and the new round numbers its own calls; what it cost is charged to no job, and what it committed counts in the new round's outcome. It counts toward the new round's delivery check as a late call of the round does: its effect happened in the turn, and no earlier collection read it. Its begin is never taken there, so no call of a closed round starts. One whose update lands before that opening is listed in its own round, after the collection's read, and the opening carries it into the new round the same way: every relaunch, a send-back's included, hands its launch the read its briefs were built from, and a new round's opening lists late, with no place, every call its round's log took after that read but the call a person approved, which the collection read with the round. Every new round also starts with the kinds of change the turn's calls committed so far, and with the calls the old round's calls' own work made after that read, which the collection had not counted. The runs answer serves the mark (`late`), and the Executors board tags such a call **finished after a relaunch**. The job working on the round as a late call lands — the one carrying the round on, the one a relaunch was readying as it landed, which that relaunch's opening hands it to, or a new round's job, for a call of the round before — is handed it at its next request, as [an item for one job](#notes-to-a-running-run): Claude Code after a tool batch, never at its finish, and OpenCode at its next step; a continuation of a session that took it is not told it again, and every other continuation is; the runs answer names such a call (`bridge_calls_told`), and the Executors board tags it **told to its run while it worked**. **What this does not reach**: a call the job is not handed as it lands — a job parked, claimed or past its ending, a job's eleventh, or a filing that failed — is told only by the continuations. And what a late call committed counts in the turn's outcome only where the log takes the call before the turn's last collection reads the log, which waits for every call of the round still in flight up to the first of its own bound, the turn's cap and its process gone ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)): one whose update lands after it is in no outcome and told to nobody. A call the old round's log dropped from a long middle after the collection's read is carried into the new round by its name and what it committed alone, and told to no job.

**A call its harness gave up on.** The bridge runs a call under the run's own context, so a call goes on after its harness stops waiting for it, which the bridge sees in four ways: the harness cancels the request (`notifications/cancelled`), as Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, Grok Build, Kimi Code and Muse Code do at their tool timeout, discarding a late answer, so its model reads the call as timed out; the harness hangs up on the call's response, which the bridge keeps going while the call runs ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)), so the next progress finds it gone; the box drops the request the call came on, which the bridge sees as that request's end (Kimi Code's drop of a silent response at 300 seconds, before the bridge answered it); or the job's session on the bridge ends with the call still running — the run settled, its next job's opening replaced it, the seat left the node, or a recovery opened the job again — and the end answers the call at once that it is still running ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)), so its harness is handed that answer and never the call's own. Its effect happens all the same. A harness that gave up on a call can still end its own run, and its job park on a question with the call still running, so the call can land as one of its job's own before a capture of that session is placed by its read, or before a relaunch reads the round's calls as the job's own copy in its box holds them: counted there, it was told to no continuation, while the session held only that it timed out, and the run could make it again. So the bridge records on the call whether anybody still waited for its answer as its tool returned — the request cancelled, its response gone, or the job's session's end answered it first, which the bridge decides once, so no call is both handed its own answer and marked for that end — and the runs answer serves the mark (`abandoned`). No save point holds a call so marked: every continuation of the round built after it landed is told it whatever its save point, the job's own copy in its box whatever its harness's end, under the late calls' words (above), but a continuation of a session that took it; no skill guard counts a skill it loaded, whose body never reached the session; and a long round's log keeps it as it keeps a late call, and counts one it does drop among them. What it committed counts in the turn's outcome as a late call's does, listed or dropped, and on the same condition: only where the log takes it before the turn's last collection reads the log. Unlike a late call it is its job's own: what it cost is charged to that job, and a successful `submit_work` among such calls can be the round's submission, though a continuation told it is told, as of a late one, to make its own, which the collection replays over it. And the job itself, still working as the call lands, is handed it at its next request, as a late call's working job is (above), so its model learns the call ran rather than taking its own timeout for its outcome and making it again; a continuation of a session that took it is not told it again, and the Executors board tags it **told to its run while it worked**, as it does a late call. The board tags every call so marked **its run stopped waiting for it**. **What this does not reach**: a harness that stops waiting for a call without cancelling it, while its job's session on the bridge is still open as the call returns, where nothing the bridge writes finds its response gone before the tool returns: one that hangs up in the last 20 seconds of the call, after the bridge's last progress, or on a call whose request carries no progress token, on which nothing is kept going; and one that gives up while it still reads the response, which the bridge cannot tell from one still waiting. Such a call lands unmarked, and a save point holds it as any call, though its session holds it as timed out. Claude Code's own watchdogs on a call give up this way, answering its model with an error and cancelling nothing. On 2.1.310, at the settings the engine runs it with, its budget for a response's first byte and its check on a silent call no longer give up a running call: its answer starts at once and is kept going, and the box's settings hold each to the bridge's bound, at which Claude Code cancels ([Claude Code](#claude-code)). One check still can: every 30 seconds it gives up a call 90 seconds after its transport was marked lost unless a progress has cleared the mark since (by reading its bundle), and the mark is routine, made on every call in flight whenever Claude Code loses the session's standing GET stream, which it does 360 seconds after opening it (measured). A call whose response is gone is not among them: the bridge's next progress finds the response gone, and the call is marked. What that check gives up unmarked is a call whose progress a hop between the box and the node holds back for 90 seconds while the response stays intact and the bridge's writes succeed, and a call whose request carries no progress token, on which nothing clears the mark (measured: a 540-second call with no token, given up at 449.9 seconds, 90 after its session's GET stream was lost, and recorded as any call when its tool returned). And a harness that gives up on a call in the moment between its tool's answer and that answer's delivery, as the bridge records the call. And a call still running as its run is collected — its run settled or parked on its question, a person's stop, the turn's cap or a reclaim ending its job, each of which ends the session and waits for no call — is waited for by that collection on the run's tool log, on whichever node makes it, up to the first of its own bound, the turn's cap and its process gone ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)); one still running past that is read as a call whose outcome is unknown, and what it committed is in no outcome unless its update lands before the turn's last collection reads the log: in its round's log, or, past a send-back, in the next round's. One whose update lands once the run's ending has deleted the record is on no record of the run at all, though its effect happened: the ending's delete names it as it goes (`sandbox_run_deleted_with_calls_in_flight`), and the engine's log names it again at warning as it returns (`bridge_abandoned_call_after_its_job`). And a call still running when the process running it is killed never makes its update: its entry stays on the run's record, the call counted by its identity and its outcome unknown; a node's graceful stop waits for it once it has given its seats back ([Graceful shutdown](agent-runtime.md#graceful-shutdown)).

Every word in it that somebody else wrote is fenced or defused under the relaunching segment's token, and every marker of any token in it escaped, so nothing the session read in an earlier segment opens or closes a fence of this one ([ADR-0040](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0040-content-a-model-reads-carries-its-provenance.md)).

**Its skills follow the session.** A continued session has the skill bodies it loaded in front of it, so a relaunch that continues it arms its [skill guard](tool-skills.md#session-scope--why-per-phase-not-per-turn) with exactly those — the skills the launch of the job it follows was armed with, and those that job's own session loaded, through the point its capture was saved at where the capture is what is restored (of a session cut off, the newest point its launch held, so a skill it loaded after that is loaded again before a call it covers), and all of them where the job's own copy in its box is continued, but only where its harness ended its own run — and never another session's: not an earlier round's, not an earlier job's of the round, and not one a late call loaded (above). One that starts a session of its own starts with an empty guard, and so does one that continues the session its conversation's last turn left: the skills that session loaded were another turn's, which its lead says were set up anew. The guard is armed when the launch has decided which session its run takes up, once it knows its box and before the run starts, so a launch that finds it cannot continue the session after all — a box whose harness cannot take it up, an object the store no longer holds, a session the seat's budget cannot carry — arms an empty one ([Runtime invariants](turn-engine.md#runtime-invariants) 7 and 8). A run whose box finds only once it starts that its restore failed — an archive that does not unpack, an import OpenCode refuses — starts a session of its own, **and its box says so before the run's first call**, so the run is held to that session's guard, an empty one ([Which session the box started](#which-session-the-box-started)).

### Which session the box started

Whether a restore succeeds is the box's to find out as its run starts, and the guard must be the run's session's before the bridge admits a call. So a launch that continues a session hands its box the seat's tools under **two bridge tokens of the job**: one for the session it continues, one for a session of its own its script starts in its place. Once its restore has settled, the script installs the token of the session it started (Claude Code's MCP configuration, OpenCode's configured values) and removes the other, before the harness starts. The token the harness dials is the box's word on which session it started, read by the [bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box) where it reads every request's token:

- **On the run's first request, before any call.** The first request on either token (often the MCP handshake) holds the guard to the session the box started before it is served; requests arriving meanwhile wait. The guard is the one the launch armed where the box took up the continued session, an empty one where it started its own.
  - Then the node that launched the run states, as the round's opening frame, the fresh brief the run was handed in the continuation's place. It is published beside the request, not on its path, so a slow broker never holds the handshake past its connect timeout, and may therefore follow a later frame of the round, its completion included. It is given up if the broker has not taken it within five seconds, which leaves the continuation as the opening frame; the collection still says the run started a session of its own (`harness_session_continued` false, and `session_not_continued` says `restore_failed` with the script's reason).
  - A node that took the run over before its box first reached the bridge holds the run to that empty guard and writes what the box said on the job's record, but holds no copy of the brief: the opening frame stays the continuation, and the collection says the same (`harness_session_continued` false, and `session_not_continued` says `restore_failed` with the script's reason).
  - A later request on the other token is refused.
  - A box whose harness never reaches its bridge makes no call, and no guard is asked.
- **Not something the run's model can forge.** The session is in what the fleet signs, and by the time the model can read a file the box holds only the token of its session. The script's own record of its restore, which the collection reads into the run's `executor_collected` (the detail of `session_not_continued`'s `restore_failed` stays its record there), is a file the model could rewrite, and is never what a guard is built from.
- **Kept on the job's record.** What the box said is written on the run's record, and every later rebuild of the guard reads it: the collection's, a relaunch after a person's answer, a loss, a replaced sign-in or a provider's refusal of the session its job continued, a reviewer's send-back that continues the session, and a node taking the run over while it works. The skills the launch armed are the session's only where the box said it took that session up.
  - The record also names **the session the job ran**: a runner names its session before its harness starts (the one it continues or one it mints, and beside a continued one, the session its script starts in its place), but for a harness that names its own only as it runs, whose reported id the record binds ([A session its harness names as it runs](#a-session-its-harness-names-as-it-runs)).
  - Where a person's answer or replaced sign-in carries the round on in the box it parked or was refused in **without the turn's kept capture** (none kept, or none the relaunch's runner restores), it continues whichever of the two the box said it started. Never the one the launch chose where the box fell back (its transcript never read the skills the job loaded), and never one a file in the box names (such as the session record the collection reads), which the model could rewrite. A launch that continued nothing ran the session it named.
  - A row that says nothing (a box that never reached its bridge, a record the coordination store did not take) reads as a session of the job's own for its guard. This is the safe direction: a guard short of a skill asks the run to load it again, where one holding a skill its session never read would let through a call the skill exists to hold back. For a launch that continued a session, such a row names neither session as the one its box ran, so no relaunch continues either by that word: an answer or replaced sign-in carries the round on from the kept capture, or in a session of its own.
  - **A kept capture names its session as its take read it**, off the session record the script writes as its harness exits, which the executor log's row then names. A relaunch continuing that capture continues that session, restored into whichever box it gets or, in the very box it was taken in after a clean exit, as that box's own copy, whatever the box said. What the box's word decides there is the guard: the job's own loads through the capture, plus the skills the job's launch armed only where the box said it took that session up.

### A session its harness names as it runs

A harness that mints its session's id only once it runs names none at launch. Its run's script reports the id its harness minted, `session-report` in the box's work directory, written whole and renamed into place, before the prompt goes in, and the engine binds that report to the job's record where the id is first used: before a save of the running job is packed, as the job is collected (a run that made no call included), and before any take of its box, a lost run's after a recovery among them. The report is the box's word, so a bind holds three rules:

- **Once.** A later report naming another id is refused, whichever node reads it: the bind is on the record, not in a node's memory.
- **Only a fresh id.** Every bound id is claimed fleet-wide in the coordination store, and an id another live run's job claims is refused. The claim is taken first; then the executor log is asked, with one seek over its index of session ids, and an id any turn's row names is refused; then the record is written. The claim is released when the bind fails, once the session's capture lands on the executor log, whose seek guards the id from then on, or with the run's record; it moves to the turn's next job when that job continues the session. The same job binding again (a recovery, a second save) is answered as bound.
- **A resume reports nothing new.** Whether a launch continued its session is the engine's word, the token its box dialled ([Which session the box started](#which-session-the-box-started)): a job that took the continued session up binds that one alone, and one that started its own in its place binds any id but that one.

A refused report fails the run closed: nothing is saved, taken, carried or collected under it, and its collection says why first. Every take and save names the bound session, and one whose box names another since the bind is refused. An executor log that cannot answer leaves the bind undecided: nothing is bound or dropped, and the read is made again. A job whose box reported nothing yet has no session: its save is skipped, saying so, and a relaunch after a loss continues none, as for a run killed before its report. Codex and Kimi Code mint their own ([A Codex run's session](#a-codex-runs-session), [A Kimi Code run's session](#a-kimi-code-runs-session)).

### What a continued launch costs

A continued run sends its session's whole context again before it reads a word of its brief, and every request it makes carries that context, mostly from the prompt cache but with every token counted against the seat's windows ([Cache share](../guides/budgets-and-spend.md#cache-share)). So:

- **Its launch's floor** is the larger of `turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens` and the session's context with the brief that continues it, taking the longer of its two briefs' estimates (which box the launch gets is the launch's to learn).

  **The context is the harness's own estimate of the session's next request** where the capture holds one.
  - Claude Code's is read off the main thread as captured, by the rule Claude Code decides whether to compact by: its last counted reply's input, cache writes, cache reads and output, placed at the first record of its message, plus Claude Code's estimate of every main-thread record after it. Estimates: text at length over three characters a token (over four for the fourteen older models Claude Code counts so, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 among them); a JSON-titled document at two; an image or a document it does not read as text 2,000; a PDF read 3,000 a page; an attachment at the rendering its record stores, or two bytes a token of its line where the harness renders it again; a system record nothing. It restarts at a compaction from its summary and the stretch it kept before its boundary. It is recorded at both rates and read at the rate of the launch's member's model, an alias at three, the larger.
  - OpenCode's is its count of the session where it holds a bound ([What a continued session is told](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)), at the one rate OpenCode counts text at.
  - The last request's input alone, which this replaces, lacks that request's reply and everything after it (p50 1,371, p99 15,899, at most 107,203 tokens on real sessions), and past a compaction no request has followed it is the compacted-away conversation's. It is never carried along a session's lineage: a job that made no request of its own may have grown its copy by its brief.

  **Where nothing estimated it**, the context is the whole input of the session's last request, cache included, read off the transcript as captured: Claude Code's last main-thread assistant message's usage (each key exactly as written, each count a whole number; a message whose usage reads otherwise gives no figure and the one before it stands), or OpenCode's last settled assistant message's tokens. That is the case for:
  - an OpenCode session whose count is marked;
  - a Claude Code thread not read whole or written by a release below 2.1.310;
  - a compaction whose kept stretch the reading cannot find;
  - a record after the last counted reply whose content Claude Code's estimate throws on (a call's name that is no string, or a text document's title that is there, not null and no string);
  - one that nests an object the estimate charges more than eight element lists deep (through results' contents and documents' sources);
  - a PDF read after it whose pages do not read;
  - a capture an older build stamped or one settled off the executor log, which carries the last request's input alone.

  **A kept capture is held to its own context**, as it measured and estimated it, never its job's newest capture's or its copy's: a session restored from it sends what it holds, however far its job went on.

  **The job before's own copy in its box is measured as that job ends.** It is held to, in order:
  1. the harness's estimate of its next request where the read that collected the job made one off the copy's main thread (`next_request_tokens` on the job's record, beside the count of [What a continued session is told](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session), in the same read);
  2. else where the job's newest capture's take made one;
  3. otherwise the larger of the job's newest capture's measure, kept or not, and what the collecting read found the copy's newest request carried, off the run's own account of its requests:
     - Claude Code's event stream: the newest main-thread assistant line (its `parent_tool_use_id` present and null) carries the usage, read by the same rule. A line after it past the stream's line bound, or a stream cut short, leaves no figure, since it may be a later request's.
     - OpenCode's session message list, asked of the run's own server once the session is exported, never on an end request: one assistant message a page, newest first, each page after the first only where the one before failed, at most six pages and one MiB, the first settled message that measured a prompt being the figure.

  The read records the figure on the job's record beside how its harness ended (`session_context`), in that read's one write and with no read of the box of its own, so a company that keeps no session measures the copy too. A job that made no request of its own carries the figure of the session it took up and says where it came from: the job whose copy it continued in place, the kept capture's own measure, the frozen base's, or none for a session of its own or where its box says it started one. No reader takes a carried figure for a fresh measure. A session neither measured has no known context: its launch is held to the floor with the continuing brief beside it, judged against the capped windows as a measured one is.

  **Each session the launch may continue is held to its own floor.** A relaunch offered both the kept capture and the job's own copy, each with its own brief, is held to the larger floor, since its box takes up the kept one where it can restore it and the copy only where it cannot. A session whose floor no capped window, or no request under the model's window, can carry is not continued while the launch still offers the other; `executor_session_not_continued` says why.

  **Every launch is held to its fresh brief's floor** (the floor with the fresh brief beside it), whatever sessions it offers, since its box starts a session of its own on that brief wherever it takes none up, a failed restore included. So a launch is held to the largest floor of every brief it may hand its run.

  **A fresh brief's floor past the room.** The room is each window's ceiling less what the launch's own turn spent there before it (a dispatch charges its context assembly, and a relaunch its review and rewrites, into those windows before the launch reads them and again every try, so a launch held at the ceiling itself would never meet it). Config holds the capped windows only at or above the floor itself, but the room can still be less. Then the floor is held rather than refused at every window, and the launch says so (`executor_floor_held`), naming the floor it is held to, which is a session's floor where that is larger:
  - Where the floor fits in the room, the launch is held at the floor alone and goes out in a window with that much left, whatever other seats or a background pass spent there first. Its first request can then take the window past its ceiling by up to the room less the floor more than a launch held at the room would; `sandbox_spend_over_budget` reports it. It is not held at the room because that would need a window holding nothing but the launch's own turn's spend, which a busy company whose own ceiling is the smallest may never leave (its other seats spend there first after every turnover); a launch that never goes out is worse than a reported overrun.
  - Where the launch's own turn left less than the floor, it is held at the room and waits for a window that holds nothing but that turn's spend.

  **A launch refused below a floor above the floor alone waits one turnover at most.** A floor within the room (a fresh brief's or a session's, measured or not) can be past what every window leaves when the launch reads it, since a busy company's other seats spend first after every turnover. The window it was refused in rides its wait:
  - on a dispatch, the seat's budget park keeps it for the delivery whose launch it was, read by that delivery's tries alone, never by a person's message the park's release hands the seat first (on that node: a seat that moves to another may wait one window more there);
  - on a resume, the job's record keeps it (`relaunch_refused_in`, written by the release that hands the held or turned-back claim back).

  Its next try, in a later window, holds its fresh brief's floor at the floor alone (or at the room below it) and drops a session whose floor that window still leaves no room for, `executor_session_not_continued` saying why. A record written by a build that keeps no such window reads as never refused, which costs the launch at most one more window.

  **The floor is the member's the launch picks.** The launch picks its member of the seat's chain once, as it launches (the first not sitting out its plan), before it reckons the floor. A kept session written by another harness than that member's is started fresh, held to the floor with its fresh brief beside it; the continuing briefs were written beforehand wherever some member could take it up, since a plan can be spent or come back between. The job before's own session in its box counts only where that member can continue in that box: the same harness in the same cell, and a box on the engine host only on the node that launched it.

  A relaunch refused below its floor is held (an answer's, turned back) on that figure. A turn's first launch that continues its conversation's session, whose context is the base's own as its row recorded it, is refused on its dispatch, and the dispatcher parks the seat's mail on that figure, never on the floor alone, which a window with room for a fresh launch but not for the session meets, and which handed the delivery straight back into the same refusal. Its reason says what the figure is made of ([Budgets and Spend](../guides/budgets-and-spend.md#budget-windows)).
- **Its context is bounded by its harness's compaction.**
  - **Claude Code.** Every run is pinned to **the context window of the model it works under** (`CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`), set by the wrapper over whatever the seat, the image or a profile set, and from 2.1.310 by the run's own settings over a repository's, with the variables that would switch compaction off or move its point unset, and the two that move it blank in those settings too. It compacts at the smaller of that window and the one it holds the model to, less its headroom: a reserve for its reply of up to 20,000 tokens, then a 13,000-token buffer. So no request of a run, or of one continuing its session, carries more than about its model's window. The launch floor keeps one request of a continued session sendable and the budget whole, never the session uncompacted: the compaction point is lower, and a continuation past it is not refused but told as a cut-off one ([What a continued session is told](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)).
  - **OpenCode.** It compacts once its own count (last settled reply's input, cache, output and reasoning, plus an estimate of everything after it) reaches its model's limit (the smaller of its input and context limits where the model sets both, else its input limit, else its context limit) less 15% of it, at least 16,000 tokens, or less a configured `compaction.buffer`. The engine does not move it: that setting is a share or a count of the model's window, which the engine does not know. The engine's own document sets no `compaction` key, since an operator's setting is read in the box ([What a continued session is told](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)) and the engine's document does not outrank a box's managed settings. So a continued OpenCode run's request carries up to about its model's window less that share.
  - **Declare a model the box serves itself, a local one above all, with a `limit` at or under its server's window**, in the box's `opencode.json`, and set that server to refuse a request past it rather than cut it. A limit nothing states is OpenCode's default of 200,000 tokens, which the launch reads as no point, and a server that cuts a prompt silently is one OpenCode never sees past its window.
  - A session past the window (an OpenCode one, or a Claude Code one whose repository switched its compaction off) is continued wherever the seat's budget can carry it, its floor saying so.
  - A Claude Code session is not continued on a member whose model's window is too small for it: where its context with the continuing brief is more than one request under that window can carry, its run starts a session of its own and `executor_session_not_continued` says why. That window is the one Claude Code holds the member's model to on the member's platform, read off its entry: the pin, held to 200,000 tokens for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, for an alias that names an older model on the entry's cloud platform, and for an entry that names no model or `default` (the account's default may be one of those). An entry whose account is served the long window of Opus 4.6 or Sonnet 4.6 opts in with `[1m]` on its model and is judged under 1,000,000. A platform the seat's own environment or its image switches the harness to is not read there.

**The window is the model's own.** The engine reads it from the model argument the launch hands Claude Code (an alias such as `opus`, an id such as `claude-opus-5-5`, the same id with a dated or platform suffix, or a `[1m]` opt-in): 1,000,000 tokens for every current Claude model, 200,000 for Claude Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 (1,000,000 with `[1m]`). That is the pin, the most Claude Code may hold a run to; it holds a run to less where the model's own window is less: Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 to 200,000 unless the account is served more or the argument opts in with `[1m]`, an alias naming an older model on a cloud platform or a gateway (Claude Code's own alias table), and no model, or `default`, to the account's default, which may be held to 200,000. A continuation's telling is judged under that standard window, or the window the run itself reported where that is less, and the launch floor under the smaller of it and the pin.

A model it does not know is pinned to **200,000**, the standard window of every Claude model, and the launch logs `executor_context_window_unknown` naming it; Claude Code lowers any pin to the model's own window, so a pin is never past what the model takes. A fixed window below the model's starves the run: its first request already carries the harness's prompt and tools, the seat's bridged tools, its standing instructions and its brief, and under a 100,000-token window Claude Code compacts at 67,000, so in a large repository a few file reads refill the context within three turns of each compaction and the harness stops the run as thrashing (`rapid_refill_breaker`, recorded as `context_exhausted`), fresh session or continued.

The cost of the larger window is per request: a continued Claude Code run of *n* requests on a 1,000,000-token model is charged up to about *n* × 967,000 input tokens, most of them cache reads, and an OpenCode run up to *n* times its model's compaction point, all counted against the seat's windows and held to its launch's floor. The engine records the window each Claude Code run was pinned to on its collected record (`context_window_tokens`).
## A conversation's next turn continues its last turn's session

A turn that serves a conversation (the thread, issue, pull request or work item its trigger names) **continues the session its conversation's last turn left**: its first launch restores the conversation's **head** into a box of its own, and the run takes that session up, told where the new turn begins. The engine tells it what no transcript holds: how each earlier turn ended.

**The head is the turn that read the conversation last.** Of the ended turns whose rows on the executor log still name a kept session, it is the one whose first launch read the conversation latest (the newest end among turns that read at one position; a turn whose read failed counts after every turn that read), never simply the one that ended last. Every first launch continues the head its read named, so sessions form a line. A turn that read early can end after turns that read later (one parked on a person's question frees its seat, and the next message, offered to it as the answer first, runs beside it only where it is not taken; a schedule's next fire, never an answer, runs beside a parked fire every time). Such a turn continued none of what later turns left, so it is told and offered beside the head, never continued, and the next turn's end absorbs it. The seat's [session budget](conversation-sessions.md#configuration) releases the oldest end first, so under pressure it can release a head before a stale sibling; the next turn then continues the still-kept session that read the conversation last, and is told the released head's ending like every other.

**A turn serves every conversation its run read.** A run that [read a wake](#notes-to-a-running-run) of another conversation (a comment in its ticket's thread while it serves a chat) holds that conversation's context too, so the turn's end names each such conversation, at most eight, and each reads the turn's session as its head, placed where the end applied: above every turn of it that read before, below one that read after. The session stays one object, counted once by the seat's budget and the retention; a wake the run never read runs as a turn of its own ([ADR-0073](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0073-a-seats-executor-session-is-a-sealed-object-its-turns-row-names.md)).

**A schedule's fires are one conversation.** The scheduler stamps every fire with its schedule's conversation, so its next fire is that conversation's next turn, handled exactly as below and told in the schedule's words: **How this schedule's earlier fires ended**, and a lead saying a new fire begins and that the schedule firing again, not a message, woke it ([Scheduling](scheduling.md#each-fire-continues-the-last-fires-session)).

**Read once, at the turn's dispatch.** The turn reads its conversation once, as dispatch starts, through the [estate router](../guides/satellite-nodes.md) at `linearizable`, so an end another node published is included: the head, and every other ended turn no ended turn was shown (the newest sixteen, the rest counted). From that read it renders how those turns ended and decides what its launches continue; no launch reads again. A turn with no conversation key (a colleague's ask, a generic source's wake) reads nothing, nor does a turn of a company with `turn_engine.conversation_session.enabled: false`. A read that fails, or that the node's copy refuses, is logged (`executor_conversation_unread`), and the turn runs with no account of its conversation and a session of its own: less context, never a turn that cannot work.

**How the conversation's earlier turns ended.** Every brief of the turn (fresh brief, a relaunch's reseed, the brief after a continued session's lead) carries a section above `## Task`, **How this conversation's earlier turns ended**. For each turn, oldest first: how it ended (`completed`, `failed`, `stopped` or `lost`) and its reviewer's last word; whether its reply reached the party waiting and on what surface, or that this is not known; what its reviewer said landed, what its executor said blocked it, who stopped it and why, what failed as the engine recorded it; that its newest session was not kept, and why; the engine's answer to a colleague's ask it took up; and what it was asked. Its rules: a reply that reached the party waiting is not to be said again, one that did not may still be owed, everything else already took effect, and where history and task disagree, the task wins.

- **Bounded at 24 000 bytes** as the run's record carries it, escapes included (about six thousand tokens): the head always, then other turns newest first, each whole, while they fit. The rest are counted (`N earlier turns of this conversation are not shown here`) and stay for the next turn, since a turn's end absorbs only the turns its brief told.
- Every account somebody else wrote (what a turn was asked, its reviewer's and executor's words, a stop's reason, the engine's accounts quoting a box or store) is fenced under the turn's token as `turn_ending`, at the least trust, and the name of whoever stopped a turn is defused in place ([ADR-0040](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0040-content-a-model-reads-carries-its-provenance.md)).
- It is rendered once at dispatch and frozen on every park, so every brief of the turn tells the same bytes.

**Frozen at the first launch, and held on the log.** The first launch freezes the read on the run's record it creates (where it was read, the turns its brief told, and the head as the turn's **base**); no later launch's write changes it. It records the read on the executor log as the turn's `begin`, right after that record exists and before any box does, asked for at most fifteen seconds on the launching frame. The turn's row then **holds the base** against every release but a retirement (a sibling turn's end, the seat's budget, the retention; not the end of a turn that [ran out of context](conversation-sessions.md#a-session-that-ran-out-of-context-is-retired) in it) until the turn's first landed capture or its end ([ADR-0073](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0073-a-seats-executor-session-is-a-sealed-object-its-turns-row-names.md)). A begin the log does not hold in time leaves the launch continuing no base; one that lands later holds no longer than the first capture or the end. Every capture carries the read its first launch froze, so the turn's end absorbs the turns it was handed (the base among them) and nothing else. A turn with no session of its own when its first job is lost (box gone with its host, capture refused or unanswered) is [relaunched](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session) into the same base on whichever node holds the seat, never a head read again. Once the turn has kept a session of its own, that one holds the base and everything after, and only the relaunch rule applies.

**In a box of its own, told where the turn begins.** A box the turn's earlier job ran in holds that job's tree and session, to be continued in place, so the base is continued only in a box of the launch's own. The launch reads the base's row again at `linearizable` and takes it up only while it still names the session the read froze. As for a [kept session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session), the runner and the box's harness must take it up, and its object is fetched sealed and opened whole before a byte reaches the box. The run gets a lead, then the turn's own brief whole. The lead says:

- everything above is the conversation as its turns left it, through the base's turn, which ended at its instant; or, where that turn's end said it **went on past** the session its row names, up to that session (kept while the turn still worked, at what instant), with what the turn did after it told below, saying too where the turn was then lost; or, where the turn was lost and said nothing of going on (the engine ended it, or its end was never recorded), through it, the session perhaps not holding the last of what it did. And a new message has woken it, the task below being this turn's;
- what it read above may be stale, and tools it activated and skills it loaded were set up anew: its [skill guard](tool-skills.md#session-scope--why-per-phase-not-per-turn) starts empty;
- it is in a new box on a fresh checkout (for a run offered `code_checkout`, of a repository the box's setup clones; a repository the session checked out of Gitlet is not there until checked out again, at its branch's head ([Repositories on Gitlet](#repositories-on-gitlet))); what the session had not committed and pushed went with the old box, and absolute paths under the base's home were that box's;
- where the base's capture was cut off, it may end mid-call.

The launch's record says `continued_conversation`; the run carries the fresh brief beside the lead, for its script to hand a session of its own where its restore fails in the box, and its box says which session it started ([below](#which-session-the-box-started)).

**What it costs, and where the seat waits.** Continuing sends the session's whole context first, as a relaunch does: the launch is held to the base's context as its row recorded it, with lead and brief beside it ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)). A base no capped window can ever carry is not continued, and a first launch refused below that figure **parks the seat's mail on it** until a window has room ([Budgets and Spend](../guides/budgets-and-spend.md#budget-windows)).

**What starts fresh.** A conversation's first turn, and one whose every earlier session was released, absorbed or aged out (not logged). Logged as `executor_session_not_continued`: no conversation key, the switch off, a failed read; no member of the seat's chain that restores the base, or a launch on a member running another harness; a base no window can carry; a begin the log did not hold; a box whose harness cannot take the session up, an object the store no longer holds, a restore that fails in the box; a launch that reuses its turn's earlier box.

**A turn of a conversation that ends in its own frame leaves its ending too.** A turn that never launched and ended without an error (refused at the delegation cap), and a first launch abandoned once its record was written, record their end from the dispatching frame ([How a turn ends on the executor log](turn-engine.md#how-a-turn-ends-on-the-executor-log)), so the next turn is told how they ended and an abandoned launch's hold lifts at once. A turn whose frame failed before it launched records none: its delivery is handed back, to be parked or run again.

**Siblings are told and absorbed, never continued.** A turn that ran beside the head and ended with a session of its own is told how it ended and absorbed by the turn's end; no launch holds or opens it.

## Setup steps — provisioning the box

A harness's box needs wiring beyond the harness: git auth, registry credentials, toolchains. Provisioning is a declarative **setup-step** framework (`internal/sandbox/setup.go`); each `sandbox.SetupStep` contributes:

- `files`: content written into the box, at paths that are not shell-expanded but are cleaned in every cell (a trailing `/` or `.` segment names the same file). A relative path or one starting `~/` is under the box's home in every cell (`.npmrc`, `~/.config/tool.toml`).
  - A box writes only inside its home (a `direct` box's is minted per box, so no absolute path names it; a `container` box's is its mount at `/home/user`); a step that must put a file elsewhere has a command do it, with whatever rights that box's commands run with. A document whose step writes a file a seat's box would refuse is **refused when it is written**, naming the step, path and seat (see [Local sandboxes](#local-sandboxes)).
- `commands`: shell commands run after the files land. A non-zero exit **fails the acquisition** and tears the box down, so a half-provisioned box never gets a brief promising an environment it lacks; its status says whether a wait clears the failure (75 does, below). Each runs at most its step's `timeout_seconds` (ten minutes unless set); steps run one after another, the harness's install first, however long together. The launch stamps the box's keepalive every 15 s as the completion poll does, so another launch's orphan sweep never takes it and only a command's own timeout ends a slow one;
- `env`: variables merged into the harness's run env (`${VAR}`-resolved with the rest);
- `optional_keys`: keys of the step's `env`, and paths of its `files`, whose value may resolve to nothing: such a variable is left out and such a file not written, quietly, where any other reference resolving to nothing is left out and logged as a gap at the run's start, `sandbox_env_unresolved` (see [Credentials and the run environment](#credentials-and-the-run-environment));
- `brief`: a paragraph folded into the harness's "## Your environment" block, one of its [standing instructions](#what-a-harness-is-told), *telling* it what the step made true.

Steps come **from company config**, applied in order: `providers.sandbox.setup` (engine-wide, every agent seat's box) then `role.sandbox.setup` (the seat's extras). The engine ships none of its own for any other host, git auth included. The exception is a repository on Gitlet, which a run is *granted*: the engine's commands that clone it are answered by the `code_checkout` that grants it, never applied as setup (see [Repositories on Gitlet](#repositories-on-gitlet)). Setup commands run **with the launch's environment** (the run env plus what the engine minted for this job), so a recipe can read `$CREWLET_AGENT_HANDLE`, `$CREWLET_AGENT_EMAIL` and its own configured tokens. The run's telemetry endpoint is the exception: minted as the job starts, it reaches the harness alone. A reused box skips re-apply, except for a file holding the seat's GitHub App token, which its launch brings up to date before the job starts ([below](#the-git-auth-recipe)); a repository on Gitlet it does not hold yet is one `code_checkout` away.

**A command's status says who clears its failure.** A failed setup command is one an administrator must fix (`configuration`), whatever its status, 124 included (`timeout_seconds` ran out), but one: **75**, `EX_TEMPFAIL` (`sysexits.h`: temporary failure). Exit 75 says a download failed for now, which a wait clears (`setup_unavailable`, see [When a run does not start](#when-a-run-does-not-start)). Only the command knows which failures a wait clears: retry a fetch where it fails, so a blip never fails the step, and exit 75 only when, after those retries, the service still answers that it is failing on its side (a 408, a 429 or a 5xx). Never put `|| exit 75` on a whole command: it says a wrong pin, refused credential or blocked network will clear by waiting, and in a pipeline it binds to the command before it alone, so `curl … || exit 75 | sha256sum -c -` never checks a download that succeeded. [Recipe 1](#bring-your-own-image) does both for npm and `curl`. A failure classed `configuration` twice in a row pauses its seat until a person resumes it or the setting changes ([Agent runtime § Pausing a seat](agent-runtime.md#pausing-a-seat)), so a download that fails for now without exit 75 pauses the seat.

Every step has a `name`, unique within its list: it is what a setup failure points at, and what a config read masks a step's `env` and `files` (credentials) under and [sending the read back restores them by](configuration.md#reads-and-export). A document with two steps of one name in one list is refused on every write; the same name in `providers.sandbox.setup` and a seat's `sandbox.setup` is fine. A config read shows a step's `env` and `files` values only when each is exactly one `${VAR}` reference.

**A file is content, and it reaches the box as written.** A step's `env` is a setting: `${VAR}` in it is expanded at launch with the run environment. A file's body is written as is: a `${…}` inside belongs to whatever reads the file in the box (the shell, npm reading `.npmrc`), and the engine never expands one. The exception is a body that is **exactly one** `${VAR}`: it names the whole file, and the box receives the variable's value (secret store first, then the engine's environment) byte for byte. So `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}` in an `.npmrc` is left for npm to expand from the `NPM_TOKEN` the step's `env` provides, while `.npmrc: "${NPMRC}"` writes the whole stored file into the box's home. A whole reference that resolves to nothing (unanswered or empty) is never written as an empty file: it is not written, and the run starts with the gap logged (`sandbox_env_unresolved`, naming `<step>:<path>`) as an unresolved `env` value is ([below](#credentials-and-the-run-environment)), or quietly where the step lists the path under `optional_keys`. The same holds on a seat's own `sandbox.setup`. A file whose whole body is the seat's GitHub App token, left out because the app could not issue one yet, is written by the first poll after it can ([The git-auth recipe](#the-git-auth-recipe)).

**A tool a step installs for the run goes in `$HOME/.crewlet/bin`**, which the run's wrapper puts first on the harness's PATH (inside the login shell, after the profile, so a profile cannot replace it). It is under the home because a `direct` box runs as the engine's unprivileged user, and two boxes would overwrite each other's tools in a system path.

### The git-auth recipe

A headless `git clone https://github.com/...` cannot *supply* an injected token and dies with `could not read Username`. The recommended wiring is a credential helper plus rewrites, shipped as an ordinary engine-wide step:

```yaml
providers:
  sandbox:
    setup:
      - name: git-auth
        commands:
          - mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
          - |
            cat > "$HOME/.local/bin/git-credential-crewlet" <<'SH'
            #!/bin/sh
            [ "$1" = "get" ] || exit 0
            token="$GITHUB_TOKEN"
            file="$HOME/.config/crewlet/github-token"
            [ -s "$file" ] && token=$(cat "$file")
            [ -n "$token" ] || exit 0
            ok=""
            while IFS= read -r line; do
                [ -z "$line" ] && break
                [ "$line" = "host=github.com" ] && ok=1
            done
            [ -n "$ok" ] || exit 0
            echo "username=x-access-token"
            echo "password=$token"
            SH
          - chmod +x "$HOME/.local/bin/git-credential-crewlet"
          - 'git config --global credential."https://github.com".helper "!''$HOME/.local/bin/git-credential-crewlet''"'
          - 'git config --global --add url."https://github.com/".insteadOf "git@github.com:"'
          - 'git config --global --add url."https://github.com/".insteadOf "ssh://git@github.com/"'
          - 'git config --global user.name "$CREWLET_AGENT_HANDLE"'
          - 'git config --global user.email "$CREWLET_AGENT_EMAIL"'
        env:
          GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: "0"
        brief: >-
          When a GitHub token is available, git authenticates to github.com
          with it automatically: clone, fetch and push over plain HTTPS, SSH
          remotes are rewritten, and the token is read fresh at every call, from
          $HOME/.config/crewlet/github-token or else $GITHUB_TOKEN. For the gh
          harness, pass the current token on each call: GH_TOKEN="$(cat
          "$HOME/.config/crewlet/github-token" 2>/dev/null || printf %s
          "$GITHUB_TOKEN")" gh pr create ... Without a token, public
          repositories still clone anonymously and nothing you push is
          accepted. Never embed a token in a URL or print it. Your git commit
          identity is preconfigured.

```

A seat on at GitHub needs nothing more: Crewlet puts its app's token in its box
as `GITHUB_TOKEN` and in `$HOME/.config/crewlet/github-token`, the file the
helper reads first ([An agent's own integration credentials](#an-agents-own-integration-credentials)).

**The token is the agent's own GitHub App's**, issued at launch and good for at least 50 minutes in the environment ([Acting as the app](../integrations/github.md#acting-as-the-app-the-seats-token)). A run outlives its token and a process's environment cannot change, but a file can: the box's token file, and any setup file whose whole body is the seat's `${GITHUB_APP_TOKEN_<HANDLE>}`, is rewritten by the completion poll each time the token is renewed (its launching node's poll), and by the launch of a job continuing in its turn's kept box, before it starts. No poll reaches a box paused for the reviewer or a person's answer, and a kept box runs no setup. So the helper, reading the file at every git call, always offers an accepted token.
- Each renewed token is **recorded before the file is written**, beside the run's record, so it is scrubbed from every capture of the run's session taken once its job has ended ([Each launch's session, kept](#each-launchs-session-kept)); a renewal the record does not take is written by a later poll.
- The file is **replaced whole**: the new token is written beside it under a fresh name and renamed over it, so the helper never reads an empty or half-written file.
- A run launched before the seat's app was installed starts without token (`sandbox_env_unresolved`) and file; the first poll after the app can issue one writes it.
- The helper falls back to `$GITHUB_TOKEN` where the box has no file: the shape for a seat off at GitHub that declares a personal access token (one that does not expire within the run) in its `role.sandbox.env`.

Each piece is load-bearing:

- The helper is **scoped to the code host twice** (the credential config key *and* the `host=` check), so the token is never offered to a foreign host such as a malicious submodule URL.
- It reads the token at git-runtime, from the file or else the env, and stays silent without one, so public clones fall through to anonymous.
- The `insteadOf` rewrites use `--add` because the key is multi-valued: otherwise the second value replaces the first and scp-style `git@…:` remotes stay SSH, failing host-key verification in a keyless box.
- Commit identity comes from the generic `$CREWLET_AGENT_*` facts, so commits attribute to the seat without a hardcoded name.
- An engine-wide step reaches every agent seat's box, tokenless seats included, so its `brief` is written for both; promising every box a token would send a tokenless run pushing with nothing to push as.
- The helper lives in the **box's home**, the one place every cell lets a setup step write it (see [Local sandboxes](#local-sandboxes)), and is written by a command, not a `files:` entry: git needs the helper's absolute path, which only the box's shell knows (`"$HOME"`), and it must be made executable.
- It is registered as a shell snippet with a quoted path, `"!'$HOME/…'"`, because git runs a helper's value through the shell and a box's home may hold a space: a `direct` box's sits under `local.state_dir` (default `~/.crewlet/sandboxes`), and a relative one, like the examples' `./nimbus-data/sandboxes`, resolves against where the engine was started.

So the one step works in every cell.

The GitLab form (same shape, `gitlab.com` scoping, `oauth2` username, MRs opened via `git push -o merge_request.create` push options) is in [GitLab Integration](../integrations/gitlab.md#how-code-authoring-works); the block above is the GitHub form, and [GitHub Integration](../integrations/github.md#how-code-authoring-works) covers the rest of a GitHub seat's code authoring. The repo to work in is task context, not role config: the turn's ask names it, and the run clones it in the box with the seat's injected token. This recipe is for **other hosts** only: a repository on Gitlet is given to a run by the engine, never by a recipe (next section).

---
## Repositories on Gitlet

A run can be given repositories on [Gitlet](gitlet.md), the engine's own git host (`code.backend: gitlet`). Unlike a GitHub or GitLab repository (task context the turn's ask names, cloned with a token the seat's configuration declares), a Gitlet repository is a **grant**. A run is launched with none. Its agent calls `code_checkout` over [the tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box), one repository a call. The engine resolves it for the seat and writes it on the run's record before the call answers: the repository's id beside its name (a rename cannot move the grant), the commit the run starts from, the branch it works on, whether it may push (`read` or `write`), and an optional cone of directories.

- The record judges the box's access to Gitlet on every request while the job runs: a repository is reachable from its checkout's answer on, and one never checked out never is.
- It binds the box's **git** only. Calls of the seat's own tools through [the tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box) are the seat's, held to the seat's grant and a person's stop whatever the run was given.
- Limits: 8 repositories per run; a cone names at most 64 directories, each relative to the repository's root, clean, at most 255 bytes. A checkout past them is refused before anything is written.
- A run that carries on after a person's answer (in the asking job's box, or from its branch in a fresh one) keeps its job's checkouts; any other later launch of the turn starts with none.
- The record also keeps the code-log position each checkout was resolved at, which only moves forward.
- Checking out again on the same branch with the same access answers the held grant, for a box that lost its clone: commands cloning the branch where it stands now (its head, with whatever the job before pushed, at a position the record's floor is raised to), or, where nothing was pushed and the branch does not exist, the commit the first checkout started from. Another branch or access is refused: one run works on one branch of a repository.

**What a checkout names.** `code_checkout` is offered on the run's own surface, beside `ask_and_wait`, where the company hosts code. It takes one repository, `{repo, base, branch, access, paths, change, open_change}`, every key and type read strictly, and answers the commands that clone it into the box's working directory and the branch to work on:

| Field | What it is | Left out |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | The repository's name, as `code_list_repos` lists it. A name a rename left redirecting resolves to the current one | Required |
| `branch` | The branch the run works on, created at its base if absent | `seats/<handle>/<the item's key>` for the turn's work item (every run on one item shares a branch), or `seats/<handle>/run-<the last 12 hex digits of the turn's id>` for a turn on no item.
