A job parks on at most 15 calls, as many as its row's share for them holds at their widest, so a call that arrives while the calls the job is parked on and those still running that could park number 15 is not run: it is answered at once, as failed, "Too many calls are waiting on this run; this one was not run. END YOUR TURN NOW: you will be resumed with the results of the calls already running." where the job is parked already, and "Too many of this run's calls are running at once; this one was not run. Make it again once they have returned, if it is still needed." where none is parked yet. A node that takes the seat over counts the parks the row holds.

| Harness | Ceiling | Why (measured with the bridge's bound in its entry) |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code 2.1.310 | none | its `timeout` carries the bound; a 1040-second call was answered whole |
| Codex 0.171.0 | none | `tool_timeout_sec` carries the bound, honoured whatever progress flows; unset, Codex cuts a call at 300 seconds ("timed out awaiting tools/call after 300s") |
| Gemini CLI 0.70.0, Qwen Code 0.28.4, OpenCode 2.3.2, Copilot 1.0.114, Grok Build 1.0.92, Pi 1.6.0 | none | each server's timeout carries the bound; a 1040-second call was answered whole |
| Hermes Agent 0.23.3 | none | its server's `timeout` carries the bound (unset, Hermes cuts a call at 300 seconds); a 1040-second call was answered whole. Its transport drops a response silent for 300 seconds, but its calls carry a progress token, so the bridge's progress keeps it going |
| Muse Code 1.4.25 | none | `tool_timeout_sec` carries the bound; its calls carry no progress token, and its client waits out a silent response (1040 seconds, answered whole) |
| Kimi Code 2.7.2 | 300 seconds | its calls carry no progress token, so a response is silent until its answer, and Node's fetch drops one whose headers have not come in five minutes, whatever `toolTimeoutMs` says; parked at 270 seconds |

**A call sent again after its request was lost joins the call still running.** Kimi Code, its connection gone, sends the call again under an id of its own, and once more after that (measured on 2.7.2), so the tool would take effect each time. A call of the same tool with the same arguments, made on the same job's session while the first still runs and every request for it is gone (the box dropped the request it came on, or the harness cancelled it), runs nothing: it is answered with the first's answer, its own result or the answer the bridge gave before it, and the call is recorded once, as one its harness was handed. A duplicate made while a request for the first still waits is a call of its own, since a run may make one call twice on purpose.

**A job's session ends without waiting for its calls.** A job's session on the bridge ends when the run settles, parks on its question, is stopped, reclaimed or cut by its cap; a relaunch replaces its job; a recovery opens the same job again; or the seat leaves this node while its box runs on. That closes the box's MCP sessions, and the SDK's close waits for every request in flight and writes no answer once begun. So the end first answers every call whose tool is still running:

- where the run is over for the box: "This run has ended; this call is still running, so do not make it again. End your turn now.";
- where the box goes on with the seat's next holder or this node's new session for the same job: "This call is still running; do not make it again."

Neither says where the result goes. Neither is a failure (a model makes a failed call again, while this call's effect is still to come). The end waits at most five seconds for those answers to be written (plus that of a call whose tool returned just before, and every answer the session gave without running a call), then closes the sessions; a box that does not read its answer holds the end no longer. A seat handed on gives its lease back then, rather than waiting out the call, its box's next calls waiting for a holder meanwhile.

The call's tool runs on to its own end, held by the bridge under the run's own context (a node that stops waits for it once it has given its seats back: [Graceful shutdown](agent-runtime.md#graceful-shutdown)), and its one update is made once it returns, as [one nobody waited for](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session), where the run's log still takes it (its identity is on the log from before it ran: [What a run's record and its log keep](#what-a-runs-record-and-its-log-keep)). Every collection of the run, on whichever node, waits for that update before reading the log (below); an update after the run's ending deleted its record finds no record. A call whose entry was still being written as the session ended is answered that it was not run, failed, and never runs. The session that made a call holds the end's answer, never its result, which every continuation of its round built after it landed is told from the run's log (but one of a session that took it as an item: [A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). A call reaching a job's session after its end runs nothing and is recorded nowhere: where the run is over it is told to end its turn; where the box goes on, that the session was closing and to call again, which reaches the session serving the box now (a call reaching the session as its close begins gets the close's failure instead).

**A collection waits for its run's calls in flight.** Every collection of a run (its completion, a park on its question, the turn's cap cutting it, a job lost with its host and carried on, and the ending of a stop, a loss or a reclaim before it decides how the turn ended) first ends the job's session on the bridge to new calls, waits until the run's tool log holds no call of the round in flight, and only then reads it, so the turn's outcome, reviewer and tool log hold what such a call did (a work item it filed counts in the outcome). A park's collection ends the asking job's session too, so a later call from its box is refused, and the answer's relaunch opens a session of its own under its own job.

It waits on the run's log in the coordination store, watched rather than polled, never on the bridge's memory of its calls, so whichever node collects (the seat's next holder, after a handoff) waits alike. Each call is waited for until the first of:

- its update;
- the turn's wall-clock cap, where it has one (most have none);
- the call's own bound, carried on its entry: its tool's bound and a minute, from when the bridge took it;
- its process gone, read off the taker lease of the node process running it as it first appears and every two seconds after, so a crashed node's call is given up within that lease's lifetime (`coordination.lease_ttl_seconds`, 45 seconds by default) rather than at its bound; a node that drains keeps its lease until its calls are recorded, and is waited for.

A call still in flight when the wait stops is named at warning (`sandbox_calls_unfinished`) and read as a call whose outcome is unknown: listed in the round's record, failed, as `This call's outcome is unknown: its turn stopped waiting for it before its result was recorded, so what it did may have taken effect. Check whether it did before making it again.`, counted by its identity, told to a run carrying the round on beside its late calls, and beside it an ending reads the turn's delivery as unknown. Its update, landing later while the run's record stands, replaces the unknown for every later reader. An ending reached where it cannot wait (a completion's handler, a seat's acquisition) hands a run whose log holds a call still waited for to the node's own retry of the ending, which waits. A seat's retirement leaves such a run, its session ended, to its own next pass rather than wait among the seat's other runs, saying so at info, as a wait rather than a failure ([`seat_mailbox_retirement_waiting`](seat-ownership.md#the-removed-seat)). **What it costs**: the collection holds the run's seat while it waits, as the resumed turn does after it, up to the first of those bounds, so a turn whose run left a call running resumes only once that call is recorded or given up on; plus one watch of the run's log, and one read of each running node's lease as it first appears and every two seconds after.

**The credential is per-job and expires with the run.** The box holds no API token; a signed token in the endpoint's own path admits a request, the same shape the OTLP receiver uses (`internal/runtoken`). It names the run, the **seat** it acts as and its **job** (the launch id the store mints and keeps on the run's durable row), never a process, and is signed under the fleet's keyring. Two gates: the signature says this fleet minted it, and the session map on the node holding the seat says the job it names is still the run's, so a box that outlived its run keeps no working key, and a relaunch is a new job whose old box's token stops resolving. The session is opened as soon as the job is named and before any box exists, so a launch that cannot be served is refused with nothing started.

**Where a box dials it depends on its cell and its node.**

- A `direct` box is a process tree on its node's own host, so on every node that binds `api.port` it dials that node's own listener on loopback and needs no setting.
  - On an `ingress` node that is the listener the bridge is served on (`api.public.port` where set, `api.port` otherwise), so a single node with an API port runs the quickstart's company as written.
  - On a node without `ingress` it is `api.port`, where the node serves the bridge beside its probes to its own host's loopback alone (a caller from elsewhere meets the route's absence), so a seat pool with no address of its own runs its seats too, provided `api.host` takes every interface or a loopback address.
- Every other box (a `container` box, which does not share its node's loopback, or a `direct` box on a node with no such listener, `api.port: 0`) dials `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL`, set on every node to the fleet's bridge address as the sandbox reaches it (below). A loopback one reaches a `container` box under the runtime's name for the engine host ([Local sandboxes](#local-sandboxes)), which on Linux needs the API to listen beyond loopback.

The bridge takes a call under whatever `Host` it arrives with, because the token in its path is the credential and a page cannot make one: a reverse proxy or tunnel agent on the engine host that connects to the node on `127.0.0.1` and passes the public `Host` on (as ngrok, cloudflared and Caddy do unless told otherwise) reaches it as a directly dialling box does, on its MCP endpoint and the run's notes route alike. A launch whose box has no address to dial is refused naming what to set (`api.port` on an `ingress` node that binds no listener for the route, the variable for a cell it is missing for), and each such cell is said once when a company is applied (`executor_bridge_unreachable`), before any turn is refused for it. A box dialling that variable reaches a node without `ingress` through the ingress nodes, whatever that node's own `api.port`. The phases on this host need none of this: their runs reach their tools through a socket, with no listener.

**A bridge address a box cannot use refuses the boot.** A `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL` that is not an absolute `http://` or `https://` URL a box can use refuses the node's boot, naming the variable and never repeating the value. Usable means: a host a URL parser accepts (a name, or an address with no zone; an unfilled `<host>` placeholder or a mistyped IPv4 address such as `10.0.0.300` is refused), a port from 1 to 65535 if it names one, and no user information, query or fragment. Otherwise every minted endpoint would be undialable and every tool call of every run would fail inside the box with nothing to say why. Plain `http://` is accepted; its cost is in [Security model](#security-model).

**Every bridged call acts as the run's seat.** The token is the credential, so the caller is the seat the run belongs to, with the same identity and four grants a turn's phases on this host carry, and the [authority table](identity-and-access.md#the-authority-table-one-function-decides) decides a bridged `list_work_items` exactly as it decides the native one. The bridge sets it itself rather than reading it off the request, because `/mcp/` is exempt from the credential guard, which resolves a box presenting nothing as anonymous (or, in a development build started with `-dev-principal`, as that principal). Neither may decide a seat's tool call, so the bridge replaces the request's answer with the seat's on this route only. A session whose tool surface is bound to no seat is refused at `Open`.

**Every call is written down where a resume can read it.** A phase on this host keeps its calls in memory and the turn writes them at the end; a bridged run's calls come from a process outside the engine, minutes apart, possibly across a restart. Each is appended to the run's tool log, kept in the coordination store beside the run's record ([below](#the-runs-record-and-what-it-costs-to-read)), with its order, start time, duration and answering server (a call refused once the run's tools had closed included). The log is bounded, dropping from the *middle*, since how a run began and ended explain it. A resume orders the calls by the order they reached the session. A call that finishes only after a relaunch that carried the round on has opened the log to the next job is written down too, as a call of the round, marked late, its cost charged to no job ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). Without that, the reviewer of a resumed run judges a turn with no tool log, which the delivery check reads as a turn that acted on nothing.

- **Identity**: the digest of the call's whole arguments the run's call log admitted it under, taken by the bridge before anything is recorded; a resumed segment counts the call by it. The log keeps a call's arguments and answer to the call's share of the log, and a long run's middle only as identities ([what a run's record and its log keep](#what-a-runs-record-and-its-log-keep)), so neither a cut argument nor a dropped call moves the operation id a later call derives.
- **The harness's id** (`call_id`): Claude Code gives every call the model's `tool_use` id, in the request's `_meta` under `claudecode/toolUseId`, the id its own session record files the call under (measured on 2.1.310, main thread and subagents, tool-search-loaded tools included). The bridge reads it under the key the box's runner declares and no other, and records it on the call's entry and record alike, whole or not at all: an id over 64 bytes, holding anything but letters, digits, `-` and `_`, or not a string, is recorded as none, never cut, since two ids cut alike would name two calls as one. It is the harness's word and no part of the call's identity: the record finds its entry without it, and two calls under one id are two calls. OpenCode sends no id, so its calls carry none, nor does a skill load a harness's hook reports, nor a call a person approved, which no harness made over the bridge.

**One address for the fleet; the seat's holder answers.** A session is a live tool surface in the process holding the run's seat (its MCP children, skill guard, recording), so only that process can answer a call, but the box need not dial it. `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL` is the **fleet's** address: any node that serves the API (the `ingress` role), a load balancer in front of several included, the same value on every node. The node a call lands on reads the seat's lease, which the token names, and relays the whole HTTP exchange (event stream included) to the holder over the broker (`internal/httprelay`), which answers from its own session. So a node without `ingress` (one serving its network its probes and nothing else, a [satellite](../guides/satellite-nodes.md) at the edge of a network included) runs agent seats as well as one that serves the API: nothing a box dialling the fleet's bridge address needs is a route on it, and its own `direct` boxes dial it on loopback (above). A call for a seat that node has since handed on is relayed to the new holder from there, as from any `ingress` node.

With Tier A `api.public.port` set, the route is served on the ingress nodes' public listener instead of `api.port`, so the bridge URL names the public port and a direct box dials it there ([Exposing webhooks without the admin API](../guides/deployment.md#exposing-webhooks-without-the-admin-api)). The token is signed from Tier A `secrets.keys`, under a domain separating bridge tokens from telemetry tokens. Every node holds that keyring (a node without one does not start), so any node can tell a fleet-signed token from a forged one before relaying, and a keyring that cannot sign for the fleet is refused by name when the bridge is built. Every relayed request and every frame of its answer is signed under that keyring ([ADR-0031](../../adr/0031-every-state-log-record-is-signed.md)), because the broker authenticates nobody and both are instructions.

**A call waits for a holder that can answer it.** A call that lands while no node can answer (the holder has died and its lease not yet run out, or a peer has the lease and is still taking the seat) waits, reading the lease again, for up to two seat-lease lifetimes (90 seconds at the default `coordination.lease_ttl_seconds`): one for a dead holder's lease to lapse, one for a peer to claim the seat and open its running jobs' sessions. Outcomes:

- A holder that has finished taking the seat and holds no session for the job answers `401`, as for any run that is over.
- No holder found within the bound: `503` with a `Retry-After`, never that the run is over, which nobody said.
- A call a holder took as the seat left it (released between taking and serving): also `503`; the run goes on with the seat's next holder, which the box's next call reaches.
- A request that opens an MCP session (a harness's `initialize`) which reached the run's session on its node just as that session ended there (the run ended, the seat left, or a recovery opened the job again): also `503`, never `400 no server available`. Its next try is routed afresh, to the session serving the box now, or refused where the run is over; a request naming a server the session does not serve keeps its `400`. The bridge does not route it again itself: the `503` fires only where the session ended between the routing that found it and the request's hold on it.
- A holder that took a call and stopped answering before writing a status: `502`, and the call is not offered to another node, since it may have run.

**What a box does with the `503`**, measured on Claude Code 2.1.310 and 2.1.322, which behave alike and read no `Retry-After`:

- A request opening a session at the box's startup is made again three times, about 0.5, 2 and 6 seconds after the first; the server is given up for the run where all three meet a `503`.
- One opening a session again after the box's session was lost mid-run is made five times within about fifteen seconds (at once, then 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds apart), then up to eight more times in the background over the following minutes while the answer stays `503`.
- A call that meets a `503` is not made again: the model's call fails, a hook's call is a hook error the run goes on past, and the CLI keeps the server and its session, so the model's next call is routed afresh. (A `400` there was never retried at startup, leaving the box without its tools for the run.)

**A run outlives a restart, or a move, of the node that holds its seat.** The token names the job, not a process, so whichever node takes the seat over (the same node after a restart, or a peer) re-opens the run's session as it recovers the seat, before the seat's mailbox opens: the surface is rebuilt from the run's own row (the tools and skills it launched with, and the skills it loaded over the bridge), with its call log and bridged calls' cost carried over. Only once the seat's running jobs are recovered does the node answer that a job it holds no session for is over. The node that hands the seat on ends its runs' sessions as it releases the seat, so the box's next request is routed afresh to the new holder. The box's MCP session lived on the node that let it go, so its next request there is answered `404`, which the MCP protocol answers by connecting again, through the same URL, to the new holder, with the unchanged token. A session that cannot be re-opened logs `bridge_not_reopened` and never fails the recovery. A run whose ending is already decided is not re-opened, nor is one on a seat whose pause asks for its running work to stop: the node taking that seat ends the run as it recovers it (see [Stop now](agent-runtime.md#pausing-a-seat)), so its box never gets the seat's tools back in between.

## A run's own skills

A seat's [Tool Skills](tool-skills.md) reach its executor as its harness's **own skills**, never as a catalogue in its prompt ([why](tool-skills.md#the-executors-skills-are-its-harnesss-own)): every launch hands the run the skills its phase matches, and the harness lists each to its model by name and description and hands over the text when the model loads it with its own skill tool. Each is listed as `crewlet:<name>` on both harnesses, so a refusal names the skill to load whichever harness runs:

- **Claude Code** is handed them as a plugin of the run's own, `crewlet`, started with `--plugin-dir` (`<home>/.crewlet/claude-skills`): a `SKILL.md` per skill, and one `PostToolUse` hook on the `Skill` tool, an `mcp_tool` hook that calls the bridge's `skill_loaded` with the loaded skill's name, the way the run's [hooks](#claude-codes-hooks) take its notes, so nothing else reaches the box: no credential, no URL to allow, no program. `skill_loaded` is never listed, so no model can call it to unlock a skill it never read. Claude Code 2.1.118 is the first release that runs an `mcp_tool` hook; on an older one a run with a required skill is refused before the harness starts (every tool the skill covers would be refused for the whole run), and any other run starts without its skills, which its error stream says. A run that starts the plugin keeps [every run's settings](#a-claude-code-runs-session), or its [notes' settings](#claude-codes-hooks) where it starts those too. A box whose settings switch hooks off would silently drop the plugin's hook, so no load would be reported and a required skill would never unlock: such a run is [refused before it starts](#claude-code), naming the file and the key.
- **OpenCode** is handed them as a directory its configuration's `skills` names (`<home>/.crewlet/opencode-skills`), one directory per skill named as listed (the id OpenCode loads a skill by), and a second plugin of the run's own, beside the [notes plugin](#opencodes-notes-plugin), that posts each completed `skill` load to the bridge's skill route (`POST /mcp/{token}/skill`, [the API reference](../reference/api-endpoints.md#routes)) from an `execute.after` hook OpenCode waits for, so the load is on record before the model's next request.
- **Codex** is handed them as `<home>/.codex/skills/crewlet:<name>/SKILL.md`, which Codex lists whatever its configuration, and its note helper reports each load: Codex reads a skill's file through its shell, and the helper sees that command complete off the app-server.

The bridge records each reported load as the run's own `load_tool_skill` call of the skill's key, which the [required-skill guard](tool-skills.md#required-skills--load-before-use-enforcement) unlocks by and every later segment of the run replays, and it lists no `load_tool_skill` to the run: its harness's own tool is the loader. A skill the run was not handed (the checkout's own, or the image's) loads as the harness loads any and is recorded nowhere. The names a launch handed are kept on the parked turn, so a node that reopens the run's session after a restart or seat move reads a reported load by them too. Both directories are the run's, rewritten at every launch and cleared before it, so a box never lists a previous run's skills.

A skill's text is the harness's own skill: Claude Code reads it as a template, in which a line's `` !`command` `` runs as the skill loads and `$ARGUMENTS` is a placeholder, and OpenCode hands it to its model as written.
## Notes to a running run

A person can [steer](turn-engine.md#steering-a-running-turn) a turn while its
executor works in its box. From the executor's launch until its turn ends, the turn's notes
wait on the **run's record** in the coordination store, each sealed under the
fleet keyring by the node that filed it, beside a sealed anchor naming the seat
the run serves ([ADR-0067](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0067-a-note-to-an-executor-waits-sealed-on-its-record.md)).
The run reads them at four kinds of step, and every read is recorded on the
record: by the write that hands the note over, or, for a note a Claude Code
hook handed over, once the job's own session shows the hook took it (below)
— so no two reads hand a model the
same note (a session that may not show the notes it read is told them again
when it is continued, as notes it may already show: [A relaunch continues the
turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)), and the record's read
notes are exactly what the turn carries into its review, whichever node resumes
it:

- **Its brief.** A note waiting when a run is launched — the first one, a
  relaunch the reviewer sends back, or the one that carries a person's answer —
  goes into the brief, read by the write that opens the job.
- **Between its steps, through its tool bridge.** The run's bridge serves its
  notes to its harness two ways, behind the run's own token and nothing else:
  - **`steer_take`**, a tool on the run's MCP server that a harness's hook calls
    after a batch of the main agent's tool calls (`PostToolBatch`) or as the
    run is about to finish (`Stop`). It is **never listed**, so no harness offers it
    to its model, and it is answered before the seat's surface sees the call,
    so it is never recorded on the run's ledger: it is the harness asking, not the
    model. Its answer is always text — the hook's answer, with the notes as its
    additional context, or empty for nothing — and **never an error**, because a
    hook whose call is answered with an error makes the harness drop and
    re-initialise the run's whole bridge (measured on Claude Code 2.1.263 and
    2.1.310), where one the bridge turns away with a `503` is a hook error the
    run goes on past, the bridge kept (measured on 2.1.310 and 2.1.322). Only
    the main agent's loop takes notes: a subagent's batch, and a hook whose
    agent id the harness did not fill in, take nothing, because a note handed
    to a delegated loop binds that piece of work alone. One answer
    carries the oldest waiting notes within **9,000 UTF-16 code units**, measured
    as the harness measures its context, and the rest wait for the next step; it is
    answered within **five seconds**, half the hook's timeout, or not at all.
    **A hook's answer only serves its notes.** Each note it carries is first
    recorded **served** to the run's job, in a write before the answer that
    keeps the hook's call and names the answer's own take, and is recorded read
    only once the job's own session shows the hook took it, when the job's box
    is read: at its collection, or a stop's or a loss's read ([Claude Code's
    hooks](#claude-codes-hooks)). Meanwhile no later step of the job is served
    it, and it no longer counts among the five notes that may wait. A serve the
    store has not answered within the five seconds is answered with nothing and
    removed, by the job's next serve or off the hook's path (below), so its
    notes wait for the next step. A serve the harness gave up, its call
    cancelled or its request abandoned, is lost to the cancel, and its notes
    are served again at the job's next step, unless the job's session shows the
    hook took them all the same. A note is served to one job **three times** at
    most ([`steer_serve_bound`](#failure-modes)), and past that waits for the
    review or the next launch's brief (a late call's item, for the next launch,
    whose continuation tells the call); one served after a note filed later was
    handed over says it was sent before that one, which stands where the two
    disagree. A take still under way as the run's session on
    the bridge ends is answered before that session closes, as a call still
    running is: the end waits for a hook's answer to be written
    ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)),
    for as long as the harness waits for it. A hook the harness gave up on, or
    whose connection failed, is waited for no longer: nobody reads its answer.
  - **The notes route**, `/mcp/{token}/steer/notes?after=<seq>`,
    `/mcp/{token}/steer/read`, `/mcp/{token}/steer/again` and
    `/mcp/{token}/steer/folded` (ids alone, for the second admission of a note
    a compaction folded and for the notes a plugin gave up), which a plugin
    inside the harness polls: a poll is
    held for up to **ten seconds** while no note waits, and answered at once
    when one arrives. Once the node is stopping, or the session's opening has
    ended, a held poll is let go and every later one turned away with a `503`
    and a `Retry-After` — never an empty answer a poller would ask again at
    once — and its notes wait on the record for the session's next opening, on
    this node or the seat's next holder. That holds as well for a poll the
    stopping node is relaying to another node that holds the session: the
    stopping node lets go of it at once rather than wait out the holder's hold
    on its listener's grace. And it holds for a poll or a read that reaches the
    opening just as it ends, which is turned away the same way, to ask again,
    and never answered as a run with no notes route (`404`): that ends the
    harness's plugin for the rest of the run, and a run that goes on, its
    seat moved or its session opened again, would take no more notes between
    its steps. Every note a poll answers is first recorded
    **served** to the run's job on the run's record, in a write before the answer,
    so a note its harness may deliver is never one the record says nothing of;
    one the record could not mark is not answered, nor is any after it — the
    plugin's cursor moves past every note it is answered — and they wait for the
    next poll.
    A read names the notes
    (one to twenty-four: a turn's ten notes and up to fourteen items meant for the
    job alone, ten late calls and four wakes)
    the harness put in front of its model, and is recorded read at the
    run's next step. A read the session's end overtakes on its way to the notes is
    turned away to ask again too, never answered done with nothing recorded: the
    plugin would never confirm those notes again, and the turn's ending would
    report them unconfirmed though they were delivered. So is a read on a run
    whose tools are closed, which takes nothing more from its notes: a seat
    leaving the node closes its tools here before its release ends its session,
    and the read made again reaches the seat's next holder, which records it; a
    person's stop closes them too, and the run's end then refuses the read. And
    so is a read that reaches the notes once the job's completion has claimed
    the run, whose record then takes no read of the job while its session still
    serves: the read made again is recorded where the claim is handed back and
    the run goes on in its box, and refused once the run is over. And so is a
    read naming a note that still waits, sealed under a key the node serving
    the run's session does not hold, in a fleet whose nodes hold different
    keys: that node records the read's other notes, turns it away, and logs
    `steer_read_key_unknown` once for the note, which waits for a node that
    holds its key. The read made again is recorded once it reaches such a
    node, the run's seat moved or its session opened again there; a run that
    ends first leaves the note served and never confirmed, which its ending
    reports `unconfirmed` where the node ending the run holds the key; a node
    that does not records nothing of the note (`steer_note_end_unrecorded`).
    Each
    note carries an id the harness admits it under, unique to the note and the
    job, so a poller that admits it twice admits it once.

  A harness takes notes here only where its run is set up to ask for them; a run
  whose harness asks for none still has every note read, by its review. Every
  runner is set up to: **Claude Code** through [hooks](#claude-codes-hooks)
  that call `steer_take`, **OpenCode** through a [plugin](#opencodes-notes-plugin)
  that polls the notes route and hands each note to the run's session, and
  **Muse Code** through a [plugin's hooks](#muse-code) and **Grok Build** through
  [hooks in its settings](#grok-build), each running the note helper, which
  calls `steer_take`.

  A take is pinned to the run's **job** and to a run that is launching or
  working with its ending undecided: a relaunch's job, a run parked on a
  question, a collected run and a run whose tools are closed — its seat moved,
  or a person stopped it — take nothing, and their notes wait for whatever reads
  the turn next. The bridge itself decides nothing about notes; it routes the
  call, like every bridged call, to the node holding the run's seat, whose
  inbox for the run is rebuilt from the record — so a run whose node restarted
  is served its notes by whichever node reopens its session.
- **The review's first round.** A note the run never took is read by the
  segment that reviews the run, before its first provider call.
- **After its question is answered.** A run parked on a question takes nothing
  while it waits; `steer_turn` answers `reads: "after_answer"`, and the launch
  that carries the answer carries the notes.

**A take whose answer was lost is settled.** A take's write can land while its
answer does not — a `steer_take` the store answered after its five seconds, or
a review's take whose answer a broken connection lost — and the record then
says a step was handed a note it was never handed. So every take carries an
identity of its own, and one whose call answered an error is **settled** by
it, in one of two ways:

- **A hook's serve is removed.** The hook has been answered nothing already, so
  its serve is settled off its path, removed from every note it served, by the
  job's next serve in its own write where that comes first: the notes wait
  again, for the job's next step or its review, and the removed serve counts
  nothing toward their three. A serve its harness cancelled is settled the
  same way, lost to the cancel. The settle asks the
  coordination store until it answers,
  however long that takes, and says so once an attempt has failed and thirty
  seconds have passed ([`steer_take_unsettled`](#failure-modes)) — on a member
  at thirty seconds, and across a link at the slowest pace allowed up to about
  thirteen minutes and ten seconds in, since each attempt is given its ten seconds
  and the record's crossing; only the node stopping first ends
  it, once it has asked every take it holds once more — a take a segment the
  stop ends hands off among them — in a window of five seconds from the start
  of the stop's teardown, the stop's own with no crossing of the record beside
  it, since the stop's longest case sizes a pod's grace, beside the leases the
  stop gives back and never on their allowance, since a settle that runs out
  leaves a take unsettled rather than a lease lapsing.
- **A review's take is answered.** Its round is still waiting on it, so its
  take is settled on the review's own path, in answer mode, and what its write
  recorded is handed over there and then, never marked. Where the store answers
  that settle no more than it answered the take, the take is kept by the
  segment reviewing the run and settled again at its next round, or at the
  brief of a relaunch it makes, handing over what it recorded to whichever the
  store answers first — a brief's launch then records the note read by the job
  it opens, in the take's place, so the note is that job's as every other note
  its brief carries is, and keeps the take's own place among the turn's reads,
  where the brief tells it too: a note a later round read, a correction of it,
  is never told ahead of it; meanwhile, for thirty seconds, it stands for a note
  waiting, so a round asking for tools ends and the next one opens with the
  note. Only a take the store has still not answered when the segment ends is
  marked **unanswered**, as the segment ends: in the segment's own path first,
  so the run's ending, which reads the record next where the segment ended the
  turn, finds the mark and reports the note `missed`, and off its path where
  the store answers that attempt no more. A marked note stays read by the
  record's word, so no later take hands it over and the review read it
  carried, but no capture of the job's session counts it held, and every
  later launch tells it again in its brief, as notes it may already show: the
  fresh brief among every note the turn has read, and a continued session
  from the first marked read on. The launch's write records each one it tells
  again read by the job it opens, told again, at the marked take's own place
  among the turn's reads, so a capture of that job counts it held, and keeps
  the take's read beside the telling.

Either way, a settle that finds the take recorded nothing writes the record all
the same, so that take's write, should it still be on its way to the store,
can never land after it; and the notes wait for the next step. A launch reads
the marks off the record as its brief is written, so one landed after the
segment that launches resumed is counted all the same.

What became of each note is published as `agent_turn_steered`, the note redacted: `delivered` by
the node whose step read it, with the kind of step (`boundary`: `brief`,
`tool_batch`, `finish`, `step`, or `round` for the review) and, for a read by
the run, its job (`launch_id`); a note a Claude Code hook served, by the node
that read the job's box and found the hook took it, at the serve's step
(`tool_batch` or `finish`) and its job, under one id however often the box is
read. Every
note no step reported reading is reported
by the node that finishes the run's ending, as the record knows it, and by
nothing else, in this order:

- **`delivered`, told again** (`retold: true`), a note marked unanswered that a
  later launch's brief told again, where that launch's job started: at that
  brief (`boundary: brief`, its `launch_id`). The take that recorded it never
  handed it over; the brief did.
- **`unconfirmed`**, a note the run's bridge served to its job's harness that
  never confirmed it, and that no step read after: OpenCode's plugin never
  confirmed it, or a hook's job's session neither showed it taken nor proved
  it absent (a read of its thread could not decide, or its box was never
  read). At the hook's serve that was live, its step and job, or else at the
  job a poll served it to (`boundary: step`, its `launch_id`). Its session may
  hold it, and nothing says it does. So is a note every hook's serve of which
  its harness gave up past the hook's timeout, at the last of them: the answer
  can outrun the cancel.
- **`missed`**, a note a take whose answer was lost recorded read, marked
  unanswered, that no later launch whose job started was told: at the step that
  took it. The review after it, if one ran, read it carried. A note a later
  launch told again and whose job never started (the launch failed after
  writing the record) is `missed` too, at that take: the brief handed nothing
  over, and the record keeps the take's read beside the telling. And a note
  served to a job's hooks whose every serve was lost, one of them a serve its
  job's whole session proves it never took, and that nothing read since: at
  the last of those serves.
- **`expired`**, a note no job ran with: still waiting, or read first into the
  brief of a launch that failed after writing the record, whose job never
  started, at no step.

So a note served and then left to a lost take, or to the brief of a job that
never started, is `unconfirmed`, since a session may hold it. Each is published
before the record is deleted, under an id derived from the ending, so a retried
ending records it once. A park is never an ending. Whether a job started is on
that job's own record, written when its command is attached and kept when a park
or an expired pause lets its box go, so a note a started job's brief carried,
recorded `delivered`, is never then recorded `expired`.

**Every item keeps to characters every harness carries.** As the engine hands
a person's note, a late call's account, a wake or another run's message to a
model, every control character but tab and newline, and U+2028 and U+2029, is
shown as U+FFFD, one UTF-16 unit as each was, so no bound moves;
what the engine keeps stays as written. JSON then escapes nothing in an item
but the quote, the backslash, tab and newline, so an item of N units is at most
3N bytes beside its framing in a hook's answer or a poll's message.

**An item for one job: a call that outlived its wait.** A call of the round that
finished after the run that made it stopped waiting for it — a [late
call](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session) of a job a relaunch replaced, or
one the working job's own harness gave up on — is handed to the job working on
the round at its next request. The store files it on the run's record as an
**item** for that job alone, in the writes that decide the call is late or
nobody waited for it: the append that lists it, a record of an earlier round's
call included, and the opening of the log by a relaunch, for every call that
opening marks late past the read its briefs were built from, or carries into a
new round. Only while the record names that job launching or running and its
ending is undecided, at most ten a job, once a call however
often its append is asked; a filing refused or failed fails neither the append
nor the launch, and leaves the call to the continuations, which tell every late
call. An item is the log's account of the call, so it is **unsealed** and no
person's word: the engine routes it by its kind before opening any seal, never
hands it as anybody's note, and hands over nothing else that claims a call,
saying each once at error. It holds a copy of the call held to an ordinary
call's share (8 KiB of arguments, a failed call's error, no output of a
success), rendered under its own heading, `## A call the run that made it
stopped waiting for`, in the late calls' words as statements, the outcome
first and then the call as a brief draws it: every value and error past 200
characters omitted by size and digest, never cut, every line break in a tool's
text drawn as a space, and the whole neutralised under the session's fence
token. One too wide is drawn with its arguments omitted whole, so it always
shares one hook answer with a person's widest note. **Claude Code** is handed
items after a tool batch alone, a person's notes fitted first; **never at its
finish**, where a job makes no more calls and its review reads its report: the
item waits, and the next launch's continuation tells the call. **Muse Code**
is handed one item a hook, after a tool batch alone, read once its record shows
the hook's receipt. **Grok Build** is handed items after a tool batch, as many
as its 10,000 characters hold, read once its record shows them handed over.
**OpenCode** is served each as a message of its own at its
next poll, read once its plugin confirms it. Where the job's session is **known to hold** an item (its OpenCode
plugin confirmed it delivered, or its main thread shows its hook took it after
its last restart), that write records a **telling** of the call on the run's
record, at the write's own place among the reads: kept by every relaunch that
carries the round on, cleared with a new round, one a call, at most twenty. A
continuation is not told that call again where it continues a session holding
the telling: not cut off nor possibly a summary, its capture read after that
write (its note cursor at or past the place), and none of its briefs having
counted the call without listing it. Every other continuation still tells it,
under words that say an earlier message may have told it: a session cut off
or compacting, a cursor stopped lower by a person's unread note, a telling
past the twenty, a hook's take not yet shown, a call a hook took told to a box
whose Claude Code release's resume the engine has not read (which may not
rebuild what the hook handed the session). In a fleet mid-upgrade an older
node's brief or capture records no late call it counted without listing, so a
continuation of a session holding only that count may be credited a telling
of the call and not told it. An OpenCode
session that compacts holds an item as it holds every call (its compaction is
not judged yet, above). **What this does not reach**: a Claude Code job finishing as the call
lands is not handed it, so its report may say a call failed that ran, which its
reviewer reads beside the run's tool log; and OpenCode can be handed an item
after its final step, since nothing tells its plugin whether a step will call a
tool: the run then goes on, and its report is its answer after the item, which
the item's words say.

**An item for one job: a message about its work.** The engine can hand the
working job somebody's message about the work it is doing, which would
otherwise wait on the seat's held inbox for the run to end, as a **wake**: an
item for that job alone. The node holding the seat runs its **router** while
a run holds the seat: it reads the held inbox without consuming it, at once, on
each publish to the inbox or its lane, when the seat's dispatch goes idle and
at least every two minutes, and files each wake written by **the run's own
requester** (the same seat, credential and whom-for its turn works for) in the
run's conversation, about its work item, or about a record the run created or
wrote (below); another writer's message, a schedule's fire, a colleague's ask
or answer and a delegated review (each answered on a channel of its own), and
one the completion ledger has worked stay queued for turns of their own
(ADR-0167). Each wake is decided once per job (`crewlet.seat.wakes.routed`,
rule `conversation`, `work_item` or `wrote`). Only the engine files a wake,
while the record names the job launching or running with its ending undecided,
signed under the fleet keyring in a key domain of its own (`seat.wake.item`)
bound to the turn, the job and the wake, so no writer of the coordination store
can rewrite whose words it carries or whether it asks for an answer. Wakes filed between two of
the job's steps join its newest item while nothing has served it, at most four
an item and 8 KiB of seals; a job holds at most four items and a turn eight,
and a wake past either is left to a turn of its own. A Claude Code hook serves
an item **once**, after a batch or at the finish, where it may change the run's
report, and OpenCode at its next poll; one answer carries a person's notes
first, then wakes, then late calls. Each message opens with
`## A message from <writer> about this work, sent while this turn was running`,
then a line saying where it was written and whether it asks for an answer, then
the writer's words, at most a thousand characters, inside their
[fence](agent-runtime.md#text-somebody-else-wrote); an item past what one
answer carries beside a person's widest note keeps its newest messages whole
and says how many earlier ones it leaves out. **Once a read is confirmed**, by
the job's session showing its hook took the item or by OpenCode's plugin, the
engine records every delivery the wake stands for as worked by the turn in the
completion ledger, so it starts no turn of its own when the seat's inbox is let
go (its `turn_trigger_skipped` has the disposition `joined` and names the turn),
a person's line showing it queued behind the seat moves to the turn's, the
seat's [seen-through mark](event-system.md#inbox-batching--coalescing) for its
thread moves to its record, and the turn is held to the answer it owes as to
its own trigger's, by the delivery check and the review; and it publishes
`agent_turn_joined` `delivered`. A wake served and never confirmed, or never
served, is not recorded worked: its delivery runs as a turn of its own once the
run is over, and its job's end reports it `unconfirmed` or `unread`. A relaunch
removes the job's unread wakes; a read one is the turn's, kept for every later
launch, told to a fresh session and, as a message it may already show, to a
continued session that may lack it, as is one its job was served and never
confirmed. The review reads no wake.

**What the run wrote** is kept on its call log: each bridged call whose write
landed adds the record it wrote, named exactly as a wake about that record is.
A work item it filed, updated or commented on is named by `<backend>:<id>`; a
change it opened, edited, reviewed, commented on, rebased or merged, the
thread of a chat message it posted (a direct conversation's whole line), a page
it saved or commented on and an artifact it remarked on are named by the
conversation their wakes are stamped with. A review of the change the run
opened, a reply under its post or a comment on the item it filed reaches the
run instead of waiting. Reads, refused or failed writes and calls that
committed nothing add nothing, and neither does a push the box makes over git,
a change its collection opens or a held call a person approved, none of which
passes the bridge. The set lives as long as the call log, through a park, a
relaunch, a new round and a takeover, and holds 128 records; past them a record
is refused, none held is dropped, and the node says so once
(`sandbox_run_written_set_full`). The run's record keeps a key of each, by
which other seats' runs on that work find it ([A seat's runs see each
other](#a-seats-runs-see-each-other)); one a late call's write could not keep is
said (`sandbox_run_written_keys_unkept`) and kept by its next recorded call.

**Another writer's message about the work, and a lead's, is triaged.** A wake
the requester rule leaves that was written in the run's conversation, about its
work item, about a record the run wrote, or by somebody who [leads the seat](organization-model.md#management-hierarchy) is
described once per job by one call on the seat's `llm_triage` chain (falling
back to `llm`, then `default`): `input`, `steer`, `request` or `noise`. The
model only describes it; the engine decides (ADR-0168):

| Triage | What the engine does |
|---|---|
| `input` | Files it as a wake from anybody, its line adding that the writer is not whom the turn works for: information to read and, where it asks, answer where it was written, never a request to act on. Claimed at its read, as above. |
| `steer` | From a person the chart says leads the seat, files it as that lead's [note](turn-engine.md#steering-a-running-turn), several of their messages in one read as one note, oldest first; claimed at the filing (`joined`, naming the turn). While a note of theirs waits unread, their next messages wait to become the next note; past the turn's ten notes they stay. Anybody else's steer is a request. |
| `request` | From a person or an agent seat other than the run's requester, is put once per job to the people who may let it [fold into the running work](#folding-another-writers-request-in): the requester and the seat's leads. Until one approves it waits; approved, it joins as a steer note; refused, unanswered when the job ends, or with nobody to put it to, it stays for a turn of its own, held to its own writer. Anybody else's request (a credential's) stays. |
| `noise` | Absorbed (recorded worked by the running turn, `turn_trigger_skipped` disposition `absorbed` naming it) only when it owes nothing: no answer owed, not addressed to the seat, no question put to it. One that owes anything stays. |

A triage that decides nothing (no chain, a refusal, ninety seconds, an invalid
answer) leaves the wake queued, logged `seat_wake_triaged` and counted
`triage_failed`. A job triages at most sixteen wakes and a read four; each call
is charged to the seat's budget as the turn's `wake_triage` spend. Every other
wake waits with no call.

### Folding another writer's request in

A request from somebody the run does not work for never runs on the
requester's apps on its writer's word, nor on the model's: only on the word of
a person who may decide for that work ([ADR-0109](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0109-a-turn-somebody-woke-is-held-to-the-apps-they-use.md)'s
amendment "another writer's request joins only on approval"). The engine puts
it, once per job, as a **fold-in** on the run's record: who asked, their words,
the work it would join and whose apps it would run on, offered as *Add it to
the running work* or *Run it on its own*. It is put to the run's requester,
where a person holds that seat, and the people among the seat's leads (nearest
first, at most eight), never its asker; any lead of the seat and an
administrator may answer it too, as they may a run's question. It shows in each
one's decisions on the Inbox and is answered with `answer_executor` naming the
fold-in, which records the first answer on the run's record at once and tells
the seat's node to read it. A job asks at most four; past them a request stays.

- **Approved**, the request joins at the run's next step as a [steer
  note](turn-engine.md#steering-a-running-turn) under the approver's name,
  saying who asked and who approved, the asker's words in their fence. It is
  read from the message waiting on the inbox, never from the record's excerpt.
  It counts against the turn's notes; past the cap it stays. Its delivery is
  claimed at the filing (`turn_trigger_skipped` `joined`, naming the turn),
  and the answer it was owed binds the turn, answered where it was written.
- **Refused**, the request runs as a turn of its own once the running work
  ends, from the inbox it never left.
- **Unanswered when its job ends**, the question closes with the job: the next
  job's opening clears it, a late approval is told the work it would have
  joined has ended and the request runs as its own turn, and a later job asks
  afresh.

The router counts each as `foldin_asked`, `foldin_approved`, `foldin_refused`
or `foldin_expired` on `crewlet.seat.wakes.routed`, and logs
`seat_wake_foldin_asked`, `_approved`, `_refused` and `_expired` naming the
wake, the turn and the approver. A person whose message waits is [told why,
once](event-system.md#a-person-waiting-goes-first-the-priority-lane).

A proxy between the boxes and `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL` holds a poll open for
up to those ten seconds, so it needs a request timeout of at least fifteen —
see [Deployment](../guides/deployment.md).

### Claude Code's hooks

Every Claude Code run its launch wires to its turn's notes (every seat's executor
run) is started, on a release that reads them, with a settings file of its own,
`claude-settings-notes.json` in the box's work directory, written afresh at
`0600` and named with `--settings` in place of the [settings every run
has](#a-claude-code-runs-session), which Claude Code ranks above the repository's
own settings and below a managed policy. From 2.1.310 the run is handed its
pinned copy, `claude-settings-notes-pinned.json`, which holds the same and [the
pin of its compaction point and of what a resume loads](#a-claude-code-runs-session)
in an `env` block. The file holds two hooks, nothing else:

```json
{
  "cleanupPeriodDays": 36500,
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolBatch": [{"hooks": [{"type": "mcp_tool", "server": "crewlet", "tool": "steer_take",
      "input": {"event": "${hook_event_name}", "agent": "${agent_id}"}, "timeout": 10}]}],
    "Stop": [{"hooks": [{"type": "mcp_tool", "server": "crewlet", "tool": "steer_take",
      "input": {"event": "${hook_event_name}", "agent": "${agent_id}"}, "timeout": 10}]}]
  }
}
```

- **An `mcp_tool` hook**, a call of `steer_take` on the run's own `crewlet`
  server: it rides the bridge connection the run already holds, under its token,
  so there is no new credential, no URL to allow and nothing to run in the box.
  Its input is the two values the harness fills in, where an `http` hook would
  post every batch's tool calls; every way it can fail is non-blocking, where a
  `command` hook that exits 2 ends the loop. The server and tool names are the
  ones the bridge serves, filled in by the engine.
- **What the model sees**, measured on 2.1.263 and 2.1.310 against a stub model
  API: a note handed back after a batch is read after that batch's tool results
  and stays for the rest of the run; one handed back at `Stop` continues the
  turn, and the run's result is the answer given after it. **Where it sits
  depends on the model**: on 2.1.310, after a batch, a system message after the
  tool results for `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5`, and a system reminder
  at the end of the batch's last tool result for `claude-sonnet-4-5`; at `Stop`,
  a system reminder in a user message for all three. Each is headed
  `PostToolBatch hook additional context:` or `Stop hook additional context:`.
  The hook's transcript line reaches only the run's stream, shown in the run's
  transcript as `[steer] a note from ada reached the run`, never a request.
- **How a person's transcript shows it.** Each note, late call or message a hook
  handed the model reads once, off its firing's `hook_additional_context`
  record. The copies 2.1.310 and 2.1.322 write beside it (the record's rendered
  form, the request's blob, the hook's stdout and, at `Stop`, its summary) read
  as nothing.
- **How the session shows a note taken.** The hook's transcript line ends in its
  serve's own token, `[crewlet take <id>]`, which Claude Code records in the
  session's main thread and never sends the model; the live line leaves it out.
  - Measured on 2.1.310 and 2.1.322: a hook answered in time leaves three records
    chained after the batch or the finishing reply (the hook's answer, its line
    and its context) under one firing; one answered too late leaves a
    `hook_cancelled` record alone, and the harness sends `notifications/cancelled`
    for the call, which the bridge reads before anything else of the request so
    the note can be served again.
  - A read of the job's box at its end (collection, or a stop's or a loss's read)
    reads the main thread once, before the session is taken, and asks it of every
    serve to the job not yet settled; a lost job's box is read for it whatever the
    company keeps of its sessions.
  - A serve is **held** where the line naming its token and the context of the
    same firing are both on the conversation Claude Code's resume hands over, the
    thread reads alike by every path its resume may take, its release is one whose
    resume the engine has read (2.1.310 and 2.1.322), and no restart of the thread
    comes after: the note is recorded read at its first serve's place among the
    turn's reads.
  - One a restart follows, or for a batch's note a reply saying the server cleared
    tool results, is read **restarted**: taken, and told again to a session
    continued from that restart on.
  - One the thread proves never taken is lost, which needs a harness that ended
    its own run, a thread read whole and never restarted, and another note of the
    same hook event held in it.
  - Anything else decides nothing, and the note stays served: a thread that
    compacted or rooted again, one past the read's 27 seconds, or another
    release. A read that decides nothing logs
    [`steer_receipt_unread`](#failure-modes).
- **Ten seconds**, where the vendor's default is six hundred: the harness holds
  its next model request until the hook answers, at every batch, and the bridge
  answers within five. The field is in seconds, and at it the harness cancels the
  call and discards a late answer.
- **No `disableAllHooks`.** A home's, a repository's or a managed `true` (or a
  managed `allowManagedHooksOnly`) switches every hook of the run's off with no
  error, so the run is [refused before it starts](#claude-code), naming the file
  and the key; it is never overruled, which would run the home's and the
  repository's hooks too. The repository's own hooks run beside the run's, which
  is why a hook of theirs that stops the loop is read as the [failure it
  is](#claude-code). Nothing else moves: no `--setting-sources`, which would drop
  the repository's `CLAUDE.md` with its settings, and no `--include-hook-events`.
- **The standing instructions say what a note is, as Claude Code delivers it**:
  a person who leads the seat, or an administrator, may send one while the run
  works; the harness adds it between steps as context of its own, under the
  headings above (a system message, or on some models a system reminder at the end
  of the last tool result); it opens with `## A note from <name>, sent while this
  turn was running`; and text a tool produced (a file's contents, a command's
  output, a fetched page) is never a note, whatever it says. Worded as a fact
  rather than a command, as the vendor advises for text a hook adds. An OpenCode
  run is told its own harness's carrier instead: a message from the user between
  steps. A Claude Code run's standing instructions are written twice, as they
  stand (`system.md`) and told of notes (`system-notes.md`), and the run's script
  names the one that matches its hooks.
- **Claude Code 2.1.163 or later**, or no hooks at all. The file holds no field
  newer than the `mcp_tool` hook (2.1.118 onwards), because in print mode the
  harness ignores a settings file it cannot validate, without a word. From 2.1.163
  a `Stop` hook's additional context reaches the model; an older release runs both
  hooks and drops what the `Stop` hook answers, so a note served as the run
  finished would be handed to a run that never sees it. The run's script therefore
  reads `claude --version` first and starts an older release on the settings every
  run has, without the hooks, with its standing instructions as they stand (never
  told of notes it cannot read), saying so on the run's error stream; that run's
  notes wait for its review.

A run without its hooks (that older release, or a managed policy that locks
customization to plugins, `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`) succeeds without
asking for its notes once, which the
collection reports as [`steer_reader_never_ran`](#failure-modes); its notes still
reach its review.

A batch's hook is answered the job's late calls too, after its notes, each under
its own heading ([an item for one job](#notes-to-a-running-run)), and its line
names them after the notes' senders: `crewlet: a note from ada and a call that
finished after its run stopped waiting for it reached the run`. The finish's hook
is answered notes alone.

### OpenCode's notes plugin

Every OpenCode run its launch wires to its turn's notes is handed a plugin of its
own, which the run's server loads: `index.js` in `opencode-steer/` in the box's
work directory, written before the server starts and named in the run's
[configuration](#opencode) with the run's notes route as its one option, a
`{file:}` reference to a file under `opencode-values/` like every value there, so
the configuration holds no token:

```json
{
  "plugins": [{"package": "<home>/.crewlet/opencode-steer",
               "options": {"url": "{file:<home>/.crewlet/opencode-values/v<n>}"}}]
}
```

The plugin is the engine's own, embedded in the binary: plain JavaScript with no
imports, so nothing is installed or fetched to load it. The run's script hands
the server the id of the session the run works in, as `CREWLET_STEER_SESSION` on
`opencode serve` alone, and the plugin reads that session and no other:

- **It polls only while the session works**: from the session's
  `session.execution.started` (or any of its steps starting) to its `succeeded`,
  `failed` or `interrupted`, again for an execution OpenCode starts itself, so the
  brief is always the first thing the session reads. Its setup only registers and
  returns, since OpenCode holds every prompt until each plugin's setup resolves.
- **Each note is admitted as a steer**, under the id the route gives it
  (`ctx.session.prompt` with `delivery: "steer"`): OpenCode hands every steer
  waiting at its next step boundary to the model as a user message after that
  step's tool results, or after a final step that called no tool (whose boundary
  reads the inbox again), so a note sent while the run writes its answer is still
  read in the same run. The id is derived from the job and the note, so a note
  admitted twice is admitted once. The cursor moves past a note only once it is
  admitted.
- **With `resume: false`**, a note admitted once the session has settled starts
  nothing (an execution `opencode run` no longer watched would answer nobody),
  and the plugin admits none then anyway; it waits on the run's record for its
  review. One whose admission landed just as the session settled is left pending
  in the session, whose inbox outlives the server: a run carried on in the same
  session with a person's answer would be handed it ahead of its next prompt,
  beside the continuation brief's copy. So once `opencode run` has exited, and
  before the server stops, the run's script lists the session's inbox and
  **cancels every steer the plugin admitted and OpenCode never delivered**
  (`session.inbox.cancel`, an id of the plugin's own shape and nothing else); the
  record alone carries the note, read once, by the review or the next launch's
  brief. A run killed mid-way never gets there, and its pending steers stay in
  the box's copy (measured on 2.3.2), so a run continuing that copy cancels
  them the same way before its server starts.
- **It confirms only what the model is sent plain**: OpenCode runs the
  plugin's `context` hook on every model request before sending it, and only
  where a user message of that request *is* the note (the message OpenCode made
  of the plugin's own admission, under the id it admitted the note with, one
  text part equal to its text) does the plugin post the note's id to the
  route's `read`, which
  records it read by the run's job (`boundary: step`). Delivery alone
  (`session.inbox.delivered`) is not enough: a step boundary that tips the
  session past its compaction point delivers the note and then compacts, and
  the model gets it only inside the checkpoint, framed as history. A note of
  the same words, or an earlier run's message, confirms nothing, and no request
  between a compaction's start and end confirms anything.
  - A note delivered and never sent plain when the session's compaction ends
    is **admitted again once**, under a second id the plugin asks the route's
    `again` for then, and lands plain at the next step. The engine grants it
    only for a person's note or a late call, and counts it as one of the
    note's serves when it grants it, so a note that never folds spends
    nothing. An admission under the second id that fails is made again after
    a pause, under the same id (OpenCode answers a repeat under an id it holds
    with the first, measured on 2.3.2). One the engine answers spent, one
    folded again, or one the execution settles on before it is admitted, is
    given up: never confirmed, its id posted to the route's `folded`, which the
    engine logs as `steer_note_folded`, and its review reads it. A wake or a run's
    message is served once and never admitted again: folded, it runs as a turn
    after the run. A compaction that fails confirms and posts nothing.
  - **A note's poll serves span the run's jobs**: each job a poll first serves
    it to spends one, a poll of the same job again none, and a second
    admission one more, up to three for a note or a late call and one for a
    wake. A note at its budget is served to no new job and waits for its
    review.
  - A note admitted and never delivered is never confirmed, and its review reads
    it.
  - One delivered whose confirmation never landed (its harness cut off first, or
    the store not answering) waits on the record all the same, **served**
    (above): its review reads it, and a launch that continues the run's session
    tells it as a note the session may already show; a fresh run is told it as it
    is told every note. Where nothing reads it before the turn ends, the ending
    reports it `unconfirmed` at the job it was served to, never `expired`.
  - A confirmation whose write landed while its answer was lost is reported
    `delivered` all the same: the route settles its take on its own path and
    reports what the take recorded, and a confirmation made again for a note
    already read at its job's step reports the same record.
- **It asks, and never insists**: a poll is held up to the route's ten seconds
  and given twenty, a confirmation ten. A confirmation or fold in flight when
  the server stops is let finish for up to four seconds (OpenCode awaits the
  plugin's cleanup, and the run's script kills the server five seconds on). A failed request (a stopping node's `503`
  among them) is made again after a pause of a second, doubling to thirty and
  reset by the next success, whatever its `Retry-After`, which the plugin does not
  read. A poll that admitted nothing is followed by the next no sooner than a
  second after it began, so no answer can drive it into a loop of requests. A
  refused token (`401`) or a run with no notes route (`404`) ends the plugin for
  the rest of the run, its notes waiting for the review.
- **It writes nothing**: OpenCode reloads a configured plugin whose directory
  changes, and a note never touches the box's disk.

Measured against a stub model API recording every request, on OpenCode 2.3.2:
a note of up to 1,048,576 UTF-16 units reached
the model byte for byte; it arrives plain while the session has room for it
(round(N/4) tokens more than its last reported usage stays within its
compaction point), and otherwise inside the checkpoint, so the plugin's check
is what keeps a folded note from being recorded read. A note admitted while a
tool call ran was read by the next request, after the tool's result, and one
admitted after the execution settled, with `resume: false`, started nothing
and stayed pending in the session across the server's restart, handed to the
next run in that session ahead of its prompt; cancelled, it was handed to
nobody (measured on 2.3.2). One admitted during the final model call read in
the same execution, after the answer it superseded, is untested on 2.3.2. The run's [result](#opencode) is its
**last** message's text, so a run steered past its answer reports the answer it
gave after the note.

A managed policy that denies the plugin (`integration.use`), or a plugin OpenCode
fails to load (its own log names it), leaves a run that succeeds without asking
for its notes once, which the collection says as
[`steer_reader_never_ran`](#failure-modes); its notes still reach its review.

The plugin admits the job's late calls as it admits notes, one message each under
its own inbox id ([an item for one job](#notes-to-a-running-run)), and confirms
them with its notes in the same read.

---

### Codex's notes

A Codex run its launch wires to its turn's notes takes them through
**`turn/steer`**, the app-server call that adds words to the turn in flight:
Codex 0.171.0 puts a steered note into the next request as a user message after
the tool output of the step in flight. No Codex hook is used, so a note has one
route and one confirmation.

**The note helper** is a small static program the engine embeds
(`internal/notehelper`, built for linux amd64 and arm64) and writes into the box
at each launch, so an image needs nothing for it. The run's script starts it
beside the app-server and stops it with `exec`; its errors go to the run's error
stream. The same helper holds a run to its round cap and reports its skill loads
([Codex](#codex)). It polls the run's notes route **outbound**, as OpenCode's plugin does
(the route, which carries the job's token, reaches it in its environment alone,
never on a command line), joins the thread the script wrote from
`thread.started` over the server's socket, and steers each note into the turn in
flight. It confirms nothing; the session's rollout does, as Qwen Code's record
does: a note is confirmed read only once the part of the rollout the run wrote
holds it as a user message, matched by the digest of the text the route served,
and the model replied after it (its words, its reasoning or a call). Codex
writes the message before the request that carries it, and whether a resume
hands back a trailing message no reply followed was not measured, so a note
whose run was killed or whose request failed after that write is served again.
The run's part starts where its script counted the rollout's lines as it
began, since a continued session's rollout holds every earlier launch's
messages. Each message matches the first note after the last one matched
with its text, so notes of one text need one message each, a note Codex
never recorded (an accepted steer is taken as delivered) is passed over
unconfirmed, and a note already read keeps its place, so its message
confirms no later note of the same words; a
compaction before the reply, a compaction's summary and a torn last line
confirm nothing. A note Codex refuses or a turn already over is steered again
at the next poll. A
notes route that refuses the helper (401 or 404) ends its polls alone: the cap
and the skill reports go on.

**A note may run to 1,048,576 characters**, the most `turn/steer` takes (it
counts code points; a text never holds more than its UTF-16 length, so the
runner's ceiling is that many UTF-16 units). The model's window, not the call,
is the real bound: a steer past it is compacted.

### Gemini CLI's notes hook

A Gemini CLI run takes its notes at one boundary, as it is about to finish, through an **AfterAgent** command hook in its settings: `node <home>/.crewlet/gemini-take.mjs <home>/.crewlet/gemini-take.json`, under a 10-second timeout at which Gemini CLI kills the hook and goes on. At every finish, a finish that continues an earlier block included, the hook calls the bridge's unlisted `steer_take` (initialize, initialized, `tools/call` over streamable HTTP, 120 to 285 ms measured) and prints the answer, which the engine renders in Gemini CLI's own JSON: `decision: block` with the note as its `reason`. Gemini CLI hands the reason to the model as a message from the user, and the run goes on. A hook answer is at most 9,000 UTF-16 units, the least that holds the engine's widest note beside its widest item; the reason carried 1 MB whole on 0.70.0. The hook reads the bridge's address from its configuration file, never its command line or environment.

**A take is confirmed by its text.** Nothing out of the model's view reaches Gemini CLI's session, so no take token can, and a take counts as read once the main session holds its exact text as a user message, matched in order: two takes of the same text need two deliveries. 0.70.0 writes that message before its next request and keeps it through a kill of every `gemini` process. Gemini CLI compresses its history at a turn's start, before a note joins it, so a note is always first sent plain and its plain entry confirms it, even once a later compression folds it into a `<state_snapshot>` summary; the summary and the copies of the entries a compression keeps confirm nothing. A session's transcript reads a compression as Claude Code's compaction: the entries before it stay, and the snapshot is its summary.

An **AfterTool** hook, the same script, reports a skill the model activates (`activate_skill`) to the run's skill route, as OpenCode's plugin does. It takes no note.

### Qwen Code's notes

A Qwen Code run takes its notes on the [notes route](#opencodes-notes-plugin), polled by its helper while the turn runs. Qwen Code asks its ACP host for messages after every tool batch of the main agent (`craft/drainMidTurnQueue`), never inside a subagent's loop, gives each ask 2 seconds and stops asking for the rest of the session after three asks time out. The helper answers every ask at once with every note it has already polled, so it never meets either bound. Qwen Code adds each to its next request in a message from the user, after `[User message received during tool execution]: `. A message carries at most 4,505 UTF-16 units, the engine's item bound. A note sent after the turn's last tool batch is not asked for in that run and waits on the run's record.

**A note is confirmed by its record and the reply after it.** Qwen Code records a handed note in the session's chat file as a `type: user`, `subtype: mid_turn_user_message` record holding its exact text, before the request carrying the note goes out (measured on 0.28.4), so the record alone does not show the model read it: the next `assistant` record, the reply to that request, does. The helper confirms each note on the notes route only once both are there, matched in order, so two notes of one text need two records, a note the helper never handed or Qwen Code never recorded is passed over unconfirmed, and a note already read keeps its place; and every read of the job's box reads the same records itself, matching each serve's digest of the item it handed (`sandbox.InboxItem.Digest`) against the record's text with Qwen Code's framing cut, so a note the model replied to as the run was killed, before the helper could post it, is still read. A note with no reply after its record (its request failed on a 429 past its retries or on the context, or was cancelled or the run killed before any of the reply streamed; a turn cancelled mid-reply records the reply's streamed part, which settles the note as any reply does, since a load hands the note back before it, measured on 0.28.4) is never confirmed: the engine serves it again, and a run that [continues the session](#qwen-code) cuts its record from the chat file before the load. So is one with a line the read passes over between its record and the reply (past the read's bound, or one that does not decode), which may have been a compaction that summarized it. Notes the helper polled and never handed die with it; nothing of them is left in Qwen Code's session.

**A compaction takes back a note it only summarized** ([ADR-0177](../../adr/0177-an-in-box-runners-note-take-meets-one-contract.md)). A note is confirmed once a response follows its record, which shows the model took it as a current instruction, so a later compaction takes nothing back. A `chat_compression` record before that response keeps it only where its text stands plain in the history Qwen Code goes on with, past the prefix, in a user entry (the larger of `summaryPrefixLength` and `contextPrefixLength`, which no capture tells apart, so a summarized note is never counted), so a note held only in the summary is served again. A transcript reads that record as one summary entry, its headings heading nothing, and does not read again the tail it copies.
