**The run stops with `session/cancel`**, never a signal: Qwen Code tears its chat file on SIGTERM. An end request reaches the helper as SIGTERM; it cancels the turn, closes Qwen Code's stdin and exits. Qwen Code runs in a process group of its own, so no signal meant for the job reaches it.

### Hermes Agent's notes

A Hermes run its launch wires to its turn's notes takes them through
**`session.steer`**, the gateway call that adds words to the turn in flight:
Hermes 0.23.3 puts a steered note after the newest tool result as a user
message framed as an out-of-band message from the user (measured). The
runner's plugin, loaded in the run's gateway, polls the notes route
**outbound** while a turn runs, at the pace OpenCode's plugin keeps (the
route, which carries the job's token, is read from its file at each poll,
never from an environment or a command line), and steers each note through
Hermes's own gateway client, on the endpoint Hermes's discovery names, so it
never starts a gateway. Hermes's plugin API's own `inject_message` queues a
message as a turn of its own after the run's, so it is not used. The plugin
confirms nothing: a note is confirmed read only once the session's record
holds it in this launch's own rows (above the store's newest row as the
launch began) as a user message of the conversation shown as a steer, in
Hermes's frame (never one a compaction folded away, its summary, or a copy of
a row a compaction wrote again under the same `message_uid`), matched by
the digest of the text the route served, in serve order with a serve the
record lacks passed over, and a reply the model finished is stored after it
(measured: the note rides the request after the tool result). Notes steered
during one tool call share one row, each stripped and joined by a newline
(measured); the row is parsed whole into notes served in order, the earliest
serves winning where two parses take it all. Reaching the gateway and resuming
the session have a 5-second deadline (2.3 s measured with three busy loops a
core) and are tried again; the steer itself has 10 seconds (under 0.06 s
measured), and one whose outcome is unknown once sent is not sent again, its
record deciding it, since `session.steer` takes no key that would make a repeat
harmless, while one Hermes rejects (no turn running) is. The run's session is
the first top-level session the gateway turns for, and then each session a
compaction rotates it into (named by the turn hooks with no parent, measured,
so the plugin reads the store to tell); a delegated subagent's turn, which
fires the plugin's turn hooks under its own session, and another top-level
session's are no turns of the run's (measured). A notes route that refuses the
plugin (401 or 404) ends its polls. A note may run to the engine's item bound,
4,505 UTF-16 units.

## Mid-run clarification (`ask_and_wait`)

A run may hit something only a person can answer: an ambiguous spec, a design decision above its remit. A headless harness cannot pause to ask, so every executor run's [standing instructions](#what-a-harness-is-told) carry `## When you need a person's answer`, with two ways to ask:

- **If it can go on without the answer**, it asks with its own tools (`comment_on_work_item` with an `ask` naming whoever owes the answer, or a message where it was asked), keeps working, and finishes its turn with `submit_work`, saying what is waiting on whom. The answer wakes a new turn of the seat's like any other message; this run does not wait.
- **If it cannot go on without it**, it **parks**: it commits and pushes its work-in-progress branch, calls **`ask_and_wait`** on its [tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box) (`internal/agent/builtin/runask.go`) with the question, and ends its turn without `submit_work`. The audience (`to`) is `requester`, `team`, `manager`, or a named teammate; the instruction carries the seat's unit roster and manager by handle, so the park resolves the name exactly. When the person answers, the run **continues where it stopped**, in its own harness session, with the answer as its next prompt:
  - in the box it left, when the relaunch reuses that box (the box was kept, the member the launch picks runs the same harness in the same cell, and the box is on this node's own host);
  - otherwise in a new box from the branch, its session restored from the capture the turn kept ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session));
  - where the session cannot be continued, a fresh run in a new box from the branch, told the question and the answer ([Answering a parked run](#answering-a-parked-run)).

The rest of this section is the second path.

**A run asks in the shape a decision is asked** ([ADR-0068](../../adr/0068-a-run-asks-a-person-in-the-shape-a-decision-is-asked.md)). `ask_and_wait` takes:

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `question` | What the run needs answered, one sentence of at most 300 bytes: the title the person reads first. Required. |
| `context` | What the person needs to answer well, in Markdown (findings, stakes, links), at most 16 KiB. |
| `options`, `recommended`, `rationale`, `role`, `evidence` | The choice every question offers: 2 to 4 options (`id`, `label`, `detail`), the one the run recommends and why, the role the person answers in, and what it looked at. Options, recommendation, rationale and role are **required**: the person answers with one press, or in words through **Something else**, so a question the run would ask in words still offers the answers it expects ([ADR-0100](../../adr/0100-a-question-an-agent-puts-to-a-person-offers-options-and-recommends-one.md)). Same shape, caps and checks as a [work item's decision](../guides/worklet.md#asking-for-a-decision): a cited task is resolved to its id and a cited page must exist. |
| `to` | Who should answer, as above. Required. |
| `branch` | The branch the run pushed its work to, exactly as pushed. |

**The ask is validated whole before anything is written**, and every fault comes back to the run at once ([ADR-0059](../../adr/0059-a-tools-contract-is-its-validators-and-every-fault-comes-back-at-once.md)): a question past its cap, no options or no recommendation, a branch that is not one by Gitlet's grammar (`gitref.ValidBranch`: a name git accepts, valid UTF-8 because the run's record is JSON and any other byte would arrive as another branch's name, at most 244 bytes, `gitref.MaxBranchBytes`), an option id that is not a slug. A run's ask carries no `inform`: its answer resumes the run itself, so no answered turn holds a promise.

A valid ask is **recorded on the run's row** by the job that made the call (`question`, `question_context`, `decision`, `audience`, `branch`), redacted, and only while that job is running. A second question in one job is refused (one answer resumes a run); a call from an ended or replaced job records nothing. The tool then tells the run to end its turn, and the job's `submit_work` is refused (`not_running`) with the same instruction: the job is parked, so a submission is not delivered work. The bridge nudges the run's waiter, so the run is collected and parked at once. **The branch** is recorded as its own fact, because a run re-seeded on a fresh machine is told to check it out ([below](#answering-a-parked-run)); it is never inferred from the delivered refs, which name a pull request's URL as often as a branch. A run ended at its turn's wall-clock cap is never parked on a question it asked on its way out: it is collected and resumed like any ending. When a run completes with a recorded question:

1. The engine (never the sandbox) **announces** the question as `executor_asked` on the event stream, attributed to the asking seat, carrying the question, its context and decision, the audience as written, the run's conversation and work item, the asking job (`launch_id`) and, for a question about a held tool call, that call (`held_call`, never its arguments). It resolves the audience into the people it is put to ([below](#who-a-question-is-put-to)), keeping identity attribution and capability guards on the engine. **That is how it reaches them**: a row in each person's decisions on the dashboard (Home, the Inbox's *Needs you*, *Asked of me* on My work, all served by [`GET /worklet/decisions`](../reference/api-endpoints.md#queries)), a banner on the run's page and its rail in Live › Executors, a row of Live › Now running's *Waiting on a person*, and an entry on the operator's board (`GET /executors?audience=<handle>`, "what is waiting on me"). **Nothing is posted to a chat surface**: no message goes into the run's conversation or anybody's direct messages, so a person who works only in chat learns of the question from somebody who saw it. It is answered from that row, [by turn](#answering-a-parked-run), or by a reply on the run's conversation (step 3).
2. The run is parked (`awaiting_clarification`) with both conversation values; the turn's parked state stays on the row untouched; the box is left **paused** so the checkout and harness session survive. Unlike a running job, **the agent goes free**: a human reply can take days, so its inbox flows. The question is announced first and recorded second, and the agent is freed only once the record lands: a question recorded but never announced waits for an answer nobody was asked for, and a seat freed ahead of the record reads as idle with nothing open, so a person's reply would run as an unrelated turn.

   **A park that could not be written is not a park.** The run holds the claim a completion took, so a failing step gives the claim back: the completion poll fires again, the paused box is collected a second time and the park is retried. Its delivery is handed back as the node's own failure, never the message's, whether the coordination store did not answer the record or the broker did not take the announcement, so a delivery whose budget an outage spends is kept with its group's unhandled deliveries and not with the poison. If the store refuses to take the claim back, nothing retries (a row left in the claim is read by no poll, re-claimed by no redelivery, matched by no answer and expired by no reaper), so the run is ended like any lost turn: record deleted, box reclaimed, `executor_failed` with reason `claim_unreverted`. A hand-back the store did not answer is no refusal, and is often the same silence the park could not be recorded in: the node keeps the claim and repeats the release until the store answers, its seat's mail held and the job claimed by nothing meanwhile, and never ends the run for that silence (`sandbox_claim_revert_owed`, under [Failure modes](#failure-modes)). The run is ended **only while it is still the claim** (its status, job and lease, which the store checks as it decides the ending): a hand-back that reported a failure may still have landed, and a run it reached is back where the claim found it and owed its retry, so it is left to that retry. An ending that could not reach the store is kept and finished later; if it finds the run handed back after all, it resumes it with its reply. The ending is decided first and the box reclaimed second, since the decision establishes the run was still the claim's to end.
3. The **first reply posted in that conversation after the question was asked, by somebody it was put to and written for whom the run works for,** is the answer. The row records the instant the question was put (`asked_at`, taken before the announcement, so nobody can have read it earlier); a delivery answers only if posted at or after that instant (its envelope's timestamp, for chat the vendor's post time). Without the anchor, a message written while the job still ran would be taken as the answer the moment the run parked, and a held-back reply to an *earlier* question, redelivered, as the answer to the next one. The conversation is matched on the [conversation identity](event-system.md) the row was written with, not the inbox partition: a run launched from a top-level direct message parks under the bare DM channel, the seat replies as a thread, and the answer then arrives partitioned on that thread. A direct message is one conversation however it is threaded. A row with no identity (a run an A2A wake or a task assignment launched) is answered by no chat reply, and neither is a row of a schedule's conversation, which every fire carries and nothing a person writes does: a delivery on it is never offered to a parked run, so a schedule's next fire is never taken as the answer to its last fire's question. Every question is parked with its anchor (a park without one is refused), and a delivery that cannot show it was posted after the question answers nothing and goes its ordinary way.

   **Only words answer it.** A delivery is a reply only when it carries words its writer addressed to the conversation: a chat message, a comment on a work item, a page or a change, or a review, judged from the surface the event's source reads its body from (its provenance), never from its text. A status or field change on the run's own work item, a page save, an alarm firing again, a monitor's re-alert or a work pickup on the same conversation is not a reply, whoever made it: it runs as the ordinary event it is, and the run keeps waiting.

   **Only somebody the question was put to answers it there.** One turn works for one writer ([ADR-0109](../../adr/0109-a-turn-somebody-woke-is-held-to-the-apps-they-use.md)), and the answer is what the run carries on with, so a reply answers only when its writer is a seat of the question's audience ([below](#who-a-question-is-put-to)) or the run's requester, and whoever holds that seat may act when the reply arrives (read then, never at the park). The writer is the seat the engine's party registry resolves the reply to, never its words: a vendor still delivers a suspended person's chat, and the registry withholds their identities, so it names nobody. Anybody else's reply (a stranger, a person or seat outside the audience, a credential) runs as the ordinary message it is, its own turn worked for its own writer, and the run waits. A reply also answers only a run working for whom it was written for: an agent's reply written in a turn for somebody else is that somebody's work, so it runs as its own turn held to their apps, and the run waits. A reply written for nobody else (every vendor's, every person's, an agent's own work) qualifies. A credential is matched by its login, never its apps. A colleague on a node that cannot place the run's credential works for a stranger and can post no first-party reply, so such a run waits for the dashboard or a vendor reply. A question whose park named neither an audience nor a requester is answered from the dashboard alone ([ADR-0077](../../adr/0077-a-tool-call-that-needs-approval-parks-its-run-in-the-shape-a-runs-ask-does.md)).

   **The answer is recorded before anything is done with it.** The first qualifying reply is written onto the run by a compare-and-set (the run moves to **`answered`**, carrying the reply, `answer`), and only then is the delivery acknowledged. From then the answer is durable and independent of the inbox: a second reply racing it, on this node or across a seat handoff, loses the compare-and-set and finds the question answered. The coordinator then claims the answered run (at-most-once) and **resumes the same turn, which carries the run on**. The round the run asked in is not over, so the answer is never filed as the run's report: the executor is relaunched **continuing the harness's own session** (Claude Code's `--resume`, OpenCode's session) with the answer as its next prompt, so the run goes on knowing everything it read and tried:
   - in the paused box where the relaunch reuses that box, as [Reuse across launches](#how-a-coding-task-runs) has it;
   - otherwise (box reclaimed while the question waited, a fallback onto a member in another cell, or a box on the host of a node the seat has moved off) in a new box, its session restored from the capture the turn kept when the run parked, told that the box is new and the branch to check out ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session));
   - where the session cannot be continued (no capture kept, a fallback onto a member of another harness, a box whose harness cannot take it up), the run carries on **fresh** in a new box, its brief telling it the question, the answer and the branch.

   Either way it is the same round: the calls the run made before it asked stay on its record, the carried-on run's calls are numbered after them, and its collection judges the round whole, in the order the calls were made. **Its submission is one made after the answer.** The job that carries the run on records where the answer cut the round, the place of the last call the row held when it opened (`answered_through`), and the collection replays only a `submit_work` placed after it; one the asking job made before its question was made without the answer. The cut is that recorded place rather than the round's last `ask_and_wait`, because the call log is bounded: past 200 calls it drops from its middle, ordinary calls first and a submission or an ask only once nothing else is left, so a long run can lose the ask. A job carried on after a loss keeps the cut; a new round starts without one. No fresh turn and no re-investigation.

   **The answer is sealed on the run, like every other instruction channel.** Its words and who gave them are written onto the row only inside a seal under the fleet keyring (Tier A `secrets.keys`, in a key domain of its own), bound to the run, the question it answers (the asking job) and the deliveries it was made of ([ADR-0031](../../adr/0031-every-state-log-record-is-signed.md)). Whichever node resumes the run opens the seal first, and the turn is handed only what the seal carried. An answer whose seal does not open as an answer to that question is never handed to the run or attributed to anybody: it is logged at error (`sandbox_answer_unverified`) and let go (nothing handed back, nothing announced), and the run waits on its question again, where the next reply answers it. One sealed under a key the node does not hold waits instead, recorded and owed with the seat's mail behind it, logged at warning with the keys the node does hold (`sandbox_answer_key_unknown`), until a node that holds the key takes the seat or this one restarts with it ([Rotating the keyring](secret-store.md#rotating-the-keyring-with-nothing-in-flight-lost)).

   **Recording and resuming are split because the inbox's retry order is the wrong order for an answer.** On JetStream a NAK'd message returns after its redelivery backoff **behind** the conversation's newer mail ([event system](event-system.md#delivery-semantics)), so the person's next message would reach the still-waiting run first and be taken as its answer, and the real answer would answer whatever the run asked next or run as a turn with no context. A failed resume is the **coordinator's** to retry on its own schedule; the person's message is never handed back for it.

   **The seat's later mail waits behind the answer.** While a seat owes any of its runs an answer's resume, the coordinator holds the seat's inbox (the `sandbox` hold a busy seat is held under too). It lifts the hold once the resume has *returned* and, where the resume ended the run, once the run's record is gone and its turn's end is on the executor log (recorded off the resume's frame once every capture of the turn has settled; [How a turn ends on the executor log](turn-engine.md#how-a-turn-ends-on-the-executor-log)). So the person's follow-up is worked as an ordinary turn, with the run's own replies already in the thread it reads, rather than racing the resume or overtaking its end. A follow-up sent while the executor log does not answer waits until it does, which its own alarms name. It is a hold, not a park: the mail waits on the broker with its order and delivery count intact. A later reply is an ordinary message, not a note to the resumed run: a [steer note](turn-engine.md#steering-a-running-turn) is sent with `steer_turn`, and one sent to a parked run waits on the run's record and is read in the brief of the launch that carries the answer ([notes to a running run](#notes-to-a-running-run)).

   **Every delivery on a conversation somebody can reply into, to a seat with a question open, is offered to that match first.** A parked run frees its seat, so the answer arrives on the ordinary path looking like any other message. The dispatcher therefore offers each such delivery to the parked run *before* consuming it, and only what no parked run claims becomes a turn. A delivery on a conversation nobody can reply into (it carries none, only the per-event fallback, or a schedule's) is never offered: the dispatcher answers *not mine* without asking the coordination store, so a schedule's next fire runs as its own turn beside the fire parked on the question. The offer comes after the completion ledger has had its say, so a redelivered trigger that already produced a turn is never also taken as an answer. A **held** seat offers nothing: a reply to a second run of the same seat waits with the seat's mail and is offered when the first stops holding the seat. A delivery that **becomes** an answer is recorded in that ledger, so a copy (a redelivery whose acknowledgement was lost) is dropped rather than run as a turn, on whichever node it reaches; while the run still holds the answer, a copy is recognised on the run itself and spent as the answer it is.

   **The offer answers what to DO with the delivery, in four words, and an error is never one of them.**
   - *Consumed*: the answer is recorded on the run (whatever its resume then does), or the delivery is a copy of one already recorded. It is acked and no turn runs.
   - *Deferred*: a run is waiting and the answer could **not be recorded** (the coordination store failed or could not say whether the write landed, or the identity directory could not say whether the writer's seat is held by somebody who may act now). The delivery is **handed back by deferral** and offered again: it keeps its place at the head of the seat's inbox (a NAK would put it behind the person's next message), and the seat's inbox stops until the seat host's next renew.
   - *Not mine*: nothing was awaiting this conversation, the delivery was written before the question, its writer is nobody the question was put to or holds a seat whose person may not act now, or it is on a conversation nobody can reply into. It is worked as the ordinary message it looks like.
   - *Refused*: the delivery is a reply too large to be the run's answer, and its refusal is the question's outcome (below). It is **handed back by deferral, unspent,** and no turn runs: the run's record carries none of the reply, so the delivery is its only copy, kept at the head of the seat's inbox until the refusal leaves the run. Which of these a refused reply is, is read off the run **as the resume's first attempt left it**: an attempt that let the refusal go (a resume that broke before its turn, a seal that did not open) leaves the delivery *not mine* at once.

   A delivery whose answer was recorded is *consumed* even when the run's first resume ends it for good (no conversation to re-enter, a claim that could not be given back, a resume that broke before its turn): the ending hands the reply back through the run's row as below, with the seat's inbox held until the copy is out, so it still reaches the seat once and in order. The ambiguous cases resolve towards the run, because an answer that arrives twice is recoverable and an answer that is spent is not.

   **A lookup that cannot be made is decided by what this node already knows.** When the store cannot say *which* of the seat's runs is awaiting a reply, the seat's own awaiting count decides; the node holds it in memory (seeded from the store when it claimed the seat, moved since by its own transitions), so it is readable when the store is what is failing. No awaiting run on the seat: *not mine*, because nothing is owed the delivery and an unreadable store must not swallow an ordinary message (on a company with no parked runs, every message a seat receives). An awaiting run: *deferred*, because something here **is** waiting for somebody's reply and only which row could not be read. Hand-backs are bounded by the same count as any other, under a key naming the seat; past it the message is let go to the ordinary route and `sandbox_answer_lookup_exhausted` says so.

   **Both series are bounded.** *The resume of a recorded answer* is retried by the coordinator a second after it fails, doubling to a 30-second ceiling (the queue's own failure backoff, deliberately), for at most **10 attempts** and at most the run's own **`pause_ttl_seconds`**, measured from the first failure: about two and a half minutes, long enough for the failures that reach it to clear (a seat lease moving to a node that can resume the run, 45 s; a config apply that brings the missing runner; a store blip).

   A retry the seat's own conditions refuse charges nothing, and it **waits for what refused it** rather than re-checking on a timer:
   - a person's pause: until the pause watch hears them resume the seat;
   - a company with no model: until the apply that brings one;
   - a spent budget window: until the instant it turns over, or an apply that moves the ceiling;
   - a relaunch every member of which is at a usage limit it already reported: until the first is tried again;
   - a node whose posture refuses new work: until the reconcile tick that finds it admitting again;
   - a seat whose ownership cannot be proven: until it can, the moment the seat's acquisition is established (so an answer inherited from the last holder resumes as soon as the new holder can run it) or the renew that proves it again after a store blip, with one heartbeat on the clock behind both for a renew that was merely late.

   A retry the **node** refuses waits the same way and is charged nothing: every resume asks the node's admission before it claims the run (see *Completion → resume*), and a draining node refuses it until the drain hands the seat back, which lets the answer go to the seat's next holder, recorded on the run as it was. An answer's admission also asks the models' limit of its first call, the relaunch (the members of the executor chain a launch can take), and the seat's budget (a window full or too short for a launch). A completion's admission asks neither (only whether its seat is parked, below): its job is over and its tokens are spent, so it is collected first, charged in the window it ran in and its box paused, and its review and relaunch meet the budget themselves, while a limit its review's chain (`llm_review`, else `llm`) already reported refuses its resume once it is collected, before its turn runs, and parks the seat on that limit. A completion the admission refuses is acknowledged and kept until the condition clears, and the waiter announces it again meanwhile, so it spends none of its deliveries. A resume that meets its models' limit before its turn writes anything (a limit its review's chain already knew once its job was collected, its reviewer's chain at the call, or a relaunch whose every runner member sits out) is reverted and waits the same way, spending no attempt. A completion's is also held by the node that met the limit, until the instant the limit names: that node refuses the waiter's announcements of the job meanwhile, before its gate and its claim, rather than collect the box and run the review into the same limit at every poll, and its own re-fire of the job waits for that instant too, since a re-fire drops the hold. Every five minutes before the instant the node asks only whether the turn's deadline has passed, so a turn whose deadline passes while no waiter announces the job is ended within five minutes of it rather than at the limit's instant.

   **The resume parks its seat on the limit too**, as a dispatch's turn that met it would ([the provider park](llm-backends.md#falling-back-between-entries)): `seat_provider_parked`, the seat reading `stopped` with the reason `provider`, and the chain's probe, whose answer releases the park and re-fires the resume. While the park stands, the admission refuses every resume of the seat, so a completion whose own instant passes while the probe still finds the limit is refused before its claim. An answer the park refuses waits for its release, and for the instant of the probe's next call only while that is still to come: from the probe's instant until its call comes back (a whole run of the entry's harness) the instant is past and the park still stands, so the refusal names none. A refusal that names an instant already past is waited out as one that names none, whatever refused it.

   **The hold is that node's alone**, like the limit it waits on: it is kept in the node's memory and never written to the run's record, so a restart forgets it and so does the node's letting go of the seat, and the next announcement asks whoever holds the seat then, whose own models may know of no limit. The waiter goes on announcing the job meanwhile and leaves its paused box asleep, since the job was read back already (see [Durability, completion, and observability](#durability-completion-and-observability)). A resume its seat's budget refuses once it runs (a completion's review on a full window, or a relaunch on a window full or too short for a launch) waits that window out, whether or not it wrote: a completion is held on its record, collected in its paused box, which the waiter leaves asleep until the window turns over or a revision moves the ceiling, and which the seat's holder keeps for a re-fire of its own at that instant, and on that revision's signal once it has lifted the hold, since the waiter reads the record through a store whose silence has no bound; an answer is reverted to wait uncharged in its own series.

   A signal that lands while a retry is being refused is not slept through: the wait that follows re-checks at once. Each of those is a discrete event the engine already observes, and it re-checks exactly the answers waiting on it, at once; nothing runs while the condition holds. A five-minute backstop re-checks a wait whose signal never came, so a missed signal costs a late resume, well inside the 30-minute default `pause_ttl_seconds`, and never a stranded answer.

   Past the bound the answer is **let go**: the run goes back to waiting on its question, the reply is handed to the seat's inbox as the ordinary message it is (under a new id derived from the original, because the original is spent in the completion ledger), and that reply is **declined** for this question (`declined_answers`) so it never answers it again, and `sandbox_answer_requeue_exhausted` says so. **Letting go is exactly once**, across a crash at any step: one write clears the answer, declines the reply and its copy, and records the copy on the run as owed to the seat (`hand_back`); the copy is published off that record and cleared from it afterwards.
   - A node that stops before the write leaves the answer recorded and nothing published; the seat's next holder drives it again.
   - One that stops after the write leaves the copy owed; whoever reads the run next (this node's retry, the seat's next holder before it opens the mailbox, or the run's own ending) publishes it.
   - One that stops after the publish leaves the copy published *and* owed; the repeat is the same message under the same id, which the inbox's same-id dedupe and the completion ledger collapse.

   The run is **not** ended, because every failure that gets there is a statement about *this node* (no resumer, a parked turn state of an `execstate` version this build does not read, a seat not in this node's company), and the seat's next holder, or this node after a restart, takes over an `answered` run from its record and drives the resume itself. **A run that ends still owing a copy is not deleted until the copy is out**: the store refuses to delete a row that owes the seat anything, so the ending publishes the copy, clears it, and only then deletes the row. A publish that fails keeps the row, holds the seat's inbox behind the copy, and the ending is retried with the hand-back. **What a run owes is bounded by one decline**: a second answer is let go only once the first one's copies are cleared, so the row never carries more than one delivery batch of copies (20 events by default, the size of the answer they were made from); past it nothing is lost: the second answer stays recorded and owed, its seat stays held, and the retry publishes the copies already owed before it decides again. And **each answer gets its own attempts**: one recorded while an earlier answer's copy is still owed starts a fresh count.

   **A reply that leaves its run without a turn taking it goes back to the seat, once, whoever ends the run.** The run can end under its own resume, on the inline attempt or a retry (it has no parked turn state to resume, the store refuses to take its claim back, or the resume broke before its turn began), or under a seat that left the company, or a reap. A hand-back the store did not answer is kept instead: the answer's own series makes the release again before anything else, and resumes the answer with its reply once the release has landed. The delivery that carried the reply was spent when the answer was recorded, so nothing else would bring the reply to the seat. The ending is [decided on the run's record](#how-a-coding-task-runs) first, and **the decision settles whether the reply goes back**: a turn cannot take the answer once the ending is decided, so one no turn took by then goes back to the seat, and one a turn took has been used and goes with the run. A reply that arrives once the ending is decided is matched to no run: it is the ordinary message it is, at once (matched on the run's status, which an ending leaves as it was until the record is deleted, it would lose the record to the ending on every read and come back deferred until the ending finished). The ending then **lets the answer go** in one write that takes it off the run and records its copy as owed (`hand_back`), and hands the copy back before it deletes the row: **the store will not delete a run still holding a reply the ending owes the seat**, so an ending can never take the reply with the record. An ending is decided only under its own terms: a hand-back that landed and reported a failure, or an old holder's hand-back landing under a reap, puts a run back to `answered` with the reply on it, and a claim's own ending is licensed for the claim alone, so it decides nothing about that run, which is left to its retry, reply and all. The crash guarantees are a decline's (above). An ending that cannot be finished (the let-go not recorded, the copy not published, the announcement refused, or **the delete itself not taken**) keeps the row and its terms: the seat's inbox is held behind it, and this node finishes it, once the store takes it, exactly as decided, the box included, which the ending reclaims only after its decision.   **A claim whose node stopped before its turn took the answer is revived, and the run resumed with it.** The coordinator claims an answered run for its resume (the row reads `resumed` from then until settled), and a crash, deploy or seat move can stop the process before the turn runs. The resume therefore records, in one compare-and-set at the last moment before the turn runs, that **the turn took the answer** (`answer.taken_at`); a resume that cannot make that write does not run, and a release that gives the claim back for a retry clears it. A claim whose answer no turn took never used it and never touched the box (the take is a resumed turn's first act), so the seat's next holder **gives the claim back to the answer** (`sandbox_answer_revived`): in one compare-and-set the run is `answered` again, fenced to the holder's lease, with the lost claim counted on the answer (`answer.lost_claims`, `answer.first_lost_at`). The holder drives its resume like any answer its last holder recorded and never resumed with: the seat's mail held behind it, and the box still paused or, past `pause_ttl_seconds`, reclaimed and the run re-seeded from its branch.

A revival the store does not confirm (a failed write, or a claim that moved and could not be read again) is retried on the hand-back's spacing with the seat's mail held behind it (`sandbox_answer_revive_owed`), never read as a reason to end the run; finding it landed or the claim given back, the holder resumes the run it finds.

A claim a node made itself and lost track of (its write reported a failure and landed) is **not a lost claim**: no node stopped. The answer's next attempt on that node gives it back under the lease it was taken under (`sandbox_answer_claim_given_back`), **uncounted**, and goes on with the answer's own attempts: resuming, or declining the answer once those are spent, never ending the run. That holds on the last attempt and when the window lapses under a claim: the attempt that spends the budget gives the claim back first, then hands the reply back once.

**Revival is bounded by two counts kept on the row**, because a node that stops resets every count it kept: after **3** revivals of one answer (`sandbox.MaxAnswerRevivals`), or once the run's own `pause_ttl_seconds` has passed since the first claim of it died, the next claim that dies is reaped instead. Three deaths in a row mean a resume that takes its node down before its turn begins. The store will not delete a run with the reply on it, so the reap lets the answer go: the copy handed back, the run ended, and its loss announced once as `abandoned_tail`, saying why it was not resumed again and that the reply went back to the seat (`sandbox_answer_not_revived`). A claim whose turn took the answer has used it, and a copy or second resume would answer the person twice: it is spent, the run reaped, and the announcement says nothing went back.

**The take, the revival and the ending are exclusive in the store's own compare-and-set**: a revival and an ending both refuse an answer a turn took, a revived run has no claim left to take it under, and a decided ending takes no take. Whichever lands first wins, whatever any lease says, so a node still on its way to its turn cannot also answer the person. Only the claim's own ending lets go of an answer its turn took: a turn that gave its claim back as a retry reached nobody, and once the hand-back cannot land, no retry will hand the reply to a turn again.

The reap **fences the row first**, moving the run to its own, newer lease, so a node that lost the seat has its take refused and the person is answered once, through the seat's next holder. That fence holds because **every claim carries the claimant's own lease**: the claim stamps it on the row and every later write (the take, the hand-back, the ending) carries it back; a launch stamps its lease the same way, and the seat's new holder stamps its own on every run it recovers, parked ones included. **A take, a claim and the record of an answer are refused under no lease at all** on a run any lease owns (other writes let that through so a recovery holding no lease yet can write), so a stalled claimant holding no lease cannot answer on a row its successor fenced.

**A node that knows it lost the seat writes nothing on it.** Every write the coordinator would make on the seat's behalf (recording an answer, claiming one or a completion, giving a claim back, launching a run) is refused before it reaches the store (`sandbox_seat_not_held`): a reply or an answer by turn goes back to reach the seat's holder, a completion is handed back to be fired again for the holder, and a retry this node was making is dropped for the holder's recovery pass. A node that has not noticed yet writes under its old lease, which the successor's fence outranks: an answer it records is refused rather than left on a run nothing would drive.

The reap reads the row again after fencing, so a claim its old holder gave back first is taken over as a run owed its retry, not reaped. Where the reap can neither fence nor read the row, the revival (which stamps the holder's lease itself and refuses an answer a turn took) or, past the bounds, the store's refusal to delete a reply no turn took, decides.

A resume that broke before its turn began (a panic re-entering the conversation) is settled without a retry like every abandoned resume, but nothing ran, so its reply is handed back the same way rather than read as spent, and the run is announced lost once, as `resume_broken`: no turn ran to publish a completion, so the turn parked on it would otherwise read as parked for good.

**A reply too large to be the answer is the question's refusal** ([ADR-0114](../../adr/0114-a-reply-too-large-for-its-run-is-its-questions-refusal.md)). The record carries an answer up to **512 KiB** (below), which a reply reaches at about 3.4 times its words in plain text and up to about 20 in markup: a pasted log of a hundred KiB is taken whole, but five 32 KiB Chatlet messages delivered together, or one very long Slack message or GitLab note, are not. Such a reply is not taken, and its **refusal is recorded as the question's outcome** in the answer's place, by the same compare-and-set. The run reads `answered`, holding the reply's delivery ids, when it was posted and who sent it, sealed, and beside them the refusal: how many messages the reply was, what it came to as the record would hold it (rounded up; where redacted words pass the share alone, the record holding their first 512 KiB and a byte, already past it) and what an answer may, and none of its words, nor of where it was posted beyond its address (the transport, the conversation and its thread, as ids, up to 4 KiB), which the resumed turn raises its working indicator in. From that write on, **while the refusal is the run's**, the question no longer waits, so nothing the person writes afterwards (an "any luck?") is taken for its answer.

The refusal is then resumed exactly as an answer is, with every guarantee above: owed with the seat's inbox held behind it, retried, taken once, revived, or let go of. **A refusal let go of** (declined after its attempts, or one whose seal does not open here) puts the question back to waiting under the anchor it was asked at, and the next qualifying reply answers it, a short message written since included. The let-go is recorded as `executor_answered` with the outcome `declined` (below), since the refusal's own record said the run would be told.

The resumed run is told, in the engine's words and where an answer would reach it (its session's next prompt, or a fresh run's brief): the person replied; the reply was too large to take (message count and both figures), so it got none of it; if it still needs it, it asks again with `ask_and_wait`, saying in the question why, for a much shorter form or another way to get it (a file committed to its branch, a path it can read, a link); otherwise it carries on and says in its final reply that the reply never reached it. A question it asks again takes its own `asked_at`, so whatever the person wrote before it is an ordinary message to the seat.

The reply itself stays in the conversation and in its delivery, which the seat's inbox keeps (*refused*, above) until a turn keeps the refusal and it is spent, or the refusal is let go of (after its attempts, by an ending no turn reached, or a reap). It then comes round as the ordinary message it is: **back to the seat the way it came**, with nothing handed back from the row. A run that ends before any turn told it of the refusal says so: its `executor_failed` names a reply too large for it to take, which it was never told of, going back to the seat. A reply to a run that was answered another way, moved on to another question or ended meanwhile is matched to nothing, whatever it weighs, and is the ordinary message every reply after an answer is.

**The turn's reviewer is told of the refusal**: the reply is in none of the round's calls, where the question asked again reads as the same question sent twice. So the relaunch that carries the round on keeps each refusal's message count and figures for the round's review (never its words), and the review prompt shows them beside the log (`## Replies the agent did not get`), saying a question asked again after one is the follow-up the engine told the run to make, which the duplicate rule does not hold against it.

**A reply's original delivery is spent the moment the reply leaves the run.** When a turn takes the answer (inline or on a retry, at the same commit that records the take), and before the write that lets an answer go by a decline, an ending or a reap, the delivery that carried it is recorded as worked in the [completion ledger](seat-ownership.md#the-completion-ledger); a reap that finds an answer a turn took records it again, for a node that stopped between the take and its spend. Otherwise a node that stopped before acknowledging the delivery would leave it to come round again after the run had used the reply, handed a copy back, relaunched or gone, and nothing on the run would recognise it; the ledger drops it instead of running it as a second message or, for an answer by turn, instead of asking the run about it again and announcing it `gone` or `not_awaiting` after it resumed the run. That holds for an answer by turn because its route reads the ledger before it reaches the run, and because its delivery is recorded whatever its type: the ledger otherwise keeps only the types that run a turn, which an answer by turn never does. A reply spent and still on its row is not lost: the row, never the delivery, is what resumes it or hands it back, and a copy handed back goes under an id of its own.

**A refused reply's delivery is spent only once a turn that took the refusal *keeps* it** (returns having run, breaks after it began, or dies holding it, as the reap of its claim finds): its row carries no copy, so never at the take (which a turn that broke before reaching anybody gives back) nor at a let-go (when the delivery must come round as the ordinary message it is). The delivery in hand during the first resume is acknowledged on that attempt's own account, never the completion ledger's, which fails open and would hand the seat, as a new message, a reply its run had just been told never reached it. Where another attempt's turn kept it, the run's row says so: the relaunch that told the run keeps the refused question for the round's review, and only that turn writes it. A copy that comes round once the refusal has left the row is dropped by the completion ledger like any redelivered event; a miss (the read fails open) runs it as the ordinary message it is.

*A delivery whose answer could not be recorded* is handed back by deferral, with three clauses. First, every hand-back spends one of the message's deliveries, so the offer stops while **5 deliveries are still left**, kept for the ordinary route. That reserve is read on **each message's own** count, never the partition's: a delivery is a whole partition whose messages sit at different counts, and gated on the partition's number a clarification reply on its *first* delivery would be refused the answer route for good whenever an older message on the same conversation is near its own budget. One message with deliveries to spare keeps the offer open; `sandbox_answer_offered_over_a_spent_sibling` says when the hand-back may spend the last delivery of a co-partitioned one, and `sandbox_answer_headroom_reserved` when the route lets go. Second, **10 attempts on one message** inside one process. Third, the run's own `pause_ttl_seconds` (`sandbox_answer_record_exhausted`). A second reply gets its own count, and one run keeps at most four of them at a time.

**Two questions open on one direct message** are told apart by the thread each was asked in: the identity admits both (that is what makes a DM one conversation), and the run whose own partition matches the reply's wins, with the most recently parked question answering a top-level reply that matches neither.

### Who a question is put to

The audience a harness names is its own words, so the park resolves it, once, against the org chart, in the same write as the question, into the seats the question waits on (`audience_handles` on the run's record and on [`GET /executors`](../reference/api-endpoints.md#get-executors)):

| Audience | Put to |
|---|---|
| `requester` | The seat whose message, notice or ask woke the turn that launched the run. The launch records it on the run (`requester`), because the park runs when the job finishes, perhaps days later on another node, and sees no trigger. |
| `manager` | The seat's manager. |
| `team` | The lead of the seat's unit and the **people** in it; the unit's other agents are left out, since the seat could ask them itself. |
| a name | The one colleague it names exactly: a handle, an id on a chat surface, or a role name, case aside. A partial or approximate match is not a person: a guessed colleague is somebody else's question in their inbox. |

When the audience names nobody the chart has (no requester recorded, no manager, the name matches nobody), the question is put to the seat's **lead chain** (its managers, nearest first, or, for a seat nobody manages, the leads of the units that hold it) and `audience_fallback` says so. A question is never parked waiting on nobody while somebody is answerable for the seat, and a person can tell a question put to them from one that reached them because nobody else could be named. `?audience=<handle>` on the board is "what is waiting on me".

### Answering a parked run

A reply on the question's conversation (step 3 above) is one way to answer. The other is to **name the run by its turn**, with the operator tool [`answer_executor`](../reference/api-endpoints.md#answering-a-parked-executor), from your own assistant over `/operator/mcp` or from the dashboard. It is the only way for a run started by a **schedule, a task assignment or a colleague's ask**: a task assignment's and a colleague's ask's turns have no conversation, and a schedule's names its schedule's, which no person writes into, so nothing a person says in chat can reach them.

In the dashboard it is the **Answer** on a parked run's banner: on the run's page and its rail in Live › Executors, on Live › Now running's "Waiting on a person", in the Inbox and on Home. The banner names who the question is put to (the audience resolved when the run parked), how long the box is held, and whether a reply on the turn's conversation would reach it too.

**Who may answer is the run's requester (the person whose message, notice or ask woke the turn that launched it), or whoever leads the run's seat, or an administrator (`admin`)**, and never a seat: the person who asked for the work answers what it asks them, and nobody who merely leads that person does (see [the authority table](identity-and-access.md#the-sixteen-rules)).

`answer_executor{turn_id, launch_id, choice, answer}` checks the run is waiting (`not_running` if not), that it waits on the question the person read (`launch_id`, the job that asked it; `stale_version` once the run has moved on) and, where it names a `choice`, that the choice is one of the options the run's question offers (otherwise refused, naming them, and on an open question); an answer is a choice, words, or both. It then puts an `executor_answer_given` event on **the seat's control topic**, answering `pending`. The control topic, not the seat's inbox, because the answer is addressed to the run, like a completion: the inbox is held while the seat's executor holds the seat for any turn and is worked oldest first after that, so an answer riding it would wait behind every launch and older message.

The node holding the seat takes it off the control topic and hands it to the coordinator, which **records it on the run** at once (the run reads `answered` from that moment) exactly as it records a chat reply (the answer, the credential and the person it names, sealed, and the event it arrived in), and carries the run on with it as above, attributed to the person who gave it. From the record on, an answer by turn is a recorded answer like any other, except that its first attempt is queued rather than made inline: the resume starts a turn, so it waits until the seat has a slot free and no other run of its conversation (ADR-0169), the node has room for a turn of the seat and its conversation, and no person has the seat paused, and is then the seat's next turn, with the seat's mail held behind it. Its retries are the coordinator's, a resumed turn **takes** it at the last moment before it runs, and a claim whose node stops before its turn took it is revived by the seat's next holder (see [Mid-run clarification](#mid-run-clarification-ask_and_wait)).

It is **never a turn**: whatever it finds, the delivery is spent there, and only an answer the run is still owed but could not be recorded against (the store could not be read, or the record could not be confirmed) is handed back to the broker for its spaced retry; a redelivery that finds the record landed is spent as the answer it already is. Once it has become something (recorded, declined, `gone`, `not_awaiting`) it is recorded as worked in the [completion ledger](seat-ownership.md#the-completion-ledger), and so is an answer its run spends (taken by a resumed turn, let go of, reaped); the route reads the ledger first, so a redelivery after either is acknowledged without reaching the run and without a second announcement (`sandbox_answer_by_turn_already_spent`). That hand-back is a NAK, safe on this route as it is not for a chat reply: the answer names its run, so coming back behind newer mail lets no later message take its place and it cannot be taken as the answer to anything else. An answer already recorded against the question wins: the run is `answered`, and the answer by turn reports `not_awaiting`.

**An answer by turn the run could not be resumed with is let go of** like a chat reply, after the same attempts: the run waits on its question again, and the copy handed back to the seat's control topic (it has no ordinary form to become) is spent there and announced `declined`, once, so the person knows to answer again; it is never recorded against that question again. One let go of because its run ended is announced `gone` the same way. An answer given while the seat is [busy executing another turn](#how-a-coding-task-runs) is recorded at once and its resume waits until that turn's executor settles or parks; one given while the seat is paused is recorded and resumed when the pause lifts; one given while the holder restarts is still on the control topic afterwards.

**It answers the question it was given against, and no other.** The resume's wait can outlast the question, and so can a NAK's backoff or a retried copy: somebody else's answer resumes the run, its turn relaunches (a reviewer's send-back), and the new job parks on a question of its own. So the event names the question too, the job the run held when it asked (`launch_id`), off the row `answer_executor` checked, and the run is resumed with it only while it still waits on that question; once it has moved on, the answer is spent as `not_awaiting`. The question is **required**: an event naming none is spent without resuming the run, with the reason logged (`sandbox_answer_names_no_question`), since it cannot be told from an answer to a question the run has moved past; `answer_executor` never delivers one. Two answers to one question, a chat reply and an answer by turn, or two people, or a retried `answer_executor`, contend for the one record, and the run is resumed once, however far apart they arrive.

**A node that has let go of the seat hands the answer on once.** An answer or completion that reaches a node whose seat host no longer holds the seat is deferred: it goes back to the head of the control topic for the seat's holder, at the cost of one delivery, and the node stops consuming that topic until its release detaches it, so a stale node cannot walk the answer to the dead-letter subject. A refusal on the run store's word alone (a newer lease stamped the row) while the host still holds the seat is handed back on the broker's backoff, because quiescing a seat the node does hold would leave it hearing no answer or completion at all; the heartbeat settles that disagreement within a beat. The fencing epoch the store compares is monotonic across restarts on every topology ([Coordination](coordination.md#the-leases-follow-coordinationtype-the-shared-state-does-not)), so a seat's own holder is never refused as older than its runs.

**Both routes leave a record.** `executor_answered` names the run, the question it answered (`launch_id`, `question`, `question_context`, `decision`, `asked_at` and the audience), the option chosen (`choice`) and the person's own words (`answer`), the one account of the question that outlives the run: a person's [answered decisions](../guides/worklet.md#asking-for-a-decision) read it back from the event log. It also names the route (`chat` or `operator`), who answered (the chat sender, or `answered_by` and `answered_by_kind` as `iam.ActorFor` names the person, the seat they hold, which every person does, with the credential they came through in `operator_id`) and what the answer became:

- `resumed`.
- `not_awaiting`: another answer had it first, a chat reply too large for the run closed the question first, or the run is running a job.
- `gone`: the run had ended.
- `declined`: (an answer by turn every attempt failed to resume the run with, let go of; the run waits on its question again) or, on the chat route with `answer_bytes`, a refused reply's refusal let go of before any turn told the run, the reply going back to the seat as the message it was and the question waiting again, naming nobody where the refusal's seal did not open.
- `unoffered`: (an answer by turn whose choice the question it names does not offer), spent without being recorded; the question still waits.
- `too_large`: an answer past what its run may take as one, with what it came to and what an answer may (`answer_bytes` and `answer_max_bytes`), never its words. Either a chat reply too large for the run's record to carry, weighed as that record would hold it, whose refusal is the question's outcome and the resumed run is told so (one record per run, question and delivery, published under the reply's own id and instant, never a `resumed` beside it); or an answer by turn that says more than 16 KiB, spent, the question still waiting for a shorter one.

An answer by turn is measured as `answer_executor` measures it, trimmed and before any secret in it is redacted, so an answer the tool took is never refused after it, and one that did not come through the tool is held to the same 16 KiB. A chat message that matched no parked run was never an answer and records nothing; an answer recorded on its run whose resume is still being retried has not become anything yet and records nothing until it has. A chat reply let go of becomes the ordinary message it is and records nothing either, except a refused reply, whose `too_large` record said the run would be told and whose let-go is recorded as `declined`.

The durable state is always **git plus the persisted row**: the WIP branch is pushed *before* the agent asks, so the paused box is a fast-resume optimization, never the store. Clarifications chain within the same round of the same turn (an answer carries the run on rather than spending an iteration), bounded by the budget: every relaunch is held to its [launch floor](#what-a-continued-launch-costs) (`turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens`, or more for one that continues the turn's session) and each run to its `max_turns`. The wait for the person has no deadline: `pause_ttl_seconds` bounds only how long the paused box is held, and past it the pause reaper below releases the box and the answer's relaunch starts from the branch in a fresh box, continuing the turn's session there where it can.

**The pause reaper.** A human reply can take days, and a paused box holds its memory and directory on its host until something kills it, so the completion poll enforces `pause_ttl_seconds` on the same tick it uses for running jobs. The box's age is durable (`paused_at` on the run record, stamped when the box is paused), so the deadline survives an engine restart and a seat handoff. Past the TTL, a parked run gets:

1. **the box killed by id** with `sandbox.Provider.Kill`, which never wakes the box first: a `direct` box's stopped group is sent `SIGKILL` alone, with no `SIGCONT`, and a `container` box is removed (`rm -f`), so a paused run never executes again on its way out;
2. **the box released on the row** (`sandbox_id` cleared, `paused_at` cleared), which is also what makes the answer's relaunch provision a fresh box (a re-seed of its working tree) rather than reattach to a dead id;
3. **the run flipped to `reseed`**: still claimable, still matched by conversation, because the run is not over. The answer can arrive days later and still carries the run on: the same round is relaunched in a new box, continuing the asking run's kept session there, told the answer, that its box is new and the pushed branch to check out, or, where the turn kept none it can continue, as a fresh run whose brief tells it the question, the answer and the pushed branch ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). A run given [repositories on Gitlet](#repositories-on-gitlet) is relaunched with the same grants, each repository on the branch it worked on (the branch it pushed to, so a fresh clone holds its work), a repository it was given to read kept to reading, its cone kept and its `open_change` kept: the parked run opened none, so the run that finishes the work does.

**A pause that was never recorded is still a pause.** Stamping `paused_at` is a *second*, warn-only store write made once the box is paused (refusing a collected result over a timestamp would throw the run away), so a run can park holding a paused box its row does not date. A parked row naming a box therefore *is* a held box: with no stamp, the deadline runs from the row's own last write, which on a parked run is the park itself (a park that does not land is not a park; see step 2 above) and can only be later than the pause it failed to record. A pause held for any *other* reason takes no such fallback: each lasts a single dispatch and is settled by the tail that made it, so a missing stamp there means the box is live.

**An answer still waiting on its resume is still a clarification wait.** A recorded answer (`answered`) is resumed by whichever node holds the seat when the seat's conditions allow, and a seat no node holds, or one that stays paused, can leave that resume waiting as long as the question waited. Its box is held for the whole wait, so the reaper treats it as a parked run: it kills the box and clears it from the row (with the same last-write fallback when no pause instant was recorded) and does not change the status. The answer stays recorded and owed its resume, which re-seeds from the pushed branch as a `reseed` run's would. If the answer is later let go, the question reopens as `reseed` rather than `awaiting_clarification`, because the box it was parked in no longer exists. A resume that has already claimed the run moved it out of `answered`, so the reaper's flip loses, as it does against an answer's claim.

`pause_ttl_seconds: 0` takes the same path with no paused box at all: the box is torn down the moment the run blocks and the run parks straight into `reseed`.

The reaper covers **clarification waits** only: the other pause (between collecting a completion and the turn's settle or relaunch) lasts one dispatch and its tail settles it. The one paused box no tail settles is a run whose engine died mid-resume; the coordinator's recovery pass reaps it when the seat is next acquired.

### A call held for approval

A run parks the same way on a call to an MCP tool at Needs approval
([Asking a person before a tool runs](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#asking-a-person-before-a-tool-runs),
[ADR-0077](../../adr/0077-a-tool-call-that-needs-approval-parks-its-run-in-the-shape-a-runs-ask-does.md)).
The [bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box) does not
make the call: the seat's surface records it on the run's row as the job's
question (the tool, its server, its definition's digest, the work item, and the
arguments sealed under the fleet keyring), tells the harness the call was not
made and to commit, push and end its turn, and records the call as the one that
ended the job, so the waiter collects the run at once. The collection parks the
run on the question exactly as on `ask_and_wait`, its seat freed, and the job
takes no submission after it.

Where the run's turn was woken by a person's answer to a question its seat
asked, the held call names that decision: the question and the option chosen
ride the held call (`acting`) and its question's context ("It carries out a
decision on ENG-9: jane answered ... with ..."), and the approvals list says
it, so whoever approves reads a step of an answer already given. The approval
card on the server's page in Settings › MCP & tools draws the same sentence
above the call. The answers that woke the turn ride the run's row, so a later
job of the same turn names them too. A turn woken by anything else, or by an
agent's answer, names no decision.

Only `POST /mcp-approvals/{id}` answers it, never a chat reply on the run's
conversation and never `answer_executor`. The resume the answer drives makes the
call itself, through the seat's own tools on the node holding the seat, after
marking it on the row; it never makes it twice, and hands the result (or the
refusal, for `deny`) to the job that carries the work on, as its next prompt in
its own session or in a fresh run's brief. A held call names no branch, so a
fresh run is told to find the work-in-progress branch the run pushed before it
ended its turn.

---

## A seat's runs see each other

A seat runs up to its cap of runs at once (`sandbox.max_concurrent_runs`, two by default, [above](#how-a-coding-task-runs)), and two of them can take the same work item, push the same branch or answer one person twice; so can two seats' runs, when a person's ask in a thread becomes a ticket that wakes a colleague. A run launched while other runs are in flight around it is told of them and given three tools on its [bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box), beside `ask_and_wait` ([ADR-0176](../../adr/0176-a-seats-runs-see-and-message-each-other.md)). The runs around it are its seat's other runs, then up to 8 other seats' runs on its work, found in one listing of the fleet's runs: on its work item, in its conversation (never a schedule's), on an item the tracker links to its item (a dependency, a link or a duplicate, either way, at most 16), or on an item or conversation one of the two runs created or wrote through its tools, either way: the run working a ticket the caller filed or replying in a thread the caller posted in, and the run that filed the ticket or posted in the thread the caller works. A thread counts where the run's [written set](#notes-to-a-running-run) names it: a Chatlet thread does, a Slack or Mattermost post made through an MCP server does not. What a run wrote is matched off its row, which keeps a fixed-width key of each record its calls wrote (up to 128), so the listing reads no run's call log. A launch that finds none is told nothing and offered none of them.

- **Its brief** carries **Other runs in flight around this one**, one line per run, and one line on when to use the tools: a run on the same work item, branch or conversation; an unrelated run is unrelated.
- **`list_runs`** answers the same lines again, from one listing of the seat's runs and no model call.
- **`message_run`** files a message on another run's record, read at its next step.
- **`wait_for_run`** parks the run until another leaves its seat's slots. A run parks the same way, without a tool, on a call of its own its harness would give up before it returns ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)).

**What a run is shown follows whom each run works for.** Every line names the run's turn, its seat, how another seat's run relates to the caller's work (`same_item`, `same_conversation`, `linked_item`, `on_what_you_wrote` for a run on what the caller filed or wrote, `wrote_what_you_are_on` for a run that filed or wrote the caller's work), its stage (`launching`, `running`, `parked_on_question`, `parked_on_held_call`, `waiting_for_run`, `answered`; a run parked on its own calls alone, which the engine carries straight on, reads `running`) and its work item. Only a run working for the same requester also shows its conversation's kind and whether it is the caller's, the branch it named, when it started and its task's title, fenced as what its turn was asked; another requester's run reads "a run for another requester", since its task's words carry their data. Two runs share a requester when their ceilings name one principal ([ADR-0109](../../adr/0109-a-turn-somebody-woke-is-held-to-the-apps-they-use.md)), a run's own work as its seat's; a stranger is nobody's requester.

**A message is information, never a request.** It is filed as a [wake item](#notes-to-a-running-run) of its own, sealed in a key domain of its own and naming its sending run, so it is served, confirmed and told again to a continued session as a wake is, and kept as the turn's once read. The receiving run reads it under a wake's heading naming the sending run and whom it works for, the words inside the sending executor's fence, told that its own task and requester are unchanged. It is refused, naming why and never cut:

| Refused | Why |
|---|---|
| Between runs of different requesters | A run's words carry its requester's data, and no label decides whom data is for; the refusal says to tell the requester instead |
| To the caller's own run | A message goes to another run |
| To another seat's run the caller's seat may not reach as `a2a_ask` reaches a colleague | The chart decides which seats one may ask; a run reaches no further than its seat |
| To a run not launching or running, or whose harness reads no note | Nothing would read it |
| Past 2 messages a launch sends, or 2 it takes from other runs | One message says what a run is doing and one answers it; a third is a conversation for the requester. Two of a job's four wake items, so its requester's own follow-ups keep room to join |
| Past 1,000 characters | A wake's bound, which a hook's answer holds beside a person's widest note |

**A message carries the sending run's requester** as a colleague's ask does, composed from the sending run's record. **A wait parks the run as a question does**, on a run holding a slot (another seat's only on the same requester and the same reach as a message), with the run's reason and the branch it pushed. It is put to nobody: the node holding the seat watches the waits on its seats and, once a wait's run ends, fails or parks, puts a wake on the seat's control topic (`executor_wait_over`) on which the holder carries the waiting run on from its row, never recording an answer, telling it how that run went (ended and its outcome, parked and on what, or gone with nothing on record), what it pushed, and, for a run of the same requester, the first 2 KiB of what its reviewer said landed. The holder claims the run straight out of waiting: one that stops before the run's turn takes the claim leaves the run waiting again for the next holder's watch, and a run whose turn took it is not carried on twice. A run leaving on that node is seen at once; a watch also reads its seat's waits every minute. The waiting run's requester is told once, on the conversation's line, that its work waits for the seat's other run. While it waits its conversation stays busy and it holds no slot, unlike a question's park: no reply there answers the wait, and mail there waits aside behind it, its writer told why once, rather than starting a second turn on the same work. The mail is handed back when the run resumes, where a follow-up from its requester joins it, or when it ends. A wait outliving its run's pause TTL is a [parked question's](#mid-run-clarification-ask_and_wait): its box is reaped and it waits in `reseed`. A wait that would close a cycle (the run waited for waits, through at most eight runs of any seat, on the caller) is refused; none could hang, since each waiting run has itself left the seat's slots, but each would park only to be told the other parked.

## Durability, completion, and observability

**Pending runs survive restarts, and seat handoffs.** Every detached run is a record in the fleet's [coordination store](coordination.md#what-the-fleet-shares), not the node's own database, so a run outlives its turn, process and sometimes its *node*, and the next seat owner's recovery pass finds it.

On acquiring a seat (boot included), and for every seat a node already holds when an apply brings its sandbox up, the recovery pass (`Coordinator.RecoverSeat`) takes ownership of the seat's running jobs and marks the seat busy again; the waiter then drives them to completion.

- **Owed re-fire.** A running job whose record owes a refused completion its re-fire (a previous holder acknowledged a refused delivery) is owed again after the pass. It is offered to this holder's own gate at once, as the first delivery after a restart or seat move is; a refusal there is kept for this holder's condition, whose signal (above all the seat's admission, which follows every recovery) carries it. The recorded condition is the last holder's, whose signal a holder whose models know no limit never sees (`sandbox_completion_refusal_rearmed`, and `owed` on `sandbox_seat_recovered`). The re-arm also re-fires itself five minutes on, as a completion kept on a condition naming no instant does, so an unanswered first offer is not left waiting for a signal that may never come.
- **A run left in `resumed`.** The previous engine died between claiming the run's tail (a completion, or a person's answer) and settling it, so nothing would pick it up and its paused box would stay held. A completion's claim is reaped. A claim for a recorded answer no turn took yet is **revived** (given back to the answer, the run resumed with it), and reaped, its answer handed back to the seat, only past the revival's bounds. A claim whose resumed turn already took the answer is reaped as spent (see [Mid-run clarification](#mid-run-clarification-ask_and_wait)). The store revives and lets go of only an answer no turn took, and will not delete a run still holding one.
- **Fencing.** The reap first fences the row to the new holder's lease, so the stopped node cannot take the answer, then reads it again, so a claim that node gave back first is taken over rather than reaped. Every run the seat holds, a parked one included, is fenced the same way.
- **A run left in `launching`.** The engine died between starting the job and writing the parked turn state a resume reads, so nothing can resume; it is reaped. Both reaps are safe only *here*: taking the seat's lease proves no live process drives the row (a `launching` row on a seat this node already owns is a launch happening now).
- **A box the row never named.** A box records its turn when it is made, before the row names it, so one the engine stopped before attaching, or a create that failed left behind, is reclaimed by its host's completion poll once the row is gone or names another box ([Local sandboxes](#local-sandboxes)).

**The pass is exclusive with every claim of the seat's runs on its node.** A completion past its turn's deadline is claimed with no admission, and an apply on an already-held seat runs the pass with the seat established, so a delivery, signal re-fire or owed answer's attempt could be claimed mid-pass and then reaped as a resumed tail or have its answer revived. So every such claim passes one gate that refuses it while the seat's pass runs there (`sandbox.ErrSeatRecovering`, closed before the seat's control topic is attached). Nothing refused is lost: a delivery goes back to the queue as the node's failure and returns past the pass; a re-fire, a held completion's backstop and an owed answer's attempt are carried by the pass when done (`sandbox_recovery_claims_carried`). A claim let through before the pass began is its attempt's and the reap leaves it (`sandbox_reap_refused_live_claim`, logged as an error: it should never be seen).

A restart never orphans a job. A `direct` or `container` box keeps running on its host while the engine alone restarts, and the node that launched it picks it up when back (below). A restart that takes more than the engine process (its container, its systemd unit's control group, its host) takes a `direct` box's job too; that job is not collected as finished, and its round is carried on (*A job lost with its host*, below).

### The run's record, and what it costs to read

A run's **record** holds what is decided about it: status and launch, owner and fencing epoch, box, parked turn, question and answer, charge, grants on [Gitlet](gitlet.md#coding-boxes) and the floor its box reads at, and what its turn holds from Gitlet's expiry. What a job can make large is kept BESIDE it, each under its own key; the run's end removes them with the record, and the [marker sweep](coordination.md#removal-markers-are-swept) takes them where a node stopped between the two:

- the sealed secrets the job's box was handed, for a [kept session's scrub](#each-launchs-session-kept) (up to 64 KiB before sealing);
- the turn's leads;
- what carried each of the run's sessions on, for a brief to a session that may lack them (up to 512 KiB, [above](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session));
- **the bridged tool log**: every call the job made through the [tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box), arguments and output, up to 200 kept with the middle dropped past that. The session numbers each call's place in the round before it runs, after the last call the log held when the job opened. The collection reads it to rebuild the phase, a node recovering the run reads it to open the bridge again, and Live › Executors shows it, to a reader shown the run's body only.

An append is one compare-and-set of the log, taken on the job whose calls it takes, and never touches the record (which is written after only when the call moved what the job's bridged calls cost). A launch opens the log to its job once the record names the job, in one write that also decides what the job keeps: a new round starts the log with only the previous round's calls its collection did not read, as late calls, and the kinds of change the turn's calls committed so far; a job carrying the round on keeps its calls; one carried on by a person's answer cuts the round after the last of them.

That is decided by the round the record names, written by the launch's own write. If opening the log failed or the node stopped first, the log stays on an earlier job of the same round, and the relaunch carrying the round on still keeps its calls and takes the cut the answer owed. A launch whose record was removed before it opens the log (its job was stopped) is refused, not recorded again.
