all of it that can reach the entry's bound and a private key's length past it
is redacted inside as much again, so a credential that begins inside the bound
is redacted whole, and nothing the read could not settle is handed out however
much the redaction shrinks what comes before it.
An object the store no longer holds, one that does not open under the fleet's
keyring, an archive that is not one its format describes and one this build
does not read are each said as such, in the engine's own words, beside the
turn's ending, which the row still holds.

**A session released while it is read is said as released.** A read writes
nothing and keeps no session past what the seat's budget and the retention
give it — a hold taken by a read would be a write every reader makes, and it
would keep the budget from releasing the reader's own next capture — so between
the read of a session's row and the end of its object's stream a later turn's
end can absorb it, the budget release it, the end of a turn that [ran out of
context](conversation-sessions.md#a-session-that-ran-out-of-context-is-retired)
in it retire it, the retention delete it or its turn capture it again, and the
collector take the object. Read alone, that object
is missing, or, taken while it streams, one whose bytes do not open. So a read
whose object fails reads the turn's row once more, at `linearizable`, and says
what the row says now: no row, that the row went while the session was read
and nothing more of it can be read; a row naming no object, its reason and the
same; a row naming a newer capture, that capture read from its start on a first
page, and a later page's cursor refused as one captured again — of a turn that
has not ended, as one whose runs have kept its session again, which is true
whichever capture moved it, and never that a run saved it. Only where the
row still names the object is the failure the store's or the archive's own, and
the row is read again once. What the read already handed out stands: every byte
of it came from a chunk that authenticated.

**A node decodes two transcripts at a time.** One read holds no line and no
message, only a value to 2 MiB, which a longer one streams past: at most 29 MiB
measured, a value streamed at any length or one held just within the bound,
where holding costs no more than streaming (held, a value is redacted whole,
which holds about thirteen times a value of `pwd=x` lines, whose redaction
lengthens most). Its time is the redaction's, and what harnesses and ordinary
tools write sets the waits: of that, one value of `password:` lines streamed to
the 256 MiB budget is the slowest, about 45 seconds on two cores for a person
alone and 49 beside a second read, 58 for a seat's words beside a person's;
every credential shape 33. Dense tokens and a kept
session's text are mostly random bytes, which pack to three quarters of their
size, so no archive within the 48 MiB bound holds the budget's worth of them. A
value no harness or tool writes at that density, a
password's value every six or seven bytes the whole budget long (`pwd=x`
lines), takes 98 to 129 seconds for a person and about 163 for a seat's words,
sets no wait, and fails closed once it runs past its reader's wait. A node
answers every dashboard tab open on it and every REST caller, each with a read
of its own, so each node decodes at most two transcripts at once
(`TranscriptReadsAtOnce`), 58 MiB live at their worst, whichever socket or route
asks, kept at 87 MiB with the heap's room under the engine's memory limit
([The engine's memory limit](../guides/deployment.md#the-engines-memory-limit)).
A person's read is answered within 110 seconds
(`TranscriptAnsweredWithin`: the slowest read with a tenth more for a busier
node, 55 seconds, and one slot's wait), which the
dashboard waits; past it the socket ends the read, and the dashboard shows
nothing of the session and says it could not be read in time. A seat's read of
its own session has two minutes (`SessionReadWithin`, set by the object store's
pace): a read at the bounds of what harnesses write fits it alone; one queued
behind other such reads, or of a value none writes, can run past it and is
answered unavailable, never as a session that holds nothing. A relaunch's reading of a
kept session for the calls it holds is none of them: one runs at a time, in a
slot of its own (`HoldingsReadsAtOnce`), holding at most 43 MiB (an OpenCode
session's at most 2 MiB, however long one of its messages runs; a Qwen Code
one's 10 MiB measured, 12 by its bounds, however long one of its lines runs; a
Gemini CLI one's 2 MiB whatever a line's length, 4 MiB at its 16,384 records), so the two
reads and a reading hold at most 101 MiB. A read past them waits for a slot before the session's
object is opened — an opened object would hold its store's connection while it
waited — for as long as its caller waits, holding no decoder meanwhile, and a
slot frees within one bounded read; a caller that leaves first is answered
nothing, and nothing was opened for it.

**A node holds one large thread read at a time for its collections and
takes.** A job's collection reads its main thread, and a capture's take scrubs
and measures its session, holding no slot while what it holds stays within its
base: of each line read, the facts its readers keep, charged up to 128 KiB
whatever the line's length, so a long line of few facts (a large file read into
the thread) takes none; for a collection that keeps the thread's records (its
hook receipts), 2^13 of the records and call ids it files; and for the take's
scrub, 256 KiB of each line, JSON value or stretch of text it redacts as one,
four times the longest line of 99 in 100 real threads: at its worst about 5 MiB
for a collection's read and 12 MiB for a take's, whose redaction holds each
stage's window, so a node scrubs at most 29 takes at once
(`SessionTakesAtOnce`), and a take past them waits within its own wait and is
refused if it runs out. A read past its
base waits for the node's one large-read slot (`CollectionLargeReadsAtOnce`), a
pool apart from the transcripts' two, so a person paging a transcript never
delays a turn's collection. A take holds it while it holds that piece, and a
collection whose reading keeps the thread's records holds it to the read's end:
at worst about 43 MiB for a collection and 34 MiB measured for a take, which
the node's [memory limit](../guides/deployment.md#the-engines-memory-limit)
counts at its bound past what the take's own slot keeps: the scrub's 132 MiB
less its 8 MiB base, beside 10 MiB for its meter's line, 134 MiB, since one
read holds the slot at a time. The wait is spent inside the read's own: a collection whose read runs
past its 27 seconds counts the session unread and decides none of its hooks'
notes, and a take past its budget is refused, its session not kept, the safe
side each time; `executor_large_read_waited` says the slot was contended.

**It is the seat's trail, and it holds more than the run's live output
showed.** It is read by exactly who reads that output — the seat, whoever leads
it, and an administrator, `audit.seat.read`
([Identity and Access](identity-and-access.md#the-authority-table-one-function-decides))
— and by nobody it was withheld from. But the live output names a call's
subject, whole only within 8 KiB, and a failed result's first line, and never a
result's body; a session's transcript holds every call's whole input and each
result's text to an entry's bound — the contents of the files the run read and
what its commands printed — and every subagent's thread. The redaction matches
the credential shapes the engine knows, not values, so a secret of no
recognisable shape that a run read is in its transcript as the run read it.

#### A seat reads its own

**A seat's executor finds and reads its seat's other sessions itself**, with two built-in tools on the seat's registry, each a read of the seat's rows on the executor log at the seat's own level (`linearizable`):

- **`list_sessions`** lists the seat's sessions, latest begun first, ten to a page and at most ten (a larger `limit` is read as ten): the most whose page fits one 64 KiB tool answer with every field of every row at its bound, 5,994 bytes a row, so an eleventh does not fit. Each row gives:
  - its turn and conversation;
  - whether it is the reading turn's own (`this_turn`, its earlier launches) or of the conversation that turn serves (`this_conversation`);
  - when it was captured and ended;
  - whether its session is still kept and its size kept (`kept`, `kept_bytes`);
  - whether it is in progress (`in_progress`, with `in_progress_note`) and what a person is told of a session its turn went on past (`kept_note`);
  - the session its first launch was handed (`base_turn`);
  - what its turn was asked and how it ended, each cut to 300 bytes.

  **With `query`** it keeps the sessions whose words (what the turn was asked, its conversation, and its ending's accounts) hold every query word, matched whole as the engine's [search](../guides/search.md) matches (case folded, no stemming) against what the row's redaction shows. A word found only inside a redacted credential, or only in the marker the redaction wrote in its place, finds nothing. The node holding the rows examines a thousand a page and answers its hits alone, so a node without `data` is never shipped a seat's history to filter. A page says how many sessions it searched and whether they reached the seat's oldest (`searched`), never that nothing matches past them, nor among them where the answering node holds records it could not read (`incomplete`): that page says sessions may be missing from it.
- **`read_session`** reads a page of one session's transcript by its turn id: on its first page the row whole, then its entries, each with its place among every entry the transcript holds (`ordinal`).
  - A seat's page is held to fifty entries, 32 KiB of their text and 8 KiB an entry (a quarter, a thirty-second and a half of a person's), and trimmed from its end to fit one tool answer, its `next_cursor` naming the first entry left out.
  - **`kinds`** narrows it to some kinds of entry (`["brief","model","summary"]` for the gist).
  - **`match`** narrows it to the entries whose whole text holds every word. A tool call is read as the JSON its input is written in, through its strings' escapes, so the word that opens a line of a command, or of a file the call wrote, is the call's word and not glued to the escaped line break before it. It is decided on what the redaction shows of the entry's own words, so a word only a redacted credential held, or only its marker spells, is no hit, alone or beside a word the entry shows; a guess at a redacted value is answered as a wrong one is, down to where a page full of hits stops: at the next hit.
  - Each hit is the window of its redacted text around the first word it shows, cut never inside a marker, with where the window begins in that redacted text (`text_from`) and a cursor that reads the transcript on from that entry.
  - Every entry's text is redacted whole before it is cut and states the size of what its whole text redacts to (`bytes`), never its size as recorded, which beside a text shown whole would tell the seat how long each value the redaction took out was.
  - A part of the record the read could not read (an entry of kind `unread`) is handed out whatever `kinds` or `match` asks.
  - A page says what it searched: a read that reached the transcript's end, that no entry from where it began holds the words (or, beside the parts it could not read, that it cannot say what those held); one the archive's read budget stopped, where.

**Only the seat's own, by construction.** Neither tool takes a seat: both read the seat of the turn the call is made in, which over the [tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box) is the run's own seat whatever the request carried, so another seat's turn id is answered as one nobody has. The reviewer is offered neither (it judges the turn's own record, never the executor's memory), no person's surface registers them, and a person or their assistant calling one is refused as an agent seat's own verb: a person reads a seat's sessions as its trail, above. A [worker](turn-engine.md#workers) its parent grants one reads as the seat's own delegate in the same turn.

**Every word is fenced as a harness's**, under `executor_session` at `external` trust ([Agent Runtime](agent-runtime.md#text-somebody-else-wrote)): an entry naming the seat whose run kept it, the row's words naming nobody; never the reading seat's own, since a transcript quotes whatever its run's tools returned.

**What a read costs.** One read of the executor log a call, counted by its read model (150 a seat a day). A transcript is decoded on the node holding the seat, in one of its two transcript slots, and seats take at most one of those two between them, so a node whose seats page transcripts still decodes a person's. A relaunch's reading of what a cut-off session holds takes none: it reads in its node's one slot for readings, inside its own thirty-second wait. A call the object store or the node's other reads hold past two minutes is answered unavailable, naming the session's size, never as a session that holds nothing.

**A read holds nothing.** Reading a session writes no record and holds no session, so it keeps none past what the seat's budget and the retention give it. A session released while listed or read is said as released, from what its row says then, as a person's read says it (above); what was read of it before stands.

**A run is told of the session it does not continue.** Where a launch read a kept session it could have continued (the turn's own, or the one its conversation's last turn left) and its run starts a session of its own instead, the run's brief names that session and says to read it with `read_session` ([What a harness is told](#what-a-harness-is-told)). Nothing else in a prompt mentions the tools: their descriptions say what they read.
**A company that keeps no session offers neither tool**:
`turn_engine.conversation_session.enabled: false` withholds both from every
model, the sessions kept before it went off included, which people still read
as the seat's trail ([Conversation Sessions](conversation-sessions.md#configuration)).
No launch of that revision is offered them, and each call asks the revision
its node runs now, so a launch already running when its node applies it is
refused at its next call — forbidden, saying the switch is off — rather than
reading on until it ends.
Neither is offered on a node with no object store, nor on one whose keyring
cannot open a sealed stream.

---

## Budgets

The harness calls the LLM from inside the box, so the engine cannot gate it request by request. The model is **floor + cap + post-account**:

- **Pre-flight floor, on every launch.** The first launch and every relaunch (a reviewer's send-back, or a person's answer carrying a parked run on) is refused when the seat's or company's remaining budget in any capped window is below `turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens` plus the brief, or when the budget cannot be read (launching on an unknown budget is how a company discovers its ceiling by spending past it).
  - **Unset, the floor is 25000 tokens**: a run's first request is the harness prompt and tool definitions (about 15k for Claude Code) plus the seat's bridged tools and system prompt, after a box, clone and setup. The brief counts beside it at a token per four bytes. `0` turns the floor off for a launch whose session's context is not known.
  - Below the floor is a **budget refusal**, which waits rather than fails: a dispatch [parks](agent-runtime.md#the-budget-park) the seat until the window turns over or a revision moves a ceiling (`seat_budget_parked` with `starved` set); a resumed segment is held on the same window, its job kept collected and its seat held.
  - A seat or company `token_budget` ceiling below the floor is refused on the write; one below floor plus a long brief is not. A launch whose brief takes its floor past the most room a capped window can leave (each ceiling less what its own turn spent there) is held at the floor alone, or at that room where less than the floor is left, and its first request may pass the ceiling ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)).
  - **A relaunch continuing the turn's session is held to more**: the larger of the floor and the session's context plus the brief, since it sends that context first. It is held on that figure, never parked, and a session no capped window can ever leave room for is not continued ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)).
- **Self-limits.** `role.sandbox.max_turns`, else `providers.sandbox.default_max_turns` (uncapped unless one is set), becomes the harness's turn cap on every runner (Claude Code's `--max-turns`, Gemini CLI's and Qwen Code's `model.maxSessionTurns`, OpenCode's agent `steps`, Copilot's extension, Grok Build's `--max-turns`, Muse Code's `--max-model-steps`, Kimi Code's `KIMI_LOOP_MAX_STEPS_PER_TURN`, Pi's extension, a Codex run's note helper's count of each turn's model responses). An uncapped run is held to the floor at every launch and charged in full on collect.
- **A spent seat is not resumed into a refusal.** A person's reply to a clarification question, on a seat no run holds, is offered to the run only after the [budget park](agent-runtime.md#the-budget-park) confirms room, since resuming charges tokens. A refusing seat holds the reply on its inbox until the window turns over. A collected run that takes a window past its ceiling parks the seat's next delivery the same way.
- **Post-accounting.** On collect, reported usage is charged to the budget cascade and the phase event carries real usage and cost for the Tokens view. Mid-run enforcement is best-effort, the price of the capability.
  - OpenCode's tokens and price come from its session's report ([OpenCode](#opencode)); a missing report counts as zero, not an estimate.
  - **A run continuing a session is charged what it added**, never the session's whole spend: Claude Code's per-run figures, or its result less the previous job's ([Claude Code](#claude-code)); OpenCode's report less the one read before the run started.
  - **Reported usage is never a refund**: it is parsed from output inside a box whose agent can run any command, so a negative token count or cost counts as nothing spent (`sandbox_usage_negative`), on every runner.
- **Charged once per run.** A run's tokens reach the seat's and company's counters once, however often its completion is delivered. A failed resume (the seat moved between publish and receive) sends the completion back and the retry collects the same job; the run's coordination record, written by the same compare-and-swap that hands the completion back, says its spend is counted, so the retry charges nothing on any node or after a restart. A relaunch in the same turn is a second job, charged on its own.
  - The charge is a **post-charge**: both counters record the run in full, in the day, week and month it is collected in, on the company's clock, whatever the ceilings say.
  - A run taking a counter past a cap is logged as `sandbox_spend_over_budget` and the turn continues; the next round is refused against the recorded figure, before it is sent. An over-cap charge is recorded, so a retry does not repeat it.
  - Only a charge the counter never answered (`sandbox_accounting_failed`) is offered again; if it had landed, the retry double-counts, tripping a cap early rather than late.
  - A charge that reached the **company's** counter but failed on the seat's (`sandbox_accounting_partial`) keeps the company's share, and the run's record says so, so a retry records the seat's share alone. A resume that succeeds after one brings no retry, so that seat's counter stays short until its window turns over; the company's stays exact.
- **Charged to the task too.** A turn on a Worklet task charges the task for the runs it detached: the segment resuming from a collected run adds its tokens to the task's spend, plus condensing its report or failure where the run's record lacks it (see [Spend is on the task](../guides/worklet.md#spend-is-on-the-task)).
  - A run that stopped to ask a question has no segment until a person answers, so its tokens and condensing are recorded with the question on the run's row; the segment the answer resumes pays them, on any node, however long the question waited.
  - Each segment is recorded once, under the run and launch it resumed, so a retried resume adds nothing.
  - A turn a person stops closes with a segment charging only what earlier segments left unpaid: a run's spend read when stopped, and what a segment charged to nothing handed on.

---

## Security model
- **Every run is fully permissioned, and its cell decides what that reaches.** A headless run has nobody to answer a permission prompt, so the harness runs with every permission in every cell — Claude Code under `bypassPermissions`, OpenCode with every action allowed but `question` — and the engine does not filter what it does inside its box, nor which MCP servers its own configuration, the repository's or a plugin's starts there ([MCP inside the sandbox](#mcp-inside-the-sandbox)). What it can reach is the cell's: `container` confines it to a container on the engine host with only the box's own directory mounted. Human gating, where wanted, happens at the merge request — not mid-run.
- **`run_in: direct` runs it on the engine host.** There the harness runs as the engine's own user: per-box state isolation and an allowlisted environment still hold, but the host's files, and whatever that user's credentials reach, are within the run's reach. Pick it only for a dedicated host you are willing to hand to an autonomous agent, for the entry that needs the host itself, or for a first run on your own machine while its seats take work from you alone; pick `container` anywhere else, a workstation included, and before a seat takes work from anyone else, with [an image of your own](#bring-your-own-image). It is opt-in twice over — a `local:` block *plus* an explicit `run_in` naming it, on a `providers.llm` entry or as `providers.sandbox.default_run_in` — and because the choice is per entry, a company can run the entry that needs the host itself `direct` and point every other seat at an entry whose cell keeps the run off the host's files. In a company that hosts its own code a `direct` box reads more than the host's files: every repository a Gitlet node's cache holds, whatever its `visibility` or the run's grants, and — on any node, Gitlet node or not — the Tier A keyring every run's credential is derived from, in `crewlet.yaml` and in the engine process's own environment, so it can mint the token of ANY live executor and push as that executor's seat. A refusal of `direct` for a run given repositories would close neither read: both are files of the engine's user whatever the run was given. So `crewlet validate` warns, at the `run_in` that places it, of every `direct` box in such a company; point a seat whose grants must bind it at an entry whose cell is `container`.
- **Only the seat's own identity enters the box.** The injected env carries credentials the agent legitimately acts *as*: its LLM entry's key, with the rest of that entry's `env` (a gateway's token among it), and the external-service tokens its config declares (`role.sandbox.env`). Leaking those from inside the box exposes only what the agent already is. Because the code-host token is the seat's **own** (its GitHub App's installation token, scoped to its tier and repositories, or a PAT of its own), an MR/PR the harness opens is attributed to the agent, not to a shared bot identity. An app's token in a box lives at most an hour, and is renewed only in the files that name it.
- **Shared infrastructure secrets never enter the box.** The OTLP backend's ingest token is the canonical example: the sandbox sees only an engine-fronted, path-token-scoped OTLP endpoint (`CREWLET_SANDBOX_OTEL_RECEIVER_URL`); the engine attaches the real backend credential upstream. Apply the same rule to any credential you add — if the agent doesn't act *as* it, don't inject it.
- **A box URL may be plain `http://`; its run's credentials then cross the network in clear.** The engine accepts `http://` exactly as it accepts `https://` for the URLs a box dials back to it — `CREWLET_BOX_GIT_URL`, `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL` and `CREWLET_SANDBOX_OTEL_RECEIVER_URL` — in every cell, and warns about none of them. Each request carries its run's token — as `/box/git/`'s Basic password, or in its path (`/mcp/{token}`, `/otlp/{token}/v1/{signal}`) — so over `http://` the token, and what the request carries, cross in clear every network between the box and the host the URL names. Which networks those are is a property of the URL, not of the cell: a request stays on the box's machine only when the URL names the box's own host — `127.0.0.1` from a `direct` box, `172.17.0.1` or `host.docker.internal` from a `container` one. A box's request crosses the fleet's network whenever its URL names another node or a balancer — Gitlet's URL does on any fleet whose seat nodes are not its Gitlet nodes (any Gitlet node serves any box, so it names a Gitlet node or a balancer over them), and the receiver's wherever another node serves `/otlp/`. Whoever reads that traffic reads the code the box clones and pushes, the seat's tool calls and their answers and the run's telemetry, and holds each token for its own window: the git token until the run's record ends it — the run ended, reaped or launched again; its seven-day expiry is only a backstop — in which it can fetch what the run was granted and push, as the run's seat, what its grants allow; the bridge's while the run's session lives (the token has no expiry of its own, and the session closes at the run's end, a capped run's at the collection after its turn's wall-clock cap), in which it can call the seat's own tools as the seat; the receiver's until it expires, four hours after the launch that minted it (`sandbox.OtelTokenTTL`), in which it can write into the run's telemetry. Serve every box URL whose path leaves the box's host over `https://` — TLS ending at a balancer or a proxy in front of the listener the URL names — and keep `http://` only for a URL that names the box's own host.
- **A `container` box on a fleet node reaches the fleet's broker, and is refused there — but on a member's host network it can read the fleet's traffic.** A container box joins the network `local.network` names, or the runtime's default bridge, and either reaches the host it runs on: on a fleet, a broker member's route port on the member's own host, and the members' leaf listeners from a leaf's. The embedded broker admits only a connection presenting a key derived from `secrets.keys`, so a box that reaches one is refused like any process outside the fleet (see [Deployment](../guides/deployment.md#the-fleets-broker-admits-only-its-own-nodes)). What it does not do is encrypt: given the HOST's network (`local.network: host`, or a `--network host` run argument) on a member's host, a box shares the member's network namespace, and with Docker's default capabilities it can read the fleet's plaintext links — a route's credential at connect time included — and reach the member's loopback client listener, which admits only the operator's key. Keep coding boxes off a fleet node's host network. **Beside an external NATS cluster** (`stream.type: nats`) the engine dials only a server that authenticates its clients, so a box holding none of that cluster's credentials is refused there as well (see [Deployment](../guides/deployment.md#an-external-nats-server)).
- **A box on a leaf's host reaches the leaf's link tunnel, and is refused there.** A node whose broker is a leaf dials its link to the members through a tunnel of its own on the host's loopback (an HTTP `CONNECT` proxy on a random port, [satellite nodes](../guides/satellite-nodes.md#what-a-satellite-still-needs)), which a `direct` box, a `container` box given the host's network, and a `container` box under Docker Desktop or Podman's machine (whose `host.docker.internal` arrives on the host's loopback) can reach. The tunnel forwards wherever its credential's holder asks, and only the node's own broker holds that credential, minted afresh at each start: any other caller is answered `407` before anything is dialled. A caller that connects and sends nothing is closed after a second, and the oldest of them at once while 64 wait, so a box that holds connections open cannot keep the leaf from linking. What a box can still do there is what it can do to any loopback listener: flood the host with connections, which slows every listener on it.
- **A run's own tokens are redacted from everything it hands back.** Every per-run token the engine mints — the telemetry endpoint's, the tool bridge's, a coding box's git credential, an artifact view ticket's — opens with the literal `crewlet_rt1` (`crewlet_rt1.<tag>.<subject>.<expiry>.<signature>`), and every text a box hands back — its report, its transcript, its question, its failure, its live output — is redacted of every token of that shape, to `[REDACTED:run-token]`, on the node that collects the run, before anything is stored or shown. It is recognised by its shape, as a vendor's key is, because no node that collects a run holds the tokens its launch minted, and a harness that prints its environment or its MCP configuration to debug its setup prints its own. And the engine mints no token of another shape: a subject holding a dot, a `[`, a `\`, a space, a tab, a line feed, a form feed or a carriage return, or running past 64 KiB, would make a token the redaction does not recognise, and is refused where the token would be minted, so the launch that asked for it fails by name rather than handing a box a token every surface would publish.
- **A kept session leaves its box scrubbed.** Every secret the engine put in a box by value — a token the completion poll renewed in it while the run worked included, recorded before it was written, in every session taken once its job had ended — and every credential shape the engine's redaction knows, is taken out of each file of a [kept session](#each-launchs-session-kept) before it is sealed, so a session continued in another box carries none of the login or the environment its first box was handed.
- **Everything else a run hands back is redacted by shape alone.** Its report, its transcript, its question, its failure and its live output — which shows what the run said, the commands it ran and a failed call's first line, never a successful call's output — pass the denylist alone, which knows no value the engine handed the box: a vendor's key, a cloud session's access key ID and a Google access token, a JSON Web Token, a DigitalOcean token, a private key, a password, and an AWS session's secret access key and session token under the keys AWS writes them under. A credential of no shape it knows — an opaque key the box was handed, an AWS secret printed bare — is shown and recorded as printed. So is one written further than a shape is read, 64 KiB from where the redaction decides it: a JSON Web Token whose header and claims run past that together, a password's value further than that from its key, an armour whose label runs past 64 bytes. No format a credential is written in reaches that far.
- **A check's box carries nothing of a seat's, and never runs on the engine host as its user.** It runs a change's own code, so it holds no harness, no model's sign-in, no login and none of the operator's setup, only the secrets its check names, and it always runs in a container on the Gitlet node that claims it, never `direct` ([Check boxes](#check-boxes)).
- **A seat reads its own sessions whoever its turn acts for.** A session holds what the seat's runs read for whoever their turns acted for — a person's private room, a file only that person may read — and the seat's later turns read it back with `list_sessions` and `read_session` whoever they act for, as they read the seat's diary and its past turns: a transcript keeps no record of which entry needed whose permission, so no ceiling of who the reading turn acts for can be held over it ([A seat reads its own](#a-seat-reads-its-own)). Give a seat that reads one person's private work no work from anybody else, or keep no sessions (`turn_engine.conversation_session.enabled: false`), which withholds both tools from every model: no launch of that revision is offered them, and each call asks the revision its node runs, so a launch already running is refused at its next call once its node applies it.
- **Injected values are ephemeral.** `${VAR}` references are resolved at acquire time into that sandbox's process env only; the database stores references, never values, and the values die with the box.
- **Workers run on the engine host, never in a box.** A delegated worker — including one a run delegates to over its bridge — runs the engine's own tool loop, its harness's own tools denied and its grant cut from its parent's. No tool it can hold starts a run, and its control denylist keeps `delegate`, `a2a_ask` and the A2A channel tools, and the parent's discovery pair, from it by name.
- **Network egress is yours to enforce.** The engine does not enforce egress rules: put a `container` box on a `local.network` your firewall governs, and prefer an allowlist (the LLM endpoint — the gateway its entry's `env` names, where it names one — the git host, the engine's tool bridge and OTLP receiver) for your production agent seats' boxes.
- **Budgets still bound the run** (previous section), the run's `submit_work` is decoded by the same submission rules as every phase's, and the turn passes the engine's delivery check before it reaches Review.

---

## Failure modes

### When a run does not start

An executor whose run couldn't be started fails its phase, and the turn with it: the run is the executor itself, so there's no other way to do the turn's work, and the turn's error says what failed. Each backend classes what it failed with at the point it fails, by **what would clear it**, so that whatever tells the failure to a model or a person can say that and nothing of the error itself, which names hosts, statuses, a container runtime's stderr or configuration paths:

| `why` | What failed | What clears it |
|---|---|---|
| `configuration` | The node runs no sandbox runtime for the company, or no tool bridge the run's box can dial (none at all, an `ingress` node on `api.port: 0`, or a cell whose box needs `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL` to reach it, with that unset), a cell the catalogue doesn't have, an executor chain with no member whose harness runs in a box, a setup command that exited non-zero (other than 75), an image the container runtime holds and won't start, a mount it can't share or the box may not write, a mount probe the runtime refused to run (see the lines below), or a box that can't run its shell, `find` or `head` to list a build | A person: an administrator fixes the sandbox setup. Waiting won't change it |
| `setup_unavailable` | A setup command that exited 75: its recipe saying that a download it makes is failing on the service's side and still was after its own retries (see [Setup steps](#setup-steps--provisioning-the-box)) | A wait, shortly |
| `provider_unavailable` | The box or its container runtime didn't answer or failed on its side: a command the box timed out or killed, a container runtime that didn't answer the mount probe in time, a container that would not start from an image the runtime does not hold (the image failed to arrive), or a read of a running box still in flight | A wait, shortly |

The executor's phase and its turn carry the class as their `error_kind`, `sandbox_` before it (`sandbox_configuration`, …), so the one word an operator acts on is on the record beside the error. A launch this node cancelled (a drain, a lease it lost) is no class: it's `canceled`, however far the container runtime had got; one a person stopped is `stopped`, which is no failure.

A failure no backend classed isn't filed under the nearest class. A seat this node no longer holds, or one a person stopped, launches nothing, and the turn says so rather than that a launch broke (`executor_launch_stopped` for a stop). So does a seat that moves while its launch is under way, its box's setup included. What the launch then meets need not say so, since the seat's next holder ends a launching run without fencing it and the box's attach finds that ending, or no record at all; the turn's own fence is asked again whatever the launch answered, and a closed one hands the delivery on to the seat's holder (`turn_seat_moved`) rather than back for a retry here. A launch below the [budget floor](#budgets) is a budget refusal, and one whose every runner member is sitting out is a limited chain (both below); and a condition of the node (a coordination store that didn't answer, the launch running out of time) or a fault of the node itself carries no class at all. A box the engine host couldn't make a directory for is that fault.

What an operator should recognize:

- **`this seat's executor chain is …, and no member of it can run the executor`**, from `crewlet validate` or a write — every entry the seat's `llm` names drives a harness with no in-box runner, so no launch could ever pick one and the seat would fail every turn. It is reported at the seat's `llm`, or, for seats that name none, once at the company fallback entry's `harness`, naming the first seat that falls to it. Point `llm` at an entry with `harness: claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `qwen-code`, `opencode`, `copilot`, `grok`, `muse-code`, `kimi-code`, `hermes` or `pi` and keep the others for the reviewer, workers and side passes, or move one of them to one of those harnesses. It is a [runnable rule](configuration.md#what-a-stored-revision-is-held-to): refused on every write and by `crewlet validate`, and never applied: a node's reconcile refuses a revision that breaks it and keeps the epoch it was serving, and a boot, a reload or a revert refuses it by name.
- **`this seat has N tokens left and an executor run needs at least M: its brief is about B tokens beside turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens (F)`** — the launch's [budget floor](#budgets): the floor with the run's brief beside it. A launch whose floor is held adds `past R, the smallest ceiling of the seat's or the company's capped windows, so it is held at turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens alone`, the room said as `R, the most room the seat's or the company's capped windows can leave the launch (a ceiling of C, less the S its own turn spent there before it)` where the turn spent in that window, and the hold as `so it is held at that room, which only a window holding nothing but its own turn's spend leaves` where that room is below the floor; one that continues a session says that session's context instead (`an executor run that continues its session needs at least M: its session sends … tokens before its brief, …`). It is not a failure of the turn: on a dispatch the seat is parked until the window turns over or a revision moves a ceiling, logged as `seat_budget_parked` with `floor` and `starved` and a reason that names the window (`budget: <period> window <label> leaves N tokens, below the M an executor launch needs (its brief about B beside turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens, F); resets …`, or `below the F an executor launch needs (turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens)` where no launch has been refused yet), and a resumed segment is held on the same window. A budget that could not be read is refused too, and retried. Raise the ceiling, or lower the floor where the windows are right and the floor is not.
- **`seat "…"'s executor runs in a box, and this node has no sandbox runtime for this company: configure providers.sandbox`** — the launch found no sandbox runtime or no catalogue in the turn's revision. Validation refuses an agent seat with a model and no catalogue, so on a validated company this is a runtime that did not start on this node; its log says why.
- **`an executor needs a tool bridge its box can dial, …`** (or **`… a node serving its tool bridge, and nothing here reaches it`**) — the launch was refused because its box would have no address to reach the seat's tools at: a node with no bridge at all, an `ingress` node with `api.port: 0` that binds no listener for the bridge's route, or a `container` cell — or a `direct` one on a node that binds no listener its boxes reach on loopback (`api.port: 0`, or on a node without `ingress` an `api.host` of one address that is not loopback) — with no `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL`. Set what the message names (see [the tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)): the refusal is classed `configuration`, which no wait clears. A node that runs seats says each such cell once when a company is applied, as `executor_bridge_unreachable`, before any turn is refused for it.
- **Every runner member sitting out** — every member of the seat's executor chain whose harness has a runner is sitting out a spent plan on this node, so the launch fails as a call whose chain ran out does, each member's refusal on it: a [limited chain](llm-backends.md#falling-back-between-entries). On a dispatch the turn fails (`llm_unavailable`, the seat's `last_error`, which is no stop) and the seat is parked on its provider (`seat_provider_parked`), reading `stopped` with the reason `provider` until a probe of the chain answers or the company's models change. A resumed segment's relaunch (a reviewer's send-back, a person's answer) that meets it parks the seat the same way, and its resume waits for the park's release: a completion held by the node that met the limit, in that node's memory and never on the run's record, until the instant the limit names, and refused at the admission while the park stands; an answer in its own series, uncharged (see [Both series are bounded](#mid-run-clarification-ask_and_wait)). A completion whose review's chain already sits out a limit parks the seat the same way once it is collected, before its turn runs. A run that ends on its plan's limit sits its entry out on the node that collects it (`harness_run_limit_reported`), so the turn's next launch moves on to the next member; a run that meets the limit midway is not relaunched on another member.
- **`sandbox_run_past_deadline`** (a log line, at info): a turn with a wall-clock cap — a scheduled fire's `timeout_seconds` — reached it with its run still working. The run is ended as if it had finished: its collection ends its job as a person's stop does (`sandbox_job_ended`, or `sandbox_job_killed` where it would not go), reads what it did up to then and marks it cut off, and the turn resumes with that. Raise the schedule's `timeout_seconds` if its runs routinely need longer.
- **`sandbox_deadline_end_unrecorded`** (a log line, at warning): a collection saw its job still working past its turn's wall-clock cap and could not record so on the run's record before it ended the job — the coordination store refused the write, and the error says why. That collection still says the cap cut the run off. One made again after it — the first cut short as it ended the job, or its box not read back — reads the job's own record of the request where its script left one; where the script left none, the run reads there as one that ended by itself, and is parked on a question it asked on its way out.
- **`harness_context_unmeasured`** (a log line, on the node whose host the box is on): the read that collected a job read no measure of the session its box holds, and says why: at warning where the run's account is of a shape this build does not read (a Claude Code stream whose assistant lines carry a usage and none says it is the main thread's, or whose newest main-thread usage does not read; an OpenCode page that does not decode), at info otherwise (a run that made no request, a Claude Code line past the stream's line bound or cut short after its newest figure, an OpenCode job ended on request, a page past the pages' budget, no settled message that measured a prompt among the pages asked). The job's record keeps the measure carried along its copy's lineage, or none, which holds a relaunch that continues the copy in its box to the floor with its brief beside it.
- **`sandbox_harness_end_unrecorded`** (a log line, at warning): a collection could not record on the run's record how its job's harness ended, what the session's newest request carried, nor what its harness counts it at: the coordination store refused the write, or did not answer it within the room the read leaves its records, and the error says which. A relaunch that reads the record later and carries the job's round on in its box (a person's answer, the turn's kept session not what it continues) then reads the job as one whose harness may have been cut off, and tells the session there so, every call of the round and every note the turn has read, some of which it may hold ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)); its skill guard holds none of the job's own loads, and, of a Claude Code job, whose copy's count is unrecorded too and so reads as a session that may be a summary, no skill at all, its launch's among them, while it is told every lead its record keeps; and its floor holds the copy to the measure the job's record carried along its lineage, or to none ([What a continued launch costs](#what-a-continued-launch-costs)). A replaced sign-in carried on from that collection's own claim reads what the collection found.
- **`executor_session_count_unbounded`** (a log line, at info, naming the `mark`): the read that collected a Claude Code or an OpenCode job could not bound what its harness counts the copy its box holds at, and says which mark stands for the bound: a thread not read whole (a job not over, a runner that reads no thread, a line the layer refuses, the read's 27 s spent, a newest restart whose uuid does not read; of an OpenCode job, one whose harness did not end its own run, an export its script did not leave or that does not read, a provider that does not read), a release older than 2.1.310 or an OpenCode release outside its set, a saved precompact summary, a compaction with no reply after it, an OpenCode session with no counted reply since its start or its newest completed compaction, a reply's usage that does not read, a server clearing, a PDF read or an image or a document after the last counted reply, or an OpenCode file after it. A relaunch that continues the copy in its box is told it as a cut-off one ([What a continued session is told](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)), and one that continues an OpenCode copy is also held to its newest request's input. Nothing needs doing.
- **`executor_large_read_waited`** (a log line, at info, naming whether it `took` the slot and how long it `waited_ms`): a collection's read of a job's main thread or a capture's take passed its base (a line whose facts charge past 128 KiB, a collection keeping more than 2^13 of a thread's records and call ids, or a text a take's scrub redacts as one, or its plan of bits, past 256 KiB) and waited for the node's one large-read slot ([Reading a seat's sessions](#reading-a-seats-sessions)). With `took` false its read ran out waiting: the collection counted the session unread, or the take was refused. Frequent waits are a node collecting many sessions with long chains or lines of many facts at once, or capturing sessions with long lines; nothing needs doing unless captures go unkept for it.
- **`executor_session_take_waited`** (a log line, at info, naming whether it `took` a slot and how long it `waited_ms`): a capture's take found every one of the node's 29 take slots held (`SessionTakesAtOnce`) and waited for one before asking its box for anything. With `took` false its wait ran out and the take was refused, its session not kept. Frequent waits are a node capturing many sessions at once; nothing needs doing unless captures go unkept for it.
- **`executor_session_scrub_memo`** (a log line, at info, with `hits`, `misses`, `diverged`, `entries` and `evicted`): a take's scrub met lines, strings or files of 256 KiB or more, and says how many the node's memory of texts the redaction left unchanged answered for, how many it did not, and how many it answered for wrongly (each costing the take one more reading); `entries` and `evicted` are that memory's size, 4,096 texts at most and 64 an agent, and what it has dropped since the engine started. Steadily rising `evicted` beside low `hits` is a node whose seats' large texts outgrow it; it costs time, never a secret.
- **`executor_session_may_compact`** (a log line, at info, naming the `path`, `in_place` or `kept`, the bound or the `mark`, the windows and the `point`): a relaunch found that Claude Code may compact the session it continues before its first request, or that the session's count has no bound, so it tells the session as a cut-off one, every call of its round from its start, every lead its record keeps and every note the turn has read, and arms its guard with no skill; where a brief told by a reading of the session's archive rides beside it, its outcome says the launch may hand that one instead. **Its launch's form**, for a continuation judged in its box (OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code), keyed by `turn_id` and `agent`, names the `path`, the count's `bound`, `mark` and `provider`, the launch's `model`, the box's `release`, its `point` (or `never`), the `point_mark` and its `detail`, and the `box_tokens` and `brief_tokens` charged beside the bound: the box's point did not prove the held brief whole, so the launch hands the one told as a session that may be a summary. Nothing needs doing; a session that keeps meeting it is near its model's window, which a model with a larger one avoids. An OpenCode one that keeps meeting it with a `point_mark` has a box whose configuration the engine does not judge: `defaulted` is a model whose limit no document or catalog states (state it in the box's `opencode.json`, at or under the window of the server that serves it), `plugin` a plugin of the box's own, `pair` an image whose OpenCode is not the release that wrote the session. A Gemini CLI or Qwen Code one with `settings` has a box whose settings, `.env` files or environment name a knob that moves its point (the `detail` names the file), and a Gemini CLI one signed in with a Google login or on Vertex AI always meets it: sign it in with a key. A Gemini CLI one with `nomodel` has a launch naming no model: give its entry a model.
- **`executor_session_holdings_read`** (a log line, at info, naming the `seat`, the `turn_id`, how many calls were `asked`, `held` and `told`, how many distinct subagents a told call is `unreported` under, the `writer`, the release the reading was read for, whether the session `compacted` after its run began (a content reading's: OpenCode's, Qwen Code's or Gemini CLI's; always false for Claude Code's), and the `outcome`): a relaunch read which of its round's calls a cut-off Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI or Qwen Code session holds ([What a continued session is told](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). Where it holds none of them (`held` 0) and moves none under a subagent (`unreported` 0), no brief is told by it, the relaunch is told every call after its save point, and no line follows. Otherwise the launch hands the brief told by it where its box's harness answers `writer` and its first request sends the session whole; where it does not, `executor_session_holdings_unused` says why, or `executor_session_not_continued` where the launch does not continue the session at all. Nothing needs doing.
- **`executor_session_holdings_unread`** (a log line, at info, naming the `seat`, the `turn_id` and the `detail`): the reading read nothing (no reader for the session's harness, a writer or a resumer release the reader does not read, an archive it could not read whole within its bounds or its thirty seconds; for Gemini CLI also a run whose box did not pass its guard, a line separator, a patch ordering the records, a rewind to no record, a shape not measured, or a file shorter than its run's start), so the relaunch is told every call after its save point, which is never wrong. Nothing needs doing.
- **`executor_session_holdings_unused`** (a log line, at info, naming the `turn_id`, the `detail` and the `outcome`, with the `agent_id`, the `seat` or the `agent` of the site that decided it): a brief told by a reading was read and not handed: its own first request may compact the session (the runner), the seat's budget cannot carry it beside the rest (the launch's floor), or the relaunch's box answered another release than the one it was read for, or none, or the launch was given no brief told by the reading for that box, or the launch continued the copy of the session its job's own box holds, which went on past the capture the reading was read of (the launch). The relaunch is handed the brief told by the save point, which the floor's line says it offers, or, where the launch continues the copy its job's own box holds, the brief that continues the copy there: the box that decides whether the session is continued at all is acquired after the floor, and `executor_session_not_continued` says where it is not. Nothing needs doing; a box image that moved past the release that wrote the session meets it once.
- **`executor_session_subagent_unreported`** (a log line, at info, naming the `seat`, the `turn_id`, the subagent's `agent` id and the `detail`): a reading found calls in the thread of a subagent whose report the session does not hold, so it tells them under that subagent's name, one line per subagent. Nothing needs doing.
- **`sandbox_prior_reclaimed`**, **`sandbox_reuse_failed`**, **`sandbox_prior_left_to_host`** (log lines): a relaunch did not continue in its turn's previous box — the member it picked runs another harness or in another cell, the box is seven days old or older (the line's `box_since`), the box could not be reattached, or the box is on another node's host — and started in a fresh one from the pushed branch (see *Reuse across launches* under [How a coding task runs](#how-a-coding-task-runs)). Nothing is lost but the box's disk state.
- **`executor_launch_stopped`** (a log line, at info): a person stopped the seat's running work while its executor was launching, so the launch was ended and the turn closes as stopped, naming who stopped it. Nothing needs doing.
- **`executor_session_fenced`** (a log line, at warning, naming the `step` — `upload` or `record` — and the `taker_epoch` the capture was taken under, followed by the capture's `executor_session_not_kept`): a keep of a run's session found that this node's [taker lease](#each-launchs-session-kept) no longer covers it — it lapsed and was claimed again at another epoch, or its renewals went unanswered past the window of the last one the store answered — so it uploaded and recorded nothing more, and stamped the capture refused, or unresolved where a record of it had already been sent and not answered. A peer may already have settled it from the executor log. Look at the coordination store's health on this node: one renewal the store does not answer costs nothing, and a keep is fenced only once two have gone unanswered in a row. **`executor_taker_lease_lost`** (at warning) is a lapse as the node's own renewal found it, after which the lease is claimed again at a new epoch; **`executor_taker_lease_unanswered`** (at warning) a claim or a renewal the store did not answer — while it holds no lease whose last renewal still covers it, the node begins no capture, and a collection's session is not kept; **`executor_taker_lease_refused`** (at warning) a claim the store answered and refused; **`executor_taker_lease_unreleased`** (at warning) a release at the node's stop the store did not answer within the stop's [one allowance](agent-runtime.md#graceful-shutdown), after which the lease lapses on its TTL. **`executor_session_settled`** (at info) is the other side: a node waiting on a capture whose taker's lease had lapsed read what came of it off the turn's row on the executor log, its `state` landed or refused — logged only where the settle was written, since one the taker's own stamp got to first leaves that stamp standing.
- **`setup step "…" writes …, which a direct box refuses`** (or **a container box**), from `crewlet validate` or a write: a setup step writes a file outside the home of a box some seat runs in, or names another account's `~name/…`, a `~` followed by a backslash (`~\…`, which no shell reads as the home), the home itself or a directory above it, so every box of that seat would fail at setup. The problem sits at the file's entry in the step, and names the first seat whose box it fails and how many more. Name the file relative to the box's home instead — `.npmrc`, `.local/bin/tool`, or `~/.npmrc` — which every cell writes under its home, or have a command of the step write it under `"$HOME"`: a `direct` box's home is minted per box, so no absolute path a file entry holds is inside it. Moving the seat to the other cell helps only one way round: an absolute path under `/home/user`, which a `direct` box refuses, is taken by a `container` box, while a path outside the home is refused by both.
- **`local sandbox (run_in "direct") refuses to touch …`** or **`… is not a file under the sandbox home mount at /home/user`** (a `sandbox.LocalError`): a path a box was asked to write or read is outside its home, which neither cell writes outside of — `direct` because the path would be the engine host itself, `container` because only the home is mounted. A setup file that names such a path is refused on the write (above), so at launch this is a stored revision that keeps such a step — an apply warns about it rather than refusing it — or a directory in the box's home that is a link leading out of it, which only the box can see: a link in a box's home is followed only while it stays there, so one the box's own work made must be relative and lead to somewhere inside the home. For a setup file the remedy is the one above: name it relative to the box's home, or have a setup command write it under `"$HOME"`.
- **`… neither docker nor podman is on the engine host's PATH`** (a `sandbox.LocalError`, when the company is applied or a node boots on it): `run_in: container` with no container runtime on the engine's own PATH, which under a service manager can be narrower than your shell's. Install one, put the directory that holds it on that PATH, or use `direct`. Naming one in `local.runtime` does not help: a runtime named outright is looked up on the same PATH.
- **`cannot see its own box directory`** — the runtime is driving a daemon on another host, so the bind mount is that machine's filesystem rather than this one's. Point the runtime at a daemon on this host.
- **`refused to run container sandbox …'s mount probe`**: the container runtime wouldn't run the probe in the box it had just started. The container exited at once (its image's own command failed), or the daemon refused the exec. The runtime's own words end the line. It's classed `configuration`, as every refusal of the runtime's is.
- **`did not answer its mount probe`**: the runtime didn't finish running the probe in the box it had started within 10 seconds: its daemon was too slow or wedged, or reading the mount hung. It's classed `provider_unavailable`, which a wait clears.
- **`cannot make a directory in its own home`**: the probe ran, and the container can't write its home mount, because it runs as a user the mount refuses. Run it as a user that can, with `run_args`, or mount the box directory writable.
- **`could not run its mount probe, because this host could not run the container runtime`**: the engine couldn't start the runtime's binary a moment after it started the container with it. That's a fault of this host, and carries no class.
- **`"container" needs the `local:` backend configured under providers.sandbox`** — an entry's `run_in` (or `default_run_in`) names a cell the catalogue does not hold. Add the block the cell needs, or point the entry at one that is configured; the message lists what this catalogue has.
- **`the catalogue offers more than one place to run one`** — an entry a seat's executor launches on names no cell and the catalogue names no `default_run_in`. Name the cell where the message points, or name the default. A catalogue is not refused for being ambiguous on its own — only a seat or entry that would actually fall to the missing default is.
- **`nothing names one, so no backend is built`** — an ambiguous catalogue that *nothing* reaches: no `default_run_in`, no entry's `run_in`. Nothing would be built and no seat could run code, so the block reads as configuration and configures nothing. Name the default, give an entry a seat's executor launches on a `run_in`, or remove the block while no agent seat runs on a model.
- **`writes its box directory as a user this engine cannot manage`** — the container is running as someone the engine cannot follow into the mount, which happens when `run_args` overrides the `--user` the backend chose. Drop that override, or run the engine as the same user the container does.
- **`sandbox_env_unresolved`** — a `${VAR}` in the run environment, or a setup file that is one whole `${VAR}`, resolves to nothing and its key is not declared optional; the executor run starts without it. The line names the keys and the `<step>:<path>` files, never a value or a body, and sorts the variables by why each is missing. It is at info when every variable is only `awaiting`, or held only by findings this node is still reading (`unsure`), and a warning otherwise:
  - **`awaiting`**: an integration is setting the value up for the seat. A [provisioning pass](integration-reconcile.md) is minting it, and a run launched after its seal reaches this node is given it; or it is the seat's own `${GITHUB_APP_TOKEN_<HANDLE>}`, which nothing seals: the engine issues it at launch once the agent's GitHub App is created and installed (**Company › Integrations**), a run launched after the reconcile records the installation is given it, and a running job's token file is written by the first poll after the app can issue one. A token an integration issues at use also reads `awaiting` while the integration is still settling it (a grant its vendor is still applying): nobody has to act, the seat's tool servers ask for it again on the restart schedule until it is issued, and a running job's token file is written by the first poll after it is.
  - **`unsure`**: the integration that mints it cannot say whether it holds the seat up: a person owes one of its last pass's findings and one names something, and its findings are not read yet (info: the next run's judgement has them), could not be read, or were [cut](integration-reconcile.md#what-a-surfaces-records-keep) where they may name the seat (each a warning). The line says which, and its variables are also listed under `awaiting`.
  - **`stopped`**: the integration that mints or issues it won't until a person acts. Act on its finding, which the line quotes; for the agent's GitHub App that is its **Create** or **Install** on the GitHub card.
  - **`unissued`**: the engine went to issue the agent's GitHub App token and GitHub didn't give one. Where GitHub didn't answer, or answered a 408, its rate limit (a 429, or a 403 its headers mark as one) or a 5xx, the line says GitHub is asked again on the restart schedule, and the first ask it answers issues the token. Where it refused, the line carries GitHub's status (a revoked key, a suspended installation, a permission the installation hasn't approved) and says the token isn't issued until somebody fixes the app: fix the agent's GitHub App, its installation or its permissions.
  - **`unset`** or **`empty`**: set the variable the line names (`crewlet secrets set`, or the integration's provision command for a seat's own bot or account), or list its key under `optional_keys` where the run can go without it.

  `optional_keys` never releases a variable an integration mints or issues for the seat: the line names it whatever the declaration says. And `${GITHUB_APP_TOKEN_<HANDLE>}` is the engine's to issue: it is never set with `crewlet secrets set`.
- **Setup-step failure** (`sandbox_setup_failed`) — a step's provisioning did not complete, and the box is torn down before any brief runs. The message names the step and says which of three things failed: `could not write <path>`, a file the box refused (with the reason above), `command #N failed (exit S)`, a command that exited non-zero (in every cell, 124 is its `timeout_seconds` running out, with the timeout named before what the command printed, and a status above 128 is a signal that ended it — 128 plus the signal's number, 137 for a `SIGKILL` such as an out-of-memory kill — as a shell reports one; where the signal ended the box's own shell in a `direct` box, rather than a program that shell waited on, the signal is also named after what the command printed, while a `container` box's command reads as `docker exec` reports it, the status alone), or `command #N reported no exit status`, one the box could not start or whose box went away before it finished, with the box's own account after it. A command that exited 75 is its recipe saying a download it makes failed for now, which a wait clears (`setup_unavailable`); any other failure is an operator config problem (a broken recipe, `configuration`). Either is logged distinctly from a harness install failure.
- **Sandbox lost mid-run** (`sandbox_run_lost`, a log line at warning, naming the `cause`): the job was lost with the host it ran on — `engine_restarted` (its engine's restart killed it), `box_gone` (its box is gone from where it ran), `launch_node_gone`, or `launch_node_store_silent` (logged `sandbox_collect_lost_with_host` by the seat's holder: the node its box is on could not read the run's record for `host_grace_seconds`; see `sandbox_collect_unsettled`) — and its round is carried on — continuing the lost job's kept session where it can, in a fresh run otherwise (`sandbox_run_lost_carried_on` on the node that holds the seat; see *A job lost with its host* under [Durability](#durability-completion-and-observability)). Nothing needs doing for one. A run whose turn then ends with `the executor's round was lost with its host too often to start again` lost more than two jobs in one round: it is taking its own host down, most often by exhausting the memory its container is held to — give the box more, or a cell of its own. Look for `sandbox_connect_failed` streaks before a `box_gone`: a run's box is never reaped while its record names it, so `box_gone` means its box root did not outlive its node. A node down longer than `host_grace_seconds` has its running jobs recorded lost (`launch_node_gone`) and their rounds carried on, so that grace is the knob to raise for deployments with long maintenance windows.
- **Collect failure**: the box could not be read back. **It is asked again first**: nothing the completion writes — the charge, the run's phase record, the park, the resume — happens before a collection succeeds, so handing the claim back leaves the run exactly as the completion found it (running, its box kept alive, its turn parked), and the completion comes back on the queue's backoff while its waiter announces it again on its schedule (`sandbox_collect_retried`). The allowance is the poll's own for an unreachable box — at least two **consecutive** failed attempts spanning a minute, counted on the run's record so another node or a restart does not start a fresh one, and ended by a collection that did read the box (one whose park or resume then failed and handed the claim back, or one whose read answered before a later step of it that the coordination store did not answer, or that this node stopped, handed the claim back uncounted), so a box that answered is never given up on the strength of failures from before it answered — and past it the box is torn down, the run ended and announced (`collect_unreachable`), and the agent freed. A box its provider says is **gone** is settled at once, since no attempt can read it. A collection **this node** stopped — a drain, a restart, the seat moving to another node — is handed back without being counted (`sandbox_collect_interrupted`), because it says nothing about the box; a collection that ran out of its delivery's time is counted, or a box whose read always outlasts it would be retried for ever. A step the coordination store did not answer is not the box's failure either, and is never counted (`sandbox_collect_unsettled`, below). And no hand-back of a collection's claim that the store did not answer is ever an ending: the node keeps the claim and gives it back once the store answers (`sandbox_claim_revert_owed`, below). A file merely too large to read whole is never a collect failure: that piece is described by its size and the run is collected without it.
- **`sandbox_calls_drained`** (info), **`sandbox_calls_unfinished`** and **`sandbox_run_deleted_with_calls_in_flight`** (warning), on the node collecting a run: a collection waited for the calls its run's tool log held in flight before it read the log (`calls`, `unfinished`, `waited_s`) ([The tool bridge](#the-tool-bridge--a-seats-own-tools-from-inside-a-box)); it stopped waiting for one still in flight, read as a call whose outcome is unknown, naming it by its tool, its place and the first eight hex digits of its digest (`call`), the node process running it (`runner`) and why (`why`: its own bound passed, the turn's cap passed, or its process stopped) — what it committed is in no outcome of the turn unless its update lands before the turn's last collection reads the run's log; or the run's ending deleted its record with a call still in flight there, whose update then finds no record.
- **`bridge_call_not_recorded`**, **`mcp_bridge_call_update_owed`** and **`mcp_bridge_call_update_unrecorded`** (log lines, at warning, on the node serving the run's tool bridge): the coordination store did not take a bridged call's write. `bridge_call_not_recorded` is a call's entry, written on the run's log before the call runs, which the store did not take within five seconds, four attempts included, or a log holding 256 calls in flight, or one that takes no more calls of the job (`why`): the call was not run, and its box was told so — that it could not be recorded and may be made again, or that its run has ended. `mcp_bridge_call_update_owed` is a finished call's update the store did not take within four attempts over 1.75 seconds, which outlast a stream leader's re-election — never a call one of them put in the log, whatever became of what it cost (written to the record after the log), since the attempts after that one try only that write: the call ran and its answer went back to the box, its entry stays on the log, so it is counted by its identity, and the update is asked for again every one to five seconds until the call's bound (`until`); `mcp_bridge_call_update_answered`, at info, says one asked again was answered. `mcp_bridge_call_update_unrecorded` is one still not taken at the call's bound: its entry stays, read as a call whose outcome is unknown, and what it answered, cost and committed is lost. A call that ends after a relaunch that carried the round on is listed in the round's log, marked `late`, and no warning names it, since it is on the run's record — the runs answer's `late`, and the Executors board's tag ([A relaunch continues the turn's session](#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)). A call of an old round, which a new round replaced, is dropped, said only at debug, `bridge_call_after_its_job` — unless nobody waited for it, its job's session on the bridge having ended and answered it as still running, or its harness having given up on it: then neither the session that made it nor any record of the run holds what it did, though it ran, and it is named at warning, `bridge_abandoned_call_after_its_job`, by its tool, its place among the job's calls and the first eight hex digits of its digest (`call`). Each `bridge_` line names the run, the job and the call by its tool, its place among the job's calls and the first eight hex digits of its digest (`call`); each `mcp_bridge_` line names the run, the seat, the call's tool and its place (`seq`).
- **`sandbox_suspension_*` errors** (`executor_failed` with reason `suspension_unrecorded`): the turn parked but its parked state (`execstate`) never reached the run's record, because the runner recorded none, it would not serialize, it was past its share of the record however far the park condensed it (`sandbox_suspension_too_large`: the turn's own context, which no condensing touches), the coordination store refused the write, or the run was no longer launching. The run was already executing, so a run still launching has its box reclaimed at once and is ended, rather than left to run to its TTL with nothing able to collect it. A run that is no longer launching is left alone and not announced: a write reported as refused can have landed, which makes it an ordinary parked run the completion poll collects, and a run already ended was announced by whoever ended it. A store refusal points at the coordination store; a state past its share at the turn itself — a trigger whose own words are past it, since its closed rounds always fit; the other three are a defect in the engine worth reporting.
- **`executor_failed` with reason `claim_unreverted`**: the coordination store refused to take back a claim whose work had already failed. A completion claims a run's tail before collecting it, and every failure after that claim is recoverable only because the claim can be given back — so when the park a run asked for, or the revert a failed resume makes, cannot be written *and* the store refuses the claim's return as well, the run is ended here instead. The row would otherwise sit in `resumed`, which no completion poll reads, no redelivery can re-claim, no answer matches and no pause reaper expires: an unrecoverable turn plus a paused box held until the seat changes hands. Every hand-back ends here only where the store refused it, a collection's, a park's and a resume's alike: one the store did not answer is kept by the node that made it and given back once the store answers, the seat's mail held meanwhile, and the run is never ended for that silence (`sandbox_claim_revert_owed`, below). Look at the coordination store: this reason means it answered the return of the claim with a refusal no retry changes, such as a record this build cannot read or write.
- **`turn_rebased`** (a log line, not an announcement): a turn's unit of work began more than twenty-nine days before this attempt — a run resumed that long after its work began, or a trigger dispatched that long after it arrived — so its operation ids are minted at this attempt rather than at that start, and the instant is recorded so a later attempt at the same work inherits it (see [How a coding task runs](#how-a-coding-task-runs)). `seed` is the unit of work, or the run where there is none; `began` is the start, `inherited` the instant an earlier attempt had recorded (the start where none had) and `rebased_to` the new one. Nothing is wrong and nothing needs doing: it says that a tracker or knowledge-base write an earlier attempt made and this one repeats is a second write rather than a retry of the first (a work-item comment, a created item and a created view excepted, which are found by their ids and answered from their rows) — minted at the start, every data node's operation ledger would have answered every new write of this attempt `unknown` instead. It is logged once per rebase; an attempt that inherits a recorded instant logs nothing above debug.
- **`sandbox_answer_headroom_reserved`** (a log line, not an announcement): every message of this delivery has spent nearly all of its deliveries, so the answer route stopped offering it and the 5 that are left are kept for the ordinary route, which is being run on it now. It is what stops a reply being handed back until the broker dead-letters it, and it is the expected end of a resume that fails on *every* node rather than on this one — the per-process attempt count below cannot see that, because a seat handoff resets it and the broker's count is on the message. The line names the seat, what the partition had left and the reserve. A parked run is unaffected: it keeps waiting, bounded by `pause_ttl_seconds`.
- **`sandbox_answer_offered_over_a_spent_sibling`** (a log line): the opposite decision, and the one whose cost is paid elsewhere. A message of this delivery still has the deliveries to spare, so a parked run is being offered it — while another message in the same partition is inside the reserve, and a hand-back returns the whole partition. It is the advance notice for a `dead_lettered` line on that sibling, and it is the expected shape of a conversation whose earlier message has been handed back many times and which is still collecting fresh replies.
- **`sandbox_answer_resume_failed`** (a log line, at warning): the answer recorded on a parked run could not be resumed with — the error says why — and the coordinator will try again after the spacing the line names. The seat's later mail is held behind it meanwhile. Nothing is asked of the person: the answer is on the run.
- **`sandbox_answer_unverified`** (a log line, at error): the answer recorded on a parked run does not open as an answer to that run's question under the fleet keyring — the error says how — so it is handed to no turn, attributed to nobody and let go of with nothing handed back, and the run waits on its question again. A reply given after this answers it as usual.
- **`sandbox_answer_key_unknown`** (a log line, at warning): the answer recorded on a parked run is sealed under a key this node does not hold, and `node_holds` lists the ones it does. The answer stays recorded and owed, with the seat's mail behind it, until a node holding the key takes the seat or this one restarts with it in `secrets.keys`; the line repeats every five minutes while it waits.
- **`sandbox_answer_requeue_exhausted`** (a log line, not an announcement): this node could not resume one parked run with the answer recorded for it in every attempt its budget allowed — ten of them, spaced a second apart doubling to thirty, or as many as the run's `pause_ttl_seconds` left room for — so the answer was let go: the reply was handed to the seat's inbox as the ordinary message it is and is being worked as the turn it looks like, and the run waits on its question again with that reply declined for it. Its box is still bounded by `pause_ttl_seconds`. The line names the run and the window; the error beside it is the one to read, and it is nearly always this node rather than the run — no resumer on this node, a parked turn state of an `execstate` version this build does not read, or a seat that is not in this node's company. The seat's next holder, or this node after a restart, starts a clean set of attempts on the next reply.
